title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰若聖與仁則吾豈敢抑爲之不厭誨
人不倦則可謂云爾已矣公西華曰正
唯弟子不能學也
沈束
同考試官教諭王批聖賢答述詞氣自別此
篇溫潤而不浮從容而不迫縝密清純獨超諸作
同考試官教諭陳批聖德謙虛之實賢人仰
===
嘆之心皆體會而發揮之真佳作也
考試官教諭陳批意語明達
考試官學正陳批精醇雅健
聖人謙言其所能而門人以爲難焉蓋聖人之
所能仁聖之極功也故雖謙而言之抑豈下學
者所易及乎昔者夫子有曰理之在夫人也大
而化之之謂聖全而備之之謂仁世有以是而
云我者乎然其幾精微不可以淺近窺其究廣
大不可以徑易造故吾方望之而未見也若神
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「若聖與仁，則吾豈敢？抑爲之不厭，誨人不倦，則可謂云爾已矣。」公西華曰：「正唯弟子不能學也。」

沈束

同考試官教諭王批：聖賢答述，詞氣自別。此篇溫潤而不浮，從容而不迫，縝密清純，獨超諸作。

同考試官教諭陳批：聖德謙虛之實，賢人仰嘆之心，皆體會而發揮之，真佳作也。

考試官教諭陳批：意語明達。

考試官學正陳批：精醇雅健。

聖人謙言其所能，而門人以爲難焉。蓋聖人之所能，仁聖之極功也。故雖謙而言之，抑豈下學者所易及乎？昔者夫子有曰：「理之在夫人也，大而化之之謂聖，全而備之之謂仁。世有以是而云我者乎？然其幾精微，不可以淺近窺；其究廣大，不可以徑易造。故吾方望之而未見也。若神
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “As for sagehood and benevolence, how would I dare claim them? Yet striving toward them without weariness and teaching others without tiring—this much may be said of me, and nothing more.” Gongxi Hua said: “It is precisely this that we disciples cannot learn to achieve.”

Shen Shu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The sage’s statement and the worthy’s reply are naturally distinct in wording and tone. This essay is warm and polished without being superficial, unhurried without being strained, closely reasoned, clear, and pure. It stands alone above all the other compositions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Both the reality of the sage’s humility and the worthy’s feelings of admiration are apprehended and fully brought out. This is truly an excellent composition.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The ideas and language are clear and lucid.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: Refined and pure, elegant and vigorous.

The sage spoke modestly of what he could do, yet his disciples considered it difficult to attain. For what the sage could do represented the utmost achievement of benevolence and sagehood. Thus, although he spoke of it modestly, could those beginning with elementary learning readily reach it? Once the Master said: “As for the principle present in each person, greatness that brings transformation is called sagehood; completeness that lacks nothing is called benevolence. Are there people in the world who describe me in these terms? Yet their incipient workings are subtle and refined, beyond the scrutiny of shallow understanding; their ultimate reach is vast, beyond attainment by an easy shortcut. Thus I am still looking toward them without yet seeing them. As for spiritual …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
化昭融而生知安行之皆妙天理渾淪而全體
大用之兼該是旣聖與仁矣則吾豈敢耶抑性
分之常不可以不勉教思之益不可以不求故
吾則體之而弗忘焉蓋爲之于已而發憤時敏
之無斁誨之于人而啓迪善道之惟勤惟于聖
仁而學之也則可謂云爾已矣是則夫子之能
事而猶不自居者在門人視之益以難矣故公
西華仰而嘆曰以赤之觀於夫子也聖之至而
仁之極也固羣弟子之不可幾矣今而不自居
===
也曰爲之力而誨之勤也抑豈羣弟子所能學
耶蓋爲可能也而不厭則非至誠無息者不足
以純其功誨可能也而不倦則非大公無我者
不足以神其化故遊于夫子之門非不欲升堂
而入室即乎夫子之教則猶天之不可階而升
矣是知夫子之不能者乃天下之至能而其所
可能者正唯弟子之不能也非聖仁而能若是
乎吁公西華可謂深知夫子者矣抑聖人之道
猶天然門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也固宜謙已
punctuated: 化昭融，而生知安行之皆妙；天理渾淪，而全體大用之兼該，是旣聖與仁矣，則吾豈敢耶？抑性分之常，不可以不勉；教思之益，不可以不求。故吾則體之而弗忘焉。蓋爲之于已，而發憤時敏之無斁；誨之于人，而啓迪善道之惟勤。惟于聖仁而學之也，則可謂云爾已矣。」是則夫子之能事，而猶不自居者，在門人視之，益以難矣。故公西華仰而嘆曰：「以赤之觀於夫子也，聖之至而仁之極也，固羣弟子之不可幾矣。今而不自居也，曰爲之力而誨之勤也，抑豈羣弟子所能學耶？蓋爲可能也，而不厭，則非至誠無息者不足以純其功；誨可能也，而不倦，則非大公無我者不足以神其化。故遊于夫子之門，非不欲升堂而入室；即乎夫子之教，則猶天之不可階而升矣。」是知夫子之不能者，乃天下之至能，而其所可能者，正唯弟子之不能也。非聖仁而能若是乎？吁！公西華可謂深知夫子者矣！抑聖人之道猶天，然門弟子不能徧觀而盡識也，固宜謙已
translation_en: …transformation is luminous and all-pervading, and both knowing from birth and acting with ease are wondrously perfected; Heaven’s principle forms an undivided whole, embracing its entire substance and its great functioning. This is already sagehood and benevolence: how would I dare claim them? Yet one must strive to fulfill what properly belongs to one’s nature, and must seek to deepen one’s concern for teaching. Thus I embody these things without forgetting them. In practicing them myself, I rouse my resolve and apply myself diligently at every opportunity, without wearying; in teaching others, I work assiduously to enlighten and guide them along the good Way. Only of learning to attain sagehood and benevolence may I allow this much to be said of me.” These were the Master’s accomplishments, yet he would not claim them for himself; to his disciples, they seemed all the more difficult to attain. Thus Gongxi Hua looked up in admiration and sighed: “As I, Chi, see the Master, he has reached the utmost in sagehood and the pinnacle of benevolence—heights that we disciples cannot hope to approach. Now he declines to claim these for himself, saying only that he strives in practice and labors diligently in teaching. But how could we disciples learn even this? Practice may be possible, but to practice without ever wearying requires unceasing, utmost sincerity to bring that achievement to perfection. Teaching may be possible, but to teach without ever tiring requires complete impartiality and selflessness to make its transforming influence wondrous. Thus those who study at the Master’s gate certainly wish to ascend his hall and enter his inner chamber; yet when we approach the Master’s teaching, it is like Heaven, which no stairway allows us to ascend.” We see from this that what the Master professes himself unable to do is the highest accomplishment under Heaven, while what he acknowledges himself able to do is precisely what his disciples cannot do. Could anyone accomplish this without sagehood and benevolence? Ah! Gongxi Hua may indeed be said to have understood the Master deeply! Yet the sage’s Way is like Heaven, and his disciples cannot survey it in its entirety or comprehend it fully. It was certainly fitting that he should humble himself …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而誨之矣然聖人亦豈以仁聖自大而故爲是
以謙之耶蓋道無終窮學無止法聖人之心一
惟日而不足耳故乾乾終日者進德之誠也亹
亹不倦者脩業之至也富有日新者德之盛而
業之大也學有矜以自足惰以自畫斯畔道也
遠矣
誠者天之道也
王燾
同考試官教諭蔡批推原天道秩秩有章深
===
於體認非徒文也
同考試官教諭石批認意不真作多浮泛求
其發揮詳盡詞理竝至僅閲此篇
考試官教諭陳批精當
考試官學正陳批造理之文
中庸指誠之理原於天以明誠身之本也蓋誠
者天所命爲性者也其道豈非天乎中庸推本
而指言之欲使誠身者知所本也今夫爲政之
道始於明善而歸於誠身是吾人之身固有所
punctuated:
而誨之矣。然聖人亦豈以仁聖自大，而故爲是以謙之耶？蓋道無終窮，學無止法，聖人之心一惟日而不足耳。故乾乾終日者，進德之誠也；亹亹不倦者，脩業之至也；富有日新者，德之盛而業之大也。學有矜以自足，惰以自畫，斯畔道也遠矣。

誠者天之道也
王燾

同考試官教諭蔡批：推原天道，秩秩有章，深於體認，非徒文也。
同考試官教諭石批：認意不真，作多浮泛；求其發揮詳盡，詞理竝至，僅閲此篇。
考試官教諭陳批：精當。
考試官學正陳批：造理之文。

《中庸》指誠之理原於天，以明誠身之本也。蓋誠者，天所命爲性者也，其道豈非天乎？《中庸》推本而指言之，欲使誠身者知所本也。今夫爲政之道，始於明善，而歸於誠身，是吾人之身固有所
translation_en:
…and instruct them. Yet could the sage regard his benevolence and sageliness as grounds for self-importance, and deliberately speak thus to display humility? The Way has no end, and learning has no rule that permits stopping. In the sage’s heart, there is only the sense that each day affords insufficient time. Thus, unremitting diligence throughout the day is sincerity in advancing virtue; tireless exertion is the utmost cultivation of one’s undertakings; abundant possession and daily renewal constitute flourishing virtue and great accomplishment. If, in learning, one becomes conceited and self-satisfied, or indolently sets limits upon oneself, one departs far indeed from the Way.

“Sincerity Is the Way of Heaven”
Wang Tao

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “It traces the Way of Heaven to its source, proceeding in an orderly and well-articulated manner. It shows profound personal apprehension, not merely literary accomplishment.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: “Understanding of the meaning is often inexact, and compositions are mostly superficial and diffuse. In seeking a thorough exposition in which expression and principle alike attain excellence, I have encountered only this essay.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Refined and apt.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Director: “An essay that penetrates principle.”

The Doctrine of the Mean identifies the principle of sincerity as originating in Heaven, thereby clarifying the foundation for making oneself sincere. Sincerity is what Heaven ordains as human nature: is not its Way therefore Heaven’s? The Doctrine of the Mean traces it to its foundation and explicitly identifies it, wishing those who would make themselves sincere to know that on which they must ground themselves. Now, the way of governing begins with understanding goodness and culminates in making oneself sincere. Thus, within our own persons there assuredly is…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
謂誠者其本也貞而靜而其中也湛而一確
乎五性之咸具純而不雜其體也粹乎萬善之
兼備順而不妄其用也是誠也者豈由外鑠我
哉蓋天者理之所自出命者性之所由成於穆
之妙主宰乎一陰一陽之始者是貞而靜者之
體也惟皇之衷流行乎一動一靜之間者是湛
而一者之質也其通也誠爲之通則善之繼也
而吾之誠斯源矣其復也誠爲之復則性之成
也而吾之誠斯立矣五常之本其爲物不貳者
===
之妙合而凝乎彼形而後善惡分焉者則雜以
欲矣而非誠之本也百行之原其惟命不已者
之保合而正乎彼感於物而萬事出焉者則動
以人矣而非天之命也故曰誠者天之道也是
則誠身者誠此者也明善者明此者也明乎善
則身可誠身誠則達德備而達道九經皆可舉
而措之天下無難矣是以誠之爲貴而人道之
教皆所以復其天也大哉誠乎其盡天下之道
乎厥後誠明明誠之論天道人道之分大之而
punctuated: 謂誠者，其本也，貞而靜；而其中也，湛而一。確乎五性之咸具，純而不雜，其體也；粹乎萬善之兼備，順而不妄，其用也。是誠也者，豈由外鑠我哉？蓋天者，理之所自出；命者，性之所由成。於穆之妙，主宰乎一陰一陽之始者，是貞而靜者之體也；惟皇之衷，流行乎一動一靜之間者，是湛而一者之質也。其通也，誠爲之通，則善之繼也，而吾之誠斯源矣；其復也，誠爲之復，則性之成也，而吾之誠斯立矣。五常之本，其爲物不貳者之妙合而凝乎？彼形而後善惡分焉者，則雜以欲矣，而非誠之本也。百行之原，其惟命不已者之保合而正乎？彼感於物而萬事出焉者，則動以人矣，而非天之命也。故曰：「誠者，天之道也。」是則誠身者，誠此者也；明善者，明此者也。明乎善，則身可誠；身誠，則達德備，而達道九經皆可舉而措之天下，無難矣。是以誠之爲貴，而人道之教皆所以復其天也。大哉誠乎！其盡天下之道乎！厥後誠明、明誠之論，天道、人道之分，大之而
translation_en:
…what is called sincerity: at its root, it is steadfast and still; within, it is clear and undivided. Firmly possessing all five moral qualities, pure and unmixed—such is its substance. Perfectly encompassing all goodness, following principle without falsity—such is its operation. Could this sincerity be something imposed upon me from outside? Heaven is that from which principle issues; its mandate is that through which our nature is constituted. The profound mystery that presides over the inception of the alternation of yin and yang is the substance of this steadfastness and stillness. The norm bestowed by august Heaven, flowing through the alternation of activity and stillness, is the essential character of this clarity and unity. In its unfolding, sincerity effects that unfolding: this is the continuation of goodness, and here our sincerity has its source. In its return, sincerity effects that return: this is the constitution of our nature, and here our sincerity is established.

Is not the root of the five constant virtues the wondrous union and consolidation of that which, as a reality, is undivided? As for the differentiation of good and evil that occurs after physical form takes shape, this involves an admixture of desire and is not sincerity in its original state. Is not the source of all conduct the preservation, union, and rectification effected by Heaven’s unceasing mandate? As for the myriad affairs that arise when one is affected by external things, these involve the impulses of human activity and are not Heaven’s mandate. Thus it is said: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven.” To make oneself sincere is to realize this sincerity; to understand goodness is to understand this. When goodness is understood, one can make oneself sincere. When one is sincere, the universally applicable virtues are complete, and the universally applicable relationships and the nine guiding principles of government can all be put into practice throughout the world without difficulty. This is why sincerity is prized, and why all teaching concerning the human Way serves to restore what is heavenly within us.

Great indeed is sincerity! Does it not encompass the entire Way of the world? The subsequent discussion of proceeding from sincerity to understanding and from understanding to sincerity, and the distinction between the Way of Heaven and the human Way, when extended to their grandest scope…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
參天地贊化育近之而立心爲己何者不始於
誠而何者不出於天是以中庸之義始之曰天
命之謂性於脩身而曰不可以不知天於誠身
而曰誠者天之道也其指一也
乃若其情則可以爲善矣乃所謂善也若
夫爲不善非才之罪也惻隱之心人皆
有之羞惡之心人皆有之恭敬之心人
皆有之是非之心人皆有之惻隱之心
仁也羞惡之心義也恭敬之心禮也是
===
非之心智也仁義禮智非由外鑠我也
我固有之也弗思耳矣故曰求則得之
舍則失之或相倍蓰而無筭者不能盡
其才者也詩曰天生蒸民有物有則民
之秉夷好是懿德孔子曰爲此詩者其
知道乎故有物必有則民之秉夷也故
好是懿德
呂穆
同考試官教諭孫批因情觀性此孟氏深切
punctuated:
參天地，贊化育，近之而立心爲己，何者不始於誠，而何者不出於天？是以《中庸》之義，始之曰「天命之謂性」，於脩身而曰「不可以不知天」，於誠身而曰「誠者天之道也」，其指一也。
乃若其情，則可以爲善矣，乃所謂善也。若夫爲不善，非才之罪也。惻隱之心，人皆有之；羞惡之心，人皆有之；恭敬之心，人皆有之；是非之心，人皆有之。惻隱之心，仁也；羞惡之心，義也；恭敬之心，禮也；是非之心，智也。仁義禮智，非由外鑠我也，我固有之也，弗思耳矣。故曰：「求則得之，舍則失之。」或相倍蓰而無筭者，不能盡其才者也。《詩》曰：「天生蒸民，有物有則。民之秉夷，好是懿德。」孔子曰：「爲此詩者，其知道乎！故有物必有則，民之秉夷也，故好是懿德。」
呂穆
同考試官教諭孫批：因情觀性，此孟氏深切
translation_en:
…to form a triad with Heaven and Earth and assist their transforming and nourishing activity, or, closer to oneself, to establish one’s resolve and cultivate oneself—what does not begin in sincerity, and what does not issue from Heaven? Thus the Doctrine of the Mean begins by saying, “What Heaven decrees is called human nature”; concerning self-cultivation it says, “One cannot fail to know Heaven”; and concerning making oneself sincere it says, “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven.” Their purport is one.
“As for people’s natural dispositions, they can become good: this is what is meant by calling human nature good. If they do what is not good, it is not the fault of their native capacities. Everyone possesses a heart of compassion; everyone possesses a heart of shame and aversion; everyone possesses a heart of reverence and respect; everyone possesses a heart that distinguishes right from wrong. The heart of compassion is benevolence; the heart of shame and aversion is righteousness; the heart of reverence and respect is ritual propriety; the heart that distinguishes right from wrong is wisdom. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are not infused into me from outside. I inherently possess them; I simply fail to reflect upon them. Thus it is said: ‘Seek them and you will obtain them; abandon them and you will lose them.’ That people differ from one another twofold, fivefold, or beyond calculation is because they cannot fully develop their native capacities. The Book of Odes says: ‘Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is a norm. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this beautiful virtue.’ Confucius said: ‘The author of this ode surely understood the Way! Thus, wherever there is a thing, there must be a norm; because the people hold fast to their constant nature, they love this beautiful virtue.’”
Lü Mu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: “To observe human nature through its natural dispositions—this is Mengzi’s profound and penetrating…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之論真足以解羣疑而垂世訓作者多窘於題發
揮未盡若此者可謂約而能達莊而能辨矣
同考試官教諭李批不出數語說盡題意筆
力雄健老成之作
考試官教諭陳批整約意足
考試官學正陳批冲淡有味
大賢本人情而言性善必引言以明之也蓋情
動于性也情善而性斯善矣徵之前言豈不益
明矣乎孟子曉公都子者如此蓋曰吾謂性之
===
善者豈無稽耶蓋性者心之理情者性之動吾
見順應之常本可以為善則知主宰之真斷然
而無惡故謂之善也蓋情善而性固善焉矣若
夫事為之際或戾其本真則是物欲之交不免
于陷溺非才之罪也蓋性善而才亦善焉矣何
也惻隱之心羞惡之心恭敬之心是非之心夫
人皆有之情也善端發見而實原于性有不可
以為善者乎惻隱即仁羞惡即義恭敬即禮是
非即智皆天所賦之性也心體純全而實主乎
punctuated:
之論，真足以解羣疑而垂世訓。作者多窘於題，發揮未盡，若此者可謂約而能達，莊而能辨矣。

同考試官教諭李批：不出數語，說盡題意，筆力雄健，老成之作。

考試官教諭陳批：整約意足。

考試官學正陳批：冲淡有味。

大賢本人情而言性善，必引言以明之也。蓋情動于性也，情善而性斯善矣。徵之前言，豈不益明矣乎？孟子曉公都子者如此。蓋曰：吾謂性之善者，豈無稽耶？蓋性者，心之理；情者，性之動。吾見順應之常，本可以為善，則知主宰之真，斷然而無惡，故謂之善也。蓋情善而性固善焉矣。若夫事為之際，或戾其本真，則是物欲之交，不免于陷溺，非才之罪也。蓋性善而才亦善焉矣。何也？惻隱之心、羞惡之心、恭敬之心、是非之心，夫人皆有之，情也。善端發見，而實原于性，有不可以為善者乎？惻隱即仁，羞惡即義，恭敬即禮，是非即智，皆天所賦之性也。心體純全，而實主乎
translation_en:
…an argument truly sufficient to resolve the many doubts and leave instruction for generations to come. Writers are often constrained by this topic and fail to develop its meaning fully. A composition such as this may be called concise yet expressive, dignified yet discerning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: In just a few phrases, it exhausts the meaning of the topic. Its writing is vigorous and forceful—the work of a seasoned hand.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Orderly and concise, with the meaning fully conveyed.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: Quiet and unadorned, yet rich in savor.

The great worthy bases his assertion that human nature is good on human feelings, and necessarily cites earlier sayings to make it clear. For feelings arise from the activity of human nature: if feelings are good, then human nature is good. Would corroborating this with earlier sayings not make it still clearer? Such was the way Mengzi instructed Gongduzi. His meaning was this: “Could my assertion that human nature is good be without foundation? Human nature is the principle of the heart-mind; feelings are the activity of that nature. I observe that its ordinary, natural responses are inherently capable of goodness, and thus know that its true governing essence is decidedly without evil. Hence I call it good. Feelings are good, and human nature is assuredly good. If, in the course of acting and conducting affairs, one sometimes goes against one's original, true nature, this results from entanglement with material desires, through which one cannot avoid becoming submerged. It is no fault of one's inherent capacities. Human nature is good, and one's inherent capacities are likewise good. Why is this? The heart of compassion, the heart of shame and aversion, the heart of reverence and respect, and the heart that distinguishes right from wrong—everyone possesses these. They are feelings. These beginnings of goodness manifest themselves, but their actual source lies in human nature. Could any of them be incapable of goodness? Compassion is benevolence; shame and aversion are righteousness; reverence and respect are ritual propriety; distinguishing right from wrong is wisdom. All belong to the nature endowed by Heaven. The substance of the heart-mind is pure and complete, and indeed governs …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
情何莫而非至善者乎是非外鑠也我固有之
而人自弗思耳故曰求則得之舍則失之而善
惡之塗以殊或相倍蓰或至無算而善惡之去
益遠者正由不能精思以求諸己擴充以盡其
才者也豈其性之本然哉考之詩曰天生蒸民
有物有則民之秉夷好是懿德蓋言乎其性情
也孔子則曰爲此詩者其知道乎故有物必有
則民之秉夷也故好是懿德亦誠有取乎爾矣
蓋秉夷之理一人生而靜天之性者也好德之
===
誠一感物而動性之欲者也然則性善云者豈
不昭昭也哉彼謂無善無不善可以爲善可以
爲不善有性善有性不善者惑斯甚矣抑性之
易明如此而當時之人乃交于物欲溺于氣稟
茫茫焉不復知性爲何物至于邪說橫流天理
淪昧雖告子之賢猶不能察况其他乎是大道
既隱聖敎不明于天下久矣不有孟子孰開我
人故性善之論扶世立敎之大綱也
易
punctuated:
情，何莫而非至善者乎？是非外鑠也，我固有之，而人自弗思耳。故曰：「求則得之，舍則失之。」而善惡之塗以殊，或相倍蓰，或至無算，而善惡之去益遠者，正由不能精思以求諸己，擴充以盡其才者也，豈其性之本然哉？考之《詩》曰：「天生蒸民，有物有則。民之秉夷，好是懿德。」蓋言乎其性情也。孔子則曰：「爲此詩者，其知道乎！故有物必有則，民之秉夷也，故好是懿德。」亦誠有取乎爾矣。蓋秉夷之理一，人生而靜，天之性者也；好德之誠一，感物而動，性之欲者也。然則性善云者，豈不昭昭也哉？彼謂無善無不善、可以爲善可以爲不善、有性善有性不善者，惑斯甚矣。抑性之易明如此，而當時之人乃交于物欲，溺于氣稟，茫茫焉不復知性爲何物，至于邪說橫流，天理淪昧。雖告子之賢猶不能察，况其他乎？是大道既隱，聖敎不明于天下久矣。不有孟子，孰開我人？故性善之論，扶世立敎之大綱也。

易
translation_en:
…the feelings: how could any of these fail to be supremely good? This is not something infused into me from outside; I inherently possess it, but people simply fail to reflect upon it themselves. Thus it is said: “Seek it and you will obtain it; abandon it and you will lose it.” The paths of good and evil thereby diverge. Some people differ from others twofold or fivefold, some beyond all reckoning. That the distance between good and evil grows ever greater is precisely because people fail to reflect carefully and seek within themselves, and to extend and develop their goodness so as to realize their capacities fully. How could this be the original condition of their nature?

Consider the statement in the Book of Odes: “Heaven brought forth the multitude of the people; for every thing there is a rule. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this admirable virtue.” This speaks of their nature and feelings. Confucius said: “Did not the author of this ode understand the Way? For every thing there must be a rule; because the people hold fast to their constant nature, they therefore love this admirable virtue.” He indeed had good reason to approve these words. The principle of holding fast to this constant nature is one [?]: “People are still at birth”—this is their Heaven-given nature. The sincerity of their love of virtue is one [?]: “They are stirred upon contact with things”—these are the desires of that nature. Is it not, then, perfectly clear what is meant by saying that human nature is good? Those who say that nature is neither good nor bad, that it can be made good or made bad, or that some people have good natures and others bad ones, are profoundly confused.

Yet although human nature is so readily understood, people of that time became entangled in material desires and submerged in their endowments of vital energy. Bewildered, they no longer knew what human nature was. Heterodox doctrines consequently ran unchecked, and Heaven’s principle sank into obscurity. Even someone as worthy as Gaozi could not discern it; how much less could others! The great Way had become hidden, and the teaching of the sages had long ceased to be manifest throughout the world. Had there been no Mengzi, who would have enlightened us? Thus the doctrine that human nature is good is the fundamental framework for sustaining society and establishing moral teaching.

Book of Changes

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也六爻發揮
旁通情也時乘六龍以御天也雲行雨
施天下平也
沈束
同考試官教諭王批善發乾道聖治之蘊者
同考試官教諭陳批易義似此潔淨精微絶少
考試官教諭陳批簡明詳盡
===
考試官學正陳批詞理精緻
文言備賛乾道之大而因言聖人配天之治焉
夫四德統於乾而體於聖人者也文言備舉之
以賛乾也至哉今夫乾者統四德妙萬物而爲
言者也觀於乾元可知矣蓋乾元者物之所資
以始也而流形之機達焉由是而利貞者物之
自收而藏也而性情之實見焉曰始亨則顯諸
仁而溥天下以嘉美者乾始也曰性情則藏諸
用而妙美利於不言者亦乾始也甚哉乾始之
punctuated:
「乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。六爻發揮，旁通情也。時乘六龍，以御天也。雲行雨施，天下平也。」
沈束
同考試官教諭王批：「善發乾道聖治之蘊者。」
同考試官教諭陳批：「易義似此潔淨精微，絶少。」
考試官教諭陳批：「簡明詳盡。」
考試官學正陳批：「詞理精緻。」
文言備賛乾道之大，而因言聖人配天之治焉。夫四德統於乾而體於聖人者也，文言備舉之以賛乾也，至哉！今夫乾者，統四德、妙萬物而爲言者也，觀於乾元可知矣。蓋乾元者，物之所資以始也，而流形之機達焉。由是而利貞者，物之自收而藏也，而性情之實見焉。曰始亨，則顯諸仁而溥天下以嘉美者，乾始也；曰性情，則藏諸用而妙美利於不言者，亦乾始也。甚哉，乾始之
translation_en:
“The primal power of Qian is that which originates and brings to fulfillment; benefit and constancy are its nature and inherent disposition. Qian, in originating things, can benefit all under Heaven with its beautiful benefits, without specifying what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, it is pure, unalloyed, and refined. The six lines unfold their significance, communicating their inherent dispositions in every direction. In accordance with the time, he mounts the six dragons to govern Heaven. Clouds move and rain falls; all under Heaven is at peace.”
Shen Shu 沈束
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “It admirably brings out the profound implications of the Way of Qian and the sage’s governance.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Expositions of the meaning of the Book of Changes as clear, pure, subtle, and precise as this are exceedingly rare.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Concise and clear, thorough and complete.”
Examiner Chen, Director of Studies, comments: “Both the language and the reasoning are finely wrought.”
The Commentary on the Words fully praises the greatness of the Way of Qian and thereby speaks of the sage’s governance, which matches Heaven. The four virtues are united in Qian and embodied in the sage. The Commentary on the Words sets them all forth to praise Qian: how consummate it is! Now Qian is a term for that which unites the four virtues and wondrously brings the myriad things into being. This can be understood by contemplating Qian’s primal power. For Qian’s primal power is that upon which things depend for their beginnings, and through it the dynamic process by which they flow into form proceeds freely. Following from this, benefit and constancy are the gathering in and storing away of things themselves; therein the reality of their nature and inherent disposition becomes manifest. When we speak of origination and fulfillment, it is Qian’s originating power that manifests itself in benevolence and spreads excellence and beauty throughout all under Heaven. When we speak of nature and inherent disposition, it is likewise Qian’s originating power that conceals itself in functioning and wondrously bestows beautiful benefits without speaking. How extraordinary is Qian’s originating…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大也其能統天而成萬物者乎然則乾之大可
知已蓋其靜專動直而無所屈撓非剛且健乎
氣布時行而無少偏過非中且正乎絕乎陰柔
邪惡之雜何純粹也極於無聲無臭之神又何
精也乾之大也若是其能妙四德以成萬物也
有以哉體是道者其惟聖人乎聖人法乾於易
者也是故乾陽卦也六爻陽畫也曲盡天道至
精之蘊一皆龍德時成之撰故其時乘之以御
天也神道之設與天同用始焉至仁之潤雲行
===
雨施而天下被其惠者美利之澤也終焉至治
之成不識不知而萬國享其寧者不言之化也
由是觀之天大無外聖體其全其道固相配如
此夫雖然天有至德剛健中正純粹精是已故
萬物生聖人亦有至德純亦不已是已故天下
平平天下者王道也純亦不已天德也有天德
便可語王道象曰君子以自强不息此至德合
天所以行此四者而天下平之本也故曰乾元
亨利貞
punctuated:
大也！其能統天而成萬物者乎？然則乾之大可知已。蓋其靜專動直，而無所屈撓，非剛且健乎？氣布時行，而無少偏過，非中且正乎？絕乎陰柔邪惡之雜，何純粹也！極於無聲無臭之神，又何精也！乾之大也若是，其能妙四德以成萬物也，有以哉！體是道者，其惟聖人乎？聖人法乾於易者也。是故乾，陽卦也；六爻，陽畫也。曲盡天道至精之蘊，一皆龍德時成之撰，故其時乘之以御天也。神道之設，與天同用。始焉，至仁之潤，雲行雨施，而天下被其惠者，美利之澤也；終焉，至治之成，不識不知，而萬國享其寧者，不言之化也。由是觀之，天大無外，聖體其全，其道固相配如此夫！

雖然，天有至德，剛健中正純粹精是已，故萬物生；聖人亦有至德，純亦不已是已，故天下平。平天下者，王道也；純亦不已，天德也。有天德，便可語王道。《象》曰：「君子以自强不息。」此至德合天，所以行此四者而天下平之本也。故曰：「乾元亨利貞。」
translation_en:
…great indeed! Does it not encompass Heaven and bring the myriad things to completion? Thus the greatness of Qian may be understood. In stillness it is concentrated; in movement it is direct, never bending or yielding: is this not firmness and strength? Its vital energy spreads and moves with the seasons, without the slightest deviation or excess: is this not centrality and correctness? Entirely free from any admixture of yin softness or perversity and evil, how pure and unalloyed it is! Reaching the utmost spiritual efficacy, without sound or scent, how refined it is! Such is Qian’s greatness: there is indeed a basis for its wondrous operation of the four virtues to bring the myriad things to completion. Who but the sage embodies this Way? The sage takes Qian in the Book of Changes as his model. Thus Qian is a yang hexagram, and its six lines are yang strokes. They fully disclose the most refined mysteries of Heaven’s Way; all portray the timely accomplishment of the dragon’s virtue. Hence the sage mounts them at the appropriate times to ride upon Heaven. His establishment of the spiritual Way shares Heaven’s operation. At the beginning, the moistening influence of consummate benevolence is like moving clouds and falling rain: the favor that all under Heaven receive is the beneficence of its excellent benefits. At the culmination, perfect governance is achieved, without people perceiving or knowing it: the peace enjoyed by the myriad states is the transforming influence that works without words. Viewed thus, Heaven is so great that nothing lies outside it, and the sage embodies its entirety. Their Ways indeed correspond in this manner!

Nevertheless, Heaven possesses consummate virtue: firmness, strength, centrality, correctness, purity, and refinement are precisely this; hence the myriad things are born. The sage likewise possesses consummate virtue: purity that never ceases is precisely this; hence all under Heaven is at peace. Bringing peace to all under Heaven is the kingly Way; unceasing purity is Heaven’s virtue. With Heaven’s virtue, one may then speak of the kingly Way. The Commentary on the Images says: “The noble man thereby strengthens himself without cease.” This is consummate virtue in accord with Heaven, the foundation for practicing these four virtues and bringing peace to all under Heaven. Thus it is said: “Qian: origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy.”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
安土敦乎仁故能愛
俞守道
同考試官教諭王批脫去浮靡獨歸雅正因
文說理自出塵埃佳作也
同考試官教諭陳批曲盡聖人盡性之妙僅
見此篇
考試官教諭陳批體認親切
考試官學正陳批斐然成章
大傳極言聖人體仁之篤以見其盡性也夫仁
===
主乎愛非深於德者不能也故仁而敦於安土
斯為性之盡矣此聖人以易盡性之事大傳蓋
極言之謂夫仁以愛為德而體仁以安為極夫
惟有所動於外也則德有未純而愛之道亦息
惟聖人之仁性諸天者有以備萬善之長脩諸
己者有以立無欲之靜故身之所處順逆惟其
時也安焉而已本心之全德無時不在也常變
惟其適也順焉而已天理之周流無適不然也
處一而化隨在皆天理自然之安蓋無欲而好
punctuated:
安土敦乎仁，故能愛。
俞守道
同考試官教諭王批：脫去浮靡，獨歸雅正，因文說理，自出塵埃，佳作也。
同考試官教諭陳批：曲盡聖人盡性之妙，僅見此篇。
考試官教諭陳批：體認親切。
考試官學正陳批：斐然成章。
大傳極言聖人體仁之篤，以見其盡性也。夫仁主乎愛，非深於德者不能也。故仁而敦於安土，斯為性之盡矣。此聖人以易盡性之事，大傳蓋極言之。謂夫仁以愛為德，而體仁以安為極。夫惟有所動於外也，則德有未純，而愛之道亦息。惟聖人之仁，性諸天者有以備萬善之長，脩諸己者有以立無欲之靜。故身之所處，順逆惟其時也，安焉而已，本心之全德無時不在也；常變惟其適也，順焉而已，天理之周流無適不然也。處一而化，隨在皆天理自然之安，蓋無欲而好
translation_en:
“He rests content where he dwells and is steadfast in benevolence; thus he can love.”
Yu Shoudao
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Free of superficial ornament, this work turns wholly toward elegance and correctness. It elucidates principle through the text and rises above the dust of commonplace writing. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Only in this essay have I seen so thorough an exposition of the subtlety with which the sage fully realizes his nature.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Its understanding is intimate and true.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “Splendidly composed.”
The Great Commentary expounds to the fullest the sage’s steadfast embodiment of benevolence, thereby revealing how he fully realizes his nature. Benevolence centers on love: only one deeply grounded in virtue can accomplish this. Thus, when benevolence is made steadfast through contentment with one’s place, one’s nature is fully realized. This is how the sage fully realizes his nature through the Changes, and the Great Commentary expounds it to the fullest.
Benevolence, that is, has love as its virtue, while embodying benevolence reaches its culmination in being at ease. If one is stirred by external things, one’s virtue is not yet pure, and the way of love also ceases. Only in the sage’s benevolence does what Heaven has bestowed as his nature fully possess the foremost of all goodness, while what he cultivates within himself establishes the stillness of freedom from desire. Thus, whether his circumstances are favorable or adverse depends simply on the time; he rests content in them, and the complete virtue of his original mind is present at every moment. Whether he encounters ordinary conditions or change depends simply on what he meets; he accords with them, and the all-pervading flow of Heaven’s principle operates wherever he goes. Abiding in unity while responding to transformation, wherever he finds himself he enjoys the spontaneous ease of Heaven’s principle. For he is without desire, yet has likes…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無畏而惡而根心之蘊甚厚履道於坦隨寓無
人欲陷溺之危蓋非有所必非有所利而成性
之存甚固夫仁者愛之理體仁者長人之資聖
人之仁既敦則其心之公也必以天地萬物爲
一體而其施之厚也將以萬物各得其所爲極
致渾然中涵而愛之理已備凡爲仁民爲愛物
固其惻隱之發不可勝用者寂然不動而長人
之體已具凡爲博施爲濟衆皆其慈愛之存無
所不貫矣辟則天道之元而生物之理常具足
===
焉者也此聖人之仁也不與天地相似乎雖然
堯舜盡之矣好生之德洽于民心此能愛之實
也若孔子在陳無慍於匡無懼爲司寇而魯大
治何者非安何者非仁老安少懷其愛之在於
萬物有可見者故其言曰仁者安仁又曰仁人
之安宅至其賛易曰安土敦仁故能愛夫爲仁
而至於安斯可以言盡性斯可以語見易
書
無曠庶官天工人其代之天敘有典勅我
punctuated:
無畏而惡，而根心之蘊甚厚；履道於坦，隨寓無人欲陷溺之危，蓋非有所必，非有所利，而成性之存甚固。夫仁者，愛之理；體仁者，長人之資。聖人之仁既敦，則其心之公也，必以天地萬物爲一體；而其施之厚也，將以萬物各得其所爲極致。渾然中涵，而愛之理已備，凡爲仁民、爲愛物，固其惻隱之發不可勝用者；寂然不動，而長人之體已具，凡爲博施、爲濟衆，皆其慈愛之存無所不貫矣。辟則天道之元，而生物之理常具足焉者也。此聖人之仁也，不與天地相似乎？雖然，堯舜盡之矣。好生之德洽于民心，此能愛之實也。若孔子在陳無慍，於匡無懼，爲司寇而魯大治，何者非安？何者非仁？老安少懷，其愛之在於萬物有可見者。故其言曰：「仁者安仁。」又曰：「仁，人之安宅。」至其賛《易》曰：「安土敦仁，故能愛。」夫爲仁而至於安，斯可以言盡性，斯可以語見《易》。

書

無曠庶官，天工人其代之。天敘有典，勅我
translation_en:
…hating without fear, while what is rooted and stored in the heart is exceedingly rich. Treading the Way upon level ground, wherever he dwells he faces no danger of sinking into human desires. He neither insists upon a particular course nor pursues personal advantage, and his fully realized nature remains firmly preserved. Benevolence is the principle of love; embodying benevolence provides the capacity to lead others. Once the sage’s benevolence is deepened, the impartiality of his heart necessarily makes Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things one body; the generosity of his beneficence takes as its ultimate aim that all things should attain their proper places. Held within as an undivided whole, the principle of love is already complete. Showing benevolence to the people and love for other creatures are manifestations of his compassion, inexhaustible in their application. Still and unmoving, he already possesses the essential capacity to lead others. Bestowing benefits widely and aiding the multitude are expressions of his abiding compassionate love, which pervades everything. By analogy, this is the originating power of the Way of Heaven, in which the principle that generates things is always fully present. Does not this benevolence of the sage resemble Heaven and Earth? Yet Yao and Shun realized it to the fullest. Their virtue of cherishing life permeated the people’s hearts: this was the actual fulfillment of the capacity to love. As for Kongzi, he harbored no resentment in Chen and felt no fear in Kuang; when he served as Minister of Justice, Lu became well governed. Which of these deeds did not express being at ease? Which did not express benevolence? In giving the old security and cherishing the young, his love for all things becomes visible. Thus the saying goes: “The benevolent are at ease in benevolence.” It also says: “Benevolence is the secure dwelling of human beings.” And in his commentary on the Changes, he says: “At ease in his place and deep in benevolence, he can therefore love.” When the practice of benevolence reaches this state of ease, one may speak of fully realizing one’s nature and of comprehending the Changes.

Documents

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
五典五惇哉天秩有禮自我五禮有庸
哉同寅協恭和衷哉天命有德五服五
章哉天討有罪五刑五用哉政事懋哉
懋哉
呂穆
同考試官教諭孫批此篇說盡知人安民而
君臣相天之道殆無餘蘊其心臯陶之心而演臯
陶之謨者歟
考試官教諭陳批充贍
考試官學正陳批闡明仁智歸重天人深
得臯陶謨明弼諧之義
===
大臣陳知人安民之謨必推天而嚴諸人焉夫
君人者承天以從事者也而知人安民可弗慎
歟此臯陶之告其君而必嚴之天也意謂天之
立君以為民也君之用人以事天也吾欲君之
知人安民而豈徒哉誠以翕受敷施官若備矣
然用之不當其才而官斯曠焉必簡之于灼知
之餘使位不浮乎其德任之于論辨之後使職
punctuated:
五典，五惇哉！天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！同寅協恭和衷哉！天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！政事懋哉，懋哉！

呂穆

同考試官教諭孫批：此篇說盡知人安民，而君臣相天之道殆無餘蘊。其心臯陶之心，而演臯陶之謨者歟！

考試官教諭陳批：充贍。

考試官學正陳批：闡明仁智，歸重天人，深得臯陶謨明弼諧之義。

大臣陳知人安民之謨，必推天而嚴諸人焉。夫君人者，承天以從事者也，而知人安民可弗慎歟？此臯陶之告其君，而必嚴之天也。意謂天之立君以為民也，君之用人以事天也。吾欲君之知人安民，而豈徒哉？誠以翕受敷施，官若備矣，然用之不當其才，而官斯曠焉。必簡之于灼知之餘，使位不浮乎其德；任之于論辨之後，使職
translation_en:
…the five norms of human relationships: let them all be earnestly upheld! Heaven has established the ordered rites; let the five rites we observe be regularly practiced! Be united in reverence, joined in respect, and harmonious at heart! Heaven commissions the virtuous: let the five grades of ceremonial dress distinguish them! Heaven punishes the guilty: let the five punishments be applied as appropriate! Be diligent in affairs of government—be diligent!

Lü Mu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: This essay exhaustively explains discerning worthy men and bringing peace to the people, leaving scarcely anything unexplored in the way ruler and ministers assist Heaven. Does its author not take Gao Yao’s heart as his own and expound Gao Yao’s counsels?

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Full and ample.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: It elucidates benevolence and wisdom, placing the chief emphasis on Heaven and humanity. It deeply grasps the meaning of enlightened rule and harmonious assistance in the Counsels of Gao Yao.

When a great minister presents counsels on discerning worthy men and bringing peace to the people, he must trace their basis to Heaven and impress their gravity upon men. One who rules over men acts in obedience to Heaven: can he fail to exercise care in discerning worthy men and bringing peace to the people? This is why Gao Yao, in admonishing his ruler, necessarily invokes Heaven to give his counsel solemn force. His meaning is this: Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people, and rulers employ men in order to serve Heaven. Can my desire that the ruler discern worthy men and bring peace to the people be without grounds? Indeed, when men are received from all quarters and assigned their duties, the offices may appear fully staffed. Yet if their employment does not suit their abilities, those offices are effectively left vacant. They must be selected only after their qualities are clearly understood, so that their positions do not exceed their virtue; they must be appointed only after deliberation and discrimination, so that their duties…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
必稱乎其官蓋天以無心而成化而大君之所
責成皆其若天而無違者也君以無爲而成能
而百工之所敬承皆其代天而有終者也使一
職之或曠則非惟無以興事亦非所以事天矣
此知人之不可以已也至于風動協中民若安
矣然治之不盡其道而民作慝焉故五典天敘
也自我惇之五禮天秩也自我庸之皆君之所
以經綸乎天下者也君必寅恭于上而爲之臣
者不敢替厥德焉則彝倫以正其有弗化于訓
===
者乎天命有德則五服以章之天討有罪則五
刑以懲之皆君之所以鼓舞乎天下者也君必
勤恤于上而爲之臣者不敢𢘆厥心焉則勸戒
以昭其有弗若于政者乎使一職之未盡則非
惟無以安民亦非所以事天矣此安民之不可
以已也吁推天以知人則智之盡推天以安民
則仁之至臯陶可謂達天人之際者矣雖然要
之自君心始耳心之不純而能用賢以安民者
鮮矣故元首明則股肱良而庶事康言君心之
punctuated: 必稱乎其官。蓋天以無心而成化，而大君之所責成，皆其若天而無違者也；君以無爲而成能，而百工之所敬承，皆其代天而有終者也。使一職之或曠，則非惟無以興事，亦非所以事天矣。此知人之不可以已也。至于風動協中，民若安矣，然治之不盡其道，而民作慝焉。故五典，天敘也，自我惇之；五禮，天秩也，自我庸之，皆君之所以經綸乎天下者也。君必寅恭于上，而爲之臣者不敢替厥德焉，則彝倫以正，其有弗化于訓者乎？天命有德，則五服以章之；天討有罪，則五刑以懲之，皆君之所以鼓舞乎天下者也。君必勤恤于上，而爲之臣者不敢𢘆厥心焉，則勸戒以昭，其有弗若于政者乎？使一職之未盡，則非惟無以安民，亦非所以事天矣。此安民之不可以已也。吁！推天以知人，則智之盡；推天以安民，則仁之至。臯陶可謂達天人之際者矣。雖然，要之自君心始耳。心之不純，而能用賢以安民者鮮矣。故元首明，則股肱良，而庶事康，言君心之
translation_en:
…must correspond to the office he holds. Heaven accomplishes its transforming work without deliberate intent, and all those whom the sovereign holds responsible for results must follow Heaven without departing from it. The ruler accomplishes his work through nonaction, and what the officials reverently undertake is to act on Heaven’s behalf and carry their work through to completion. If even one office is left unattended, this not only prevents affairs from being carried forward but also fails to serve Heaven. Thus one must never cease discerning the character and abilities of men.

When the people respond as if moved by the wind and accord with the Mean, they seem to be at peace. Yet if governing them does not fully realize the proper Way, they will commit evil. Thus the five fundamental relationships are Heaven’s ordering, and it is for us to make them substantial; the five rites are Heaven’s prescribed ranks, and it is for us to put them into practice. These are all means by which the ruler orders the realm. If the ruler above is reverent and respectful, and those who serve him dare not abandon their virtue, the enduring human relationships will be set right. Could anyone then fail to be transformed by his instruction?

Heaven commissions the virtuous: the five grades of official dress make this manifest. Heaven punishes the guilty: the five punishments chastise them. These are all means by which the ruler rouses the realm to action. If the ruler above is diligent and solicitous, and those who serve him dare not let their hearts grow complacent [?], encouragement and admonition will be made clear. Could anyone then fail to comply with his government? If even one duty remains unfulfilled, this not only prevents the people from being brought to peace but also fails to serve Heaven. Thus one must never cease bringing peace to the people.

Ah! To take Heaven as the basis for discerning men is wisdom fully realized; to take Heaven as the basis for bringing peace to the people is benevolence at its utmost. Gao Yao may indeed be said to have understood the nexus between Heaven and humanity. Nevertheless, the essential starting point is the ruler’s heart alone. Few whose hearts are impure can employ worthy men to bring peace to the people. Thus, when the head is enlightened, the limbs are good, and all affairs prosper. This speaks of the ruler’s heart’s…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
純也勅天之道不在兹乎此臯陶知人安民之
謨所以繼迪德之後也
次五曰建用皇極
孫學古
同考試官教諭孫批數至五而中道至極而
止作者多不知故説得理數悖戾獨子以象義言
得禹心法
考試官教諭陳批明當典雅
考試官學正陳批發出大禹第疇之旨亦
===
可謂皇極經世之文矣
聖人以五疇之極歸之君所以立本也夫人君
以立極為本而五者數之極也聖王第而歸之
君也有以哉且夫洛書之數居中而臨外者莫
尊于五以一而含八者亦莫備于五統四生數
於前而其體以具分四成數於後而其用以成
是誠陰陽之會也奇偶之宗也語其位則有君
之象焉語其德則有極之義焉故禹因而第之
曰建用皇極蓋以人君居中正之位以臨萬邦
punctuated:
純也。勅天之道不在兹乎？此臯陶知人安民之謨所以繼迪德之後也。

次五曰：「建用皇極。」
孫學古

同考試官教諭孫批：「數至五而中，道至極而止。作者多不知，故説得理數悖戾。獨子以象義言，得禹心法。」
考試官教諭陳批：「明當典雅。」
考試官學正陳批：「發出大禹第疇之旨，亦可謂皇極經世之文矣。」

聖人以五疇之極歸之君，所以立本也。夫人君以立極為本，而五者數之極也。聖王第而歸之君也，有以哉！且夫洛書之數，居中而臨外者，莫尊于五；以一而含八者，亦莫備于五。統四生數於前，而其體以具；分四成數於後，而其用以成。是誠陰陽之會也，奇偶之宗也。語其位，則有君之象焉；語其德，則有極之義焉。故禹因而第之曰：「建用皇極。」蓋以人君居中正之位，以臨萬邦
translation_en:
…the purity of the ruler’s mind. Does not the way of putting Heaven’s order into effect lie here? This is why Gao Yao’s counsel on knowing men and bringing peace to the people follows his counsel on practicing virtue.

“Fifth in order: establish and employ the August Ultimate.”
By Sun Xuegu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: “Numbers reach their center at five; the Way reaches its culmination at the Ultimate. Most writers do not understand this, and consequently their explanations set principle and number at odds. You alone discuss it through images and meanings, grasping Yu’s teaching of the mind.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Clear, apt, classically refined.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “This brings out Great Yu’s intent in ordering the categories. It may indeed be called an essay on ordering the world through the August Ultimate.”

The sage assigned the Ultimate of the fifth category to the ruler in order to establish the foundation. For the ruler takes establishing the Ultimate as his foundation, and five is the ultimate of numbers. The sage king had good reason to place it in this order and assign it to the ruler! Among the numbers of the Luo Writing, none is more exalted than five, which occupies the center and presides over what lies outside; nor is any more comprehensive than five, which, as one number, embraces the other eight. It unites the four generating numbers that precede it, thereby making its substance complete; it distributes the four completing numbers that follow it, thereby bringing its functioning to fulfillment. It is truly the meeting point of yin and yang, the source of odd and even. In terms of its position, it presents the image of the ruler; in terms of its virtue, it embodies the meaning of the Ultimate. Thus Yu followed this pattern in ordering the categories, saying: “Establish and employ the August Ultimate.” For the ruler occupies the central and correct position, presiding over the myriad states…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之民則必立中正之德以定萬民之志範圍有
道則上下將爲官焉經緯有章則民物將爲理
焉因人而牖其衷者非要之使從也人不同而
同此心吾惟執此心以協天下而皇極之體立
凡天下之所立者卽此極矣猶之北辰焉其拱
眾星而不與者乎緣物而貞其教者非强之使
合也事不同而同此理吾惟執此理以式天下
而皇極之用行凡天下之所行者卽此極矣猶
之元氣焉其運四時而不流者乎夫是之謂建
===
用皇極而治天下之道尚有加此者哉抑河出
圖而易作洛出書而疇叙皆聖人治世之書也
故易首乾卦疇重建極而聖人之意見矣今觀
賛易者曰首出庶物萬國咸寧又曰天行健君
子以自强不息夫不息者聖人建極之本而萬
國咸寧者其聖人建極之化也歟治天下者當
併觀之
詩
樂只君子邦家之基
punctuated:
之民，則必立中正之德，以定萬民之志。範圍有道，則上下將爲官焉；經緯有章，則民物將爲理焉。因人而牖其衷者，非要之使從也。人不同而同此心，吾惟執此心以協天下，而皇極之體立。凡天下之所立者，卽此極矣。猶之北辰焉，其拱眾星而不與者乎？緣物而貞其教者，非强之使合也。事不同而同此理，吾惟執此理以式天下，而皇極之用行。凡天下之所行者，卽此極矣。猶之元氣焉，其運四時而不流者乎？夫是之謂建用皇極，而治天下之道尚有加此者哉？抑河出圖而易作，洛出書而疇叙，皆聖人治世之書也。故易首乾卦，疇重建極，而聖人之意見矣。今觀賛易者曰：「首出庶物，萬國咸寧。」又曰：「天行健，君子以自强不息。」夫不息者，聖人建極之本；而萬國咸寧者，其聖人建極之化也歟？治天下者，當併觀之。

詩
樂只君子，邦家之基。
translation_en:
…the people, he must establish the virtue of centrality and correctness, so as to settle the aspirations of all the people. When he sets bounds according to the Way, those above and below will be duly governed [?]; when he orders affairs according to proper patterns, people and things will be brought into order. To guide people according to their nature and enlighten their innermost hearts is not to compel their obedience. People differ, yet share this same heart. I need only hold fast to this heart to bring harmony to all under Heaven, and the substance of the august standard is established. Everything established throughout the world rests upon this standard. Is it not like the Pole Star, which gathers the other stars about it without itself taking part in their movements?

To accord with things and make one's teaching correct is not to force them into conformity. Affairs differ, yet share this same principle. I need only hold fast to this principle to provide a model for all under Heaven, and the operation of the august standard is put into effect. Everything practiced throughout the world follows this standard. Is it not like primordial vital energy, which moves the four seasons without itself drifting along with them? This is what is meant by “establishing and employing the august standard.” Could any way of governing all under Heaven surpass this?

Moreover, the Yellow River brought forth the Diagram, and the Changes was composed; the Luo River brought forth the Writing, and the Categories were arranged. Both are writings through which sages govern the world. Thus the Changes begins with the Qian hexagram, and the Categories place weight upon establishing the standard: herein the sages’ intention becomes manifest. Now consider what the commentary praising the Changes says: “It emerges foremost among the myriad things, and the myriad states are all at peace.” It also says: “Heaven moves with vigor; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without ceasing.” Is not this unceasing effort the foundation upon which the sage establishes the standard, and the peace of the myriad states the transforming influence of his establishment of that standard? Those who govern all under Heaven should consider these together.

Book of Odes

“Joyful is the gentleman, the foundation of the state and its ruling house.”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王燾
同考試官教諭蔡批此題全重基字樂只為
輕獨此作精明可錄
同考試官教諭石批作者多以此二句分盛
德大業殊悖此篇最得其旨且文又足以發之
考試官教諭陳批精緻
考試官學正陳批文有藻思
詩人言嘉賓為國之基所以美其德也甚矣賢
者有益于人國也嘉賓而為國之基則其德為
===
可知矣宜詩人道達主人之意以美之也歟南
山有臺之詩亦燕饗賓客而歌之也故其辭曰
樂只君子萃我賓筵有儀有德即其美則溫然
而可愛也令聞令望見其善則欣然而可欲也
其誠邦家之基矣乎蓋邦不自理也必資德人
以培植其元國不自治也必賴仁賢以奠麗其
始今我君子藹藹而為王之使也吾知志業顯
而翼勵明保治之良圖于此乎建濟濟而利王
之用也吾知謀猷闡而位事恪熙載之茂績于
punctuated:
王燾

同考試官教諭蔡批：此題全重基字，樂只為輕，獨此作精明可錄。

同考試官教諭石批：作者多以此二句分盛德大業，殊悖。此篇最得其旨，且文又足以發之。

考試官教諭陳批：精緻。

考試官學正陳批：文有藻思。

詩人言嘉賓為國之基，所以美其德也。甚矣，賢者有益于人國也！嘉賓而為國之基，則其德為可知矣。宜詩人道達主人之意以美之也歟！《南山有臺》之詩，亦燕饗賓客而歌之也。故其辭曰：「樂只君子。」萃我賓筵，有儀有德，即其美則溫然而可愛也；令聞令望，見其善則欣然而可欲也。其誠邦家之基矣乎！蓋邦不自理也，必資德人以培植其元；國不自治也，必賴仁賢以奠麗其始。今我君子，藹藹而為王之使也，吾知志業顯而翼勵明保，治之良圖于此乎建；濟濟而利王之用也，吾知謀猷闡而位事恪，熙載之茂績于
translation_en:
Wang Tao 王燾

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: This topic places its entire emphasis on the word “foundation”; “joyful” carries less weight. This composition alone is discerning and clear, and merits inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: Most writers divide these two lines between “flourishing virtue” and “great achievements,” which seriously misconstrues them. This essay best grasps their meaning, and its writing is fully adequate to bring that meaning out.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Refined and precise.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: The writing displays literary elegance and imagination.

The poet says that the honored guests are the foundation of the state in order to praise their virtue. How greatly worthy men benefit a state! If honored guests constitute its foundation, their virtue may thereby be known. Surely it is fitting that the poet should convey the host’s intentions and praise them! The poem “The Southern Mountain Has Terraces” (Nanshan you tai) was likewise sung when guests were entertained at a banquet. Thus its words say: “Joyful are the gentlemen.” Gathered at our banquet for guests, they possess both dignified bearing and virtue: approaching their excellence, one finds them warm and worthy of affection. With their fine reputations and high standing, they inspire delight in those who see their goodness and a desire to emulate it. Are they not truly the foundation of the state?

For a realm does not order itself: it must draw upon men of virtue to nurture its roots. A state does not govern itself: it must rely upon the humane and worthy to establish its beginnings firmly. Now our gentlemen, numerous and imposing, serve as the king’s emissaries. I know that their aspirations and accomplishments will become manifest and that they will offer assistance, encouragement, enlightened protection [?]; sound plans for governance will be established through them. Dignified and accomplished, they serve the king’s purposes. I know that their plans will be brought to light and that they will discharge the duties of their offices with reverence; splendid achievements in making all endeavors flourish will …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
此乎隆爲上爲德則賛皇猷而永天命有以措
宗社于泰山之安爲下爲民則惠中國而綏四
方有以鞏邦家于磐石之固譬之地乎其體博
厚而承載之無窮也譬之築乎其本堅固而墉
垣之攸墅也謂之曰邦家之基豈不信然也哉
吁詩人可謂善道主人尊賓之意而美其德者
矣抑以是而知先王之治未嘗不急于用賢也
既有禮樂敎化以養之又有燕饗誠敬以求之
宜天保治內采薇治外菁莪樂育棫樸效用而
===
周道煕隆景祚長盛有繇然也故孔子刪詩取
鹿鳴魚麗之什爲小雅之正得非著先王之治
所繇起云
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祇
金淛
同考試官敎諭李 批 聖敬本無積累之漸而
意則相續是義能發其蘊
同考試官敎諭石 批 此題意本聯屬但措詞
最易重疊精切典雅無踰此篇
punctuated:
此乎隆。爲上爲德，則賛皇猷而永天命，有以措宗社于泰山之安；爲下爲民，則惠中國而綏四方，有以鞏邦家于磐石之固。譬之地乎，其體博厚而承載之無窮也；譬之築乎，其本堅固而墉垣之攸墅也。謂之曰邦家之基，豈不信然也哉！吁！詩人可謂善道主人尊賓之意而美其德者矣。抑以是而知先王之治，未嘗不急于用賢也。既有禮樂敎化以養之，又有燕饗誠敬以求之。宜《天保》治內，《采薇》治外，《菁莪》樂育，《棫樸》效用，而周道煕隆，景祚長盛，有繇然也。故孔子刪詩，取《鹿鳴》《魚麗》之什爲《小雅》之正，得非著先王之治所繇起云？
聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祇。
金淛
同考試官敎諭李批：聖敬本無積累之漸，而意則相續，是義能發其蘊。
同考試官敎諭石批：此題意本聯屬，但措詞最易重疊，精切典雅，無踰此篇。
translation_en:
…here flourish. In serving those above and advancing virtue, they assist imperial plans and perpetuate Heaven’s mandate, thereby placing the ancestral temples and altars of state in security like that of Mount Tai. In serving those below and benefiting the people, they bestow blessings upon the central realm and pacify the four quarters, thereby making the state as firm as a great rock. Compare them to the earth: its substance is broad and deep, and its capacity to bear things is inexhaustible. Compare them to a building: its foundation is firm, and upon it the walls are established [?]. Is it not truly fitting to call them the foundation of the state?
Ah! The poet may indeed be said to have skillfully expressed the host’s intention to honor his guests and to have praised their virtue. From this we also know that the government of the former kings never failed to give urgency to employing worthy men. They nurtured them through ritual, music, instruction, and moral transformation, and sought them out through banquets offered with sincerity and reverence. Thus, fittingly, “Heaven Protects” (Tian bao) concerns ordering affairs within, “Gathering Bracken” (Cai wei) ordering affairs without, “Luxuriant Mugwort” (Jing e) delight in nurturing talent, and “Oak and Thorn” (Yu pu) putting talent to use. There was thus a reason why the Way of Zhou flourished so splendidly and its great dynastic blessings long endured. When Confucius edited the Book of Odes, he therefore selected the groups headed by “Deer Calling” (Lu ming) and “Fish in the Weir” (Yu li) as the orthodox Lesser Odes. Was this not to make manifest the origins of the former kings’ good government?
“His sagely reverence rose daily; his radiant influence reached far and wide; he revered the Lord on High.”
Jin Zhe 金淛
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Sagely reverence fundamentally has no gradual process of accumulation, yet the ideas here form a continuous sequence. This essay can bring out their underlying meaning.
Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: The ideas in this topic are inherently connected, but the wording is especially liable to repetition. For precision, aptness, classical refinement, and elegance, no essay surpasses this one.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭陳批敬德之旨明盡
考試官學正陳批琅然可誦
聖人敬德之至一惟純乎天而已矣夫德莫大
于敬天而成湯以之此所以爲聖德之至也歟
商人禘祭而歌之如此蓋謂人知王業集于湯
而不知天命本于德是故當上帝不違之時適
聖祖有作之際則懋昭厥德而昧爽丕顯之惟
寅顧諟明命而夙夜愼脩之匪懈不邇不殖亹
亹乎利欲之防者無時而弗然也制事制心存
===
===
存乎道義之門者與日而俱升也以至精誠之
極明格于皇天而懋哉之念一允懷而不忘敬
明之德昭通于上帝而肅若之心一悠久而不
息惟曰天監有赫一念不謹或以貽終身之憂
故乾乾奉若猶懼有失而吾豈敢以不敬耶帝
命有嚴一日不謹或以貽庶事之害故勉勉欽
承猶懼有間而吾豈敢以或怠耶克綏厥猷惟
皇天之時憲也欽崇天道惟上帝之是祗也夫
湯之聖敬如此則有以合德于天矣此其所以
punctuated:
考試官教諭陳批：敬德之旨明盡。
考試官學正陳批：琅然可誦。
聖人敬德之至，一惟純乎天而已矣。夫德莫大于敬天，而成湯以之，此所以爲聖德之至也歟！商人禘祭而歌之如此，蓋謂人知王業集于湯，而不知天命本于德。是故當上帝不違之時，適聖祖有作之際，則懋昭厥德，而昧爽丕顯之惟寅；顧諟明命，而夙夜愼脩之匪懈。不邇不殖，亹亹乎利欲之防者，無時而弗然也；制事制心，存存乎道義之門者，與日而俱升也。以至精誠之極，明格于皇天，而懋哉之念，一允懷而不忘；敬明之德，昭通于上帝，而肅若之心，一悠久而不息。惟曰：天監有赫，一念不謹，或以貽終身之憂，故乾乾奉若，猶懼有失，而吾豈敢以不敬耶？帝命有嚴，一日不謹，或以貽庶事之害，故勉勉欽承，猶懼有間，而吾豈敢以或怠耶？克綏厥猷，惟皇天之時憲也；欽崇天道，惟上帝之是祗也。夫湯之聖敬如此，則有以合德于天矣。此其所以
translation_en:
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The purport of reverent virtue is explained clearly and fully.”
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Sonorous and worthy of recitation.”
The utmost attainment of the sage’s reverent virtue consists solely in being wholly in accord with Heaven. No virtue is greater than reverence for Heaven, and Cheng Tang practiced it. Is this not what made his sagely virtue supreme? Thus the people of Shang sang of him at the di ancestral sacrifice. Their meaning was that people knew that the royal enterprise came to fruition under Tang, but did not know that Heaven’s Mandate was rooted in virtue. Thus, when the Lord on High did not oppose him, precisely when the sagely ancestor arose, he diligently manifested his virtue: from the first light of dawn, he made it shine forth in reverence. He kept the luminous Mandate constantly before him, cultivating himself carefully morning and night without slackening. He neither drew near to nor fostered [the pursuit of wealth and sensual pleasure]; there was no moment when he did not labor diligently to guard against profit and desire. He regulated affairs and regulated his mind, continually abiding at the gateway of the Way and righteousness, advancing with each passing day. His consummate sincerity reached its utmost, ascending luminously to August Heaven, while the resolve to be diligent remained steadfastly in his heart, never forgotten. His reverent and luminous virtue reached through to the Lord on High, while his solemn, obedient heart remained constant and unceasing.
His thought was simply this: “Heaven’s scrutiny is awe-inspiring. A single unguarded thought might leave me with lifelong sorrow. Thus I diligently serve and obey, still fearing that I may fall short. How could I dare be irreverent? The Lord’s command is stern. A single day without care might bring harm to the many affairs of government. Thus I strive to receive it reverently, still fearing an interruption in my efforts. How could I dare slacken at all?” His ability to establish his course securely consisted in taking August Heaven as his model; his reverent exaltation of Heaven’s Way consisted in honoring the Lord on High. Such was Tang’s sagely reverence, and through it he could bring his virtue into accord with Heaven. This was how he …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
受命而成王業也歟抑以是而知帝王之受天
命未嘗不本于敬也故堯之授舜舜之授禹禹
之傳湯湯之傳文武者皆是道也桀紂幽厲不
繇也故天命之去留靡常而曆數之歸于有德
則一而已矣然則有天下者豈可以不敬哉商
人大禘升歌祖德推本受命之祥與其格天之
敬而竝及其保衡佐時之士其用意亦淵矣乎
春秋
春正月公狩于郎桓公四年
===
王宗沐

受命而成王業也歟？抑以是而知帝王之受天命，未嘗不本于敬也。故堯之授舜，舜之授禹，禹之傳湯，湯之傳文武者，皆是道也。桀紂幽厲不繇也，故天命之去留靡常，而曆數之歸于有德，則一而已矣。然則有天下者，豈可以不敬哉？商人大禘，升歌祖德，推本受命之祥與其格天之敬，而竝及其保衡佐時之士，其用意亦淵矣乎！

…was this not why he received the Mandate and established his royal enterprise? From this, moreover, we know that emperors and kings have invariably received Heaven’s Mandate on the basis of reverence. Thus Yao’s conferral upon Shun, Shun’s conferral upon Yu, Yu’s transmission to Tang, and Tang’s transmission to Wen and Wu all followed this Way. Jie, Zhou, You, and Li did not follow it. Thus Heaven’s Mandate is inconstant in departing or remaining, yet the allotted succession invariably falls to those possessing virtue. How, then, could those who possess all under Heaven fail to be reverent? At the great di sacrifice, the people of Shang ascended the hall to sing of their ancestor’s virtue, tracing back the auspicious signs of his receiving the Mandate and the reverence through which he reached Heaven. They also included his Protector and Rectifier, the worthy man who assisted him in his age. How profound their intention was!

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
桓四年之春乃有于郎之狩何獨見譏於春秋
誠以先王於四時之隙以講武必度閒曠之地
以為囿物有恒植無暴殄焉民有寧宇無淫虐
焉今魯之狩也則既有大野矣不於大野而於
郎郎何地耶疆場之所固非閒曠之區矣而必
於此狩焉馳騖於稼穡場圃之中物之罹害也
必甚蕩廢其耕作經營之業民之被擾也何堪
公豈不謂用民以訓軍旅非遠出無以示威歟
殊不知田不踰郊古之制也耀疆場之武以貽
===
閭井之戚先王所以威天下者固如是乎抑豈
不謂取物以祭宗廟非遠出無以多獲歟殊不
知追不踰防古之制也侈籩豆之實以空田野
之資先王所以順天下者固如是乎夫物失其
利則財用匱民匱於財則怨聲作將有聞車馬
之音見羽旄之美舉疾首蹙頞而相告者亦其
勢所必至矣聖人於此有感焉若曰民胞物與
王者仁愛之德也事必始於微而後著德必謹
於微而後全故常事不書而此特書之者欲人
punctuated: 桓四年之春，乃有于郎之狩，何獨見譏於春秋？誠以先王於四時之隙以講武，必度閒曠之地以為囿，物有恒植，無暴殄焉；民有寧宇，無淫虐焉。今魯之狩也，則既有大野矣，不於大野而於郎。郎何地耶？疆場之所，固非閒曠之區矣，而必於此狩焉。馳騖於稼穡場圃之中，物之罹害也必甚；蕩廢其耕作經營之業，民之被擾也何堪！公豈不謂用民以訓軍旅，非遠出無以示威歟？殊不知田不踰郊，古之制也。耀疆場之武，以貽閭井之戚，先王所以威天下者，固如是乎？抑豈不謂取物以祭宗廟，非遠出無以多獲歟？殊不知追不踰防，古之制也。侈籩豆之實，以空田野之資，先王所以順天下者，固如是乎？夫物失其利，則財用匱；民匱於財，則怨聲作。將有聞車馬之音，見羽旄之美，舉疾首蹙頞而相告者，亦其勢所必至矣。聖人於此有感焉，若曰：「民胞物與，王者仁愛之德也。事必始於微而後著，德必謹於微而後全。」故常事不書，而此特書之者，欲人
translation_en:
…in the spring of Duke Huan’s fourth year, there was a hunt at Lang. Why was this alone censured in the Spring and Autumn Annals? It was precisely because, when the former kings conducted military exercises during intervals of leisure in the four seasons, they invariably selected unoccupied, open ground for hunting preserves. Living things could grow steadily, without reckless destruction; the people had peaceful dwellings, without excessive oppression. Now Lu already had Daye as a hunting ground, yet the hunt took place not at Daye but at Lang. What sort of place was Lang? It was frontier territory, certainly no unoccupied, open tract; yet the duke insisted on hunting there. Galloping through crops, threshing grounds, and gardens was bound to inflict severe harm on living things. Disrupting and laying waste the people’s work of cultivation and livelihood—how could they bear such disturbance?

Did the duke perhaps think that, in employing the people to train his troops, he could not display his might without venturing far afield? He failed to understand that the ancient rule was that hunting should not extend beyond the suburbs. To flaunt military might on the frontier and thereby bring distress upon the villages—was this really how the former kings awed the world? Or did he perhaps think that, in taking game to offer in the ancestral temple, he could not obtain a large catch without venturing far afield? He failed to understand that the ancient rule was that pursuit should not pass beyond the embankments. To make lavish the contents of sacrificial baskets and dishes while exhausting the resources of the fields—was this really how the former kings brought harmony to the world?

When living things lose the conditions that sustain them, material resources become scarce; when the people lack resources, voices of resentment arise. There would surely come a time when, hearing the sound of chariots and horses and seeing the splendor of feathered and yak-tail banners, they would all complain to one another with aching heads and furrowed brows. This was the inevitable outcome of such circumstances. The Sage was moved by this, as if to say: “To regard the people as siblings and living things as companions is the virtue of benevolent love proper to a true king. Affairs necessarily begin in small things before becoming conspicuous; virtue must be guarded in small things before it becomes complete.” Thus ordinary events were not recorded, but this one was specially recorded out of a desire that…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
君謹德於微而不可使之至於著而不可救也
其爲君道計何如哉雖然行道有序要必自親
親爲之始莫親於兄鍾巫之變桓且忍而甘心
焉則何有於民物而春秋顧以王德責之何歟
曰春秋爲萬世扶人紀而作其義公於天下而
非私於一魯也不然指斬關之盜而問其穿窬
春秋輕重之權衡不如是也是故狩郎之書聖
人爲萬世有民物之責者示謹於魯桓乎何誅
春王正月公會王人齊侯宋公衛侯許男
===
曹伯陳世子款盟于洮〔僖公八年〕夏公
會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男曹
伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕
鄧棟
同考試官教諭鄭批講春秋尊王謹臣大義
似易寔難場中多失之泛而俗會傳明白而措詞
老健獨見此篇矣錄之
考試官教諭陳批精確
考試官學正陳批書法不隱
punctuated:
君謹德於微，而不可使之至於著而不可救也。其爲君道計何如哉！雖然，行道有序，要必自親親爲之始。莫親於兄，鍾巫之變，桓且忍而甘心焉，則何有於民物？而《春秋》顧以王德責之，何歟？曰：《春秋》爲萬世扶人紀而作，其義公於天下，而非私於一魯也。不然，指斬關之盜而問其穿窬，《春秋》輕重之權衡不如是也。是故狩郎之書，聖人爲萬世有民物之責者示謹，於魯桓乎何誅？
春，王正月，公會王人、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、許男、曹伯、陳世子款，盟于洮。〔僖公八年〕夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕
鄧棟

考試官教諭陳批：精確。
考試官學正陳批：書法不隱。
translation_en:
…the ruler to attend carefully to his virtue in its slightest manifestations, rather than allow matters to become conspicuous and beyond remedy. How profound is this concern for the way of rulership! Nevertheless, putting the Way into practice has an order: it must begin with affection for one’s kin. No one is closer than an elder brother; yet in the Zhongwu affair, Duke Huan could bear what was done and willingly accept it. What concern, then, could he have for the people and other living things? Why, nevertheless, does the Spring and Autumn Annals hold him accountable to kingly virtue? The answer is that the Spring and Autumn Annals was written to uphold human relationships for ten thousand generations. Its principles apply impartially to all under Heaven, rather than concern Lu alone. Otherwise, this would be like pointing to a robber who hacks through gates and questioning him about slipping through a hole in a wall. Such is not the Spring and Autumn Annals’ weighing of greater and lesser offenses. Thus, in recording the hunt at Lang, the Sage enjoins vigilance upon all those in every age who bear responsibility for the people and other living things. What particular censure of Duke Huan of Lu is intended?
In spring, in the first month of the king’s calendar, the duke met with the king’s representative, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, heir apparent of Chen, and they made a covenant at Tao. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xi〕 In summer, the duke met with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi〕
Deng Dong.

Most essays in this examination fall into generalities and commonplace expressions. Only in this essay have I seen a lucid synthesis of the commentaries combined with mature and vigorous wording. Select it.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Precise and exact.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “The principles governing the text’s manner of recording events are made clear.”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋兩紀王臣之與信好有所以尊王命者有
所以謹臣禮者此王人之微得序於諸侯之上
而冢宰三公之貴不得以殊會書聖人於君臣
之際嚴矣且于洮曷為而盟耶齊桓因王人下
會而有是盟也夫內臣莫微於下士王人下士
也而序于諸侯之上何歟蓋一王之靈所以照
四國而風天下者惟命耳是故朝聘會盟之禮
自公卿大夫而下有不得以私交者人臣之義
也彼王人者職在下士則誠微矣然其所將者
===
王命也命出於王則雖以下士之微而奔走在
外之方伯公侯以從事焉亦肅將之義所得為
者孰得而抗之苟以其職任之微而降從班列
之末則將與私自交好如祭伯輩比矣如王命
何噫朝服雖敝必加於上弁冕雖舊必加於首
聖人所以序王人於諸侯之上意如此若葵丘
曷為而會耶齊桓因宰孔下勞而有是會也夫
人臣莫貴於三公宰孔兼三公矣而不以殊會
書何歟蓋人君之尊所以御羣工而勵天下者
punctuated: 春秋兩紀王臣之與信好，有所以尊王命者，有所以謹臣禮者。此王人之微得序於諸侯之上，而冢宰三公之貴不得以殊會書，聖人於君臣之際嚴矣。且于洮曷為而盟耶？齊桓因王人下會而有是盟也。夫內臣莫微於下士，王人下士也，而序于諸侯之上，何歟？蓋一王之靈所以照四國而風天下者，惟命耳。是故朝聘會盟之禮，自公卿大夫而下，有不得以私交者，人臣之義也。彼王人者，職在下士，則誠微矣。然其所將者，王命也。命出於王，則雖以下士之微，而奔走在外之方伯公侯以從事焉，亦肅將之義所得為者，孰得而抗之？苟以其職任之微，而降從班列之末，則將與私自交好如祭伯輩比矣。如王命何？噫！朝服雖敝，必加於上；弁冕雖舊，必加於首。聖人所以序王人於諸侯之上，意如此。若葵丘，曷為而會耶？齊桓因宰孔下勞而有是會也。夫人臣莫貴於三公，宰孔兼三公矣，而不以殊會書，何歟？蓋人君之尊所以御羣工而勵天下者
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals twice records royal ministers participating in pledges of amity [?]: one entry serves to honor the king’s command, and the other to enforce due observance of a minister’s ritual obligations. Thus a low-ranking royal representative could be listed above the regional lords, while even the exalted rank of Grand Steward and Three Dukes did not warrant recording a meeting separately. The Sage was strict indeed concerning the relationship between ruler and minister.

Why, then, was a covenant sworn at Tao? Duke Huan of Qi held this covenant meeting because a royal representative had come down to attend. Among ministers at court, none ranks lower than a junior serviceman. The royal representative was a junior serviceman; why, then, was he listed above the regional lords? It is through commands alone that the august power of the one king illuminates the states in all four quarters and influences all under Heaven. Thus, in the rites of court audience, diplomatic visitation, meeting, and covenant, those from dukes, ministers, and grandees downward may not establish private relations: this is a minister’s duty. That royal representative held the office of junior serviceman and was indeed of low rank. Yet what he bore was the king’s command. Since the command issued from the king, even someone of the low rank of junior serviceman could set the regional chiefs, dukes, and marquises outside the court hastening about to carry out its business. This was permissible under the duty of reverently executing that command. Who could resist him? If, because of his low office, he were demoted to the end of the ranks, he would be put on a par with those such as the Earl of Ji, who established friendly relations on their own authority. What treatment of the king’s command would that be? Ah! Though a court robe be worn, it must be worn on the upper body; though a ceremonial cap or crown be old, it must be worn on the head. Such was the Sage’s intention in listing the royal representative above the regional lords.

As for Kuiqiu, why was a meeting held there? Duke Huan of Qi held this meeting because Zai Kong had come down to convey royal recognition of his services. Among ministers, none ranks higher than the Three Dukes. Zai Kong also held the dignity of the Three Dukes; why, then, was his meeting not recorded separately? For that whereby the ruler’s exalted authority governs the assembled officials and spurs all under Heaven to exert themselves …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
惟爵耳是故進退出入之節雖冢宰三公之貴
有不得以常尊者人臣之分也彼宰孔者貴兼
三公則誠尊矣然其所貴者王爵也爵出於王
則雖以冢宰三公之貴而出從在外之方伯諸
侯以服政焉亦均勞之義所當然者誰得而違
之苟以其職任之重而遽從殊會之文則將與
貴有常尊如王世子比矣如臣禮何噫天尊地
卑而其分定典敘禮秩而其義明聖人所以列
序宰周公於諸侯之上而不殊會之者意如此
===
由是觀之則知春秋尊君抑臣之旨矣謂春秋
爲道名分而作有以夫抑吾於是而知齊桓戴
周之功爲大也維時下陵上替內弱外強天下
何時而重以王室之內釁耶齊桓奉襄之勤將
庶幾乎南門逆釗之義矣襄王賜胙之禮其亦
庶幾于賜履專征之烈歟卒也服楚之後志驕
德衰桓之不能進於王可惜也夫
禮記
夫禮先王以承天之道以治人之情
punctuated:
惟爵耳。是故進退出入之節，雖冢宰三公之貴，有不得以常尊者，人臣之分也。彼宰孔者，貴兼三公，則誠尊矣；然其所貴者，王爵也。爵出於王，則雖以冢宰三公之貴，而出從在外之方伯諸侯以服政焉，亦均勞之義所當然者，誰得而違之？苟以其職任之重而遽從殊會之文，則將與貴有常尊如王世子比矣，如臣禮何？噫！天尊地卑而其分定，典敘禮秩而其義明。聖人所以列序宰周公於諸侯之上而不殊會之者，意如此。由是觀之，則知《春秋》尊君抑臣之旨矣。謂《春秋》爲道名分而作，有以夫！抑吾於是而知齊桓戴周之功爲大也。維時下陵上替，內弱外強，天下何時，而重以王室之內釁耶？齊桓奉襄之勤，將庶幾乎南門逆釗之義矣。襄王賜胙之禮，其亦庶幾于賜履專征之烈歟？卒也，服楚之後，志驕德衰，桓之不能進於王，可惜也夫！

禮記

夫禮，先王以承天之道，以治人之情。
translation_en:
…is rank alone. Thus, in the rules governing advancement and retirement, entry into and departure from office, even those holding the exalted positions of Grand Steward or Three Dukes cannot invariably claim precedence: such is the station of a subject. Zai Kong, whose eminence encompassed that of the Three Dukes, was indeed honored. Yet what conferred that eminence was rank granted by the king. Since rank proceeds from the king, even one as exalted as the Grand Steward or the Three Dukes, when going out to join regional overlords and feudal lords in performing governmental duties, must act according to the principle of sharing the burden of service. Who could depart from it? If, merely because of the weight of his office, the text were immediately to distinguish his participation in the meeting, he would be placed alongside those whose rank carries constant precedence, such as the king’s heir apparent. What would become of the ritual obligations of a subject? Ah! Heaven is exalted and earth lowly, and their stations are fixed; established norms provide order and ritual provides gradation, making the proper principles clear. Such was the Sage’s intention in listing the Duke of Zhou, serving as Grand Steward, above the feudal lords without separately distinguishing his participation in the meeting.

Viewed in this light, the purpose of the Spring and Autumn Annals in exalting rulers and restraining subjects becomes clear. There is indeed reason to say that the Spring and Autumn Annals was written to expound the distinctions of title and station! Moreover, from this I recognize the greatness of Duke Huan of Qi’s achievement in upholding Zhou. At that time, inferiors encroached upon superiors, while those above neglected their duties; the royal center was weak and the outlying states strong. What a time it was for the realm—and must internal strife in the royal house compound its troubles? Duke Huan of Qi’s diligent support of King Xiang came close to the righteousness shown in welcoming Zhao at the southern gate. Did King Xiang’s ritual bestowal of sacrificial meat upon him likewise approach the illustrious precedent of granting territory and authority to conduct punitive campaigns independently? In the end, after bringing Chu to submission, his ambitions grew arrogant and his virtue declined. That Duke Huan could not advance to true kingship is indeed regrettable!

Record of Rites

As for ritual, the former kings used it to accord with the Way of Heaven and to regulate human feelings.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
邵章
同考試官教諭鄭批禮有關於天人所以爲
急此作能於承治處說最明快獨超諸卷子亦可
謂達禮之本矣
考試官教諭陳批理明詞暢
考試官學正陳批整潔
先王之禮法天道而立人極者也夫天道者禮
制之原也先王法之而人極立焉禮其可以已
乎哉禮運記聖人答言偃之意若謂天下之道
===
同歸而禮之用爲急是禮也固衆之紀也治之
準也而天下後世所共由者也然豈先王作而
致其情哉蓋天道有自然之序禮制於是乎肇
矣先王有以承之智周玄微成能於效法之下
而中正之矩立情通幽遠盡道於範圍之餘而
辨異之典成探造化之蘊以敦其叙也冥會默
契有若命之而奉順惟謹焉達神明之德以庸
其秩也仰窺俯察若有授之而欽若弗違焉蓋
天道妙而難知著之節文而爲禮則顯而可行
punctuated:
邵章

同考試官教諭鄭批：禮有關於天人，所以爲急。此作能於承治處說最明快，獨超諸卷子，亦可謂達禮之本矣。
考試官教諭陳批：理明詞暢。
考試官學正陳批：整潔。

先王之禮，法天道而立人極者也。夫天道者，禮制之原也。先王法之，而人極立焉，禮其可以已乎哉？《禮運》記聖人答言偃之意，若謂天下之道同歸，而禮之用爲急。是禮也，固衆之紀也，治之準也，而天下後世所共由者也。然豈先王作而致其情哉？蓋天道有自然之序，禮制於是乎肇矣。先王有以承之，智周玄微，成能於效法之下，而中正之矩立；情通幽遠，盡道於範圍之餘，而辨異之典成。探造化之蘊以敦其叙也，冥會默契，有若命之而奉順惟謹焉；達神明之德以庸其秩也，仰窺俯察，若有授之而欽若弗違焉。蓋天道妙而難知，著之節文而爲禮，則顯而可行
translation_en:
Shao Zhang

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, an Instructor: “Ritual concerns Heaven and humankind, which is why it is of urgent importance. This composition explains with exceptional clarity and vigor the points about receiving Heaven’s Way and governing human feelings. It stands above all the other papers; its author may indeed be said to understand the foundation of ritual.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, an Instructor: “Clear reasoning and fluent expression.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, a School Director: “Orderly and polished.”

The ritual of the former kings took Heaven’s Way as its model and established the supreme standard for humankind. Heaven’s Way is the source of ritual institutions. The former kings modeled themselves upon it, and thereby the supreme human standard was established. How, then, could ritual be dispensed with? The “Evolution of Ritual” chapter records the sage’s response to Yan Yan. Its meaning seems to be that all the ways of the world converge upon the same end, but the application of ritual is most urgent. Ritual is indeed the organizing principle of the multitude, the standard of government, and the common path followed throughout the world and by later generations. Yet could it have been something the former kings created simply to give expression to their own feelings?

Heaven’s Way possesses a spontaneous order, and ritual institutions originate therein. The former kings had the means to receive and uphold it. Their wisdom encompassed the profound and subtle; through emulation they perfected their capacities, and the standard of centrality and correctness was established. Their feelings reached into the hidden and remote; through comprehensively ordering things they fully realized the Way, and the institutions distinguishing differences were completed. They probed the hidden workings of creation and transformation to give substance to its proper sequence. In profound understanding and silent accord, they acted as though commanded, obeying with the utmost care. They comprehended the potency of spiritual illumination so as to put its ordered ranks into practice. Looking upward and examining below, they acted as though receiving instructions, reverently conforming without deviation. For Heaven’s Way is subtle and difficult to know; when manifested in the graded forms and patterned observances that constitute ritual, it becomes evident and practicable…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣是則所謂承天之道也豈非爲人極而立哉
蓋人情有難制之欲變僞由此而生矣先王有
以治之觀會通以作則使感物而動者有所防
焉而不流陳藝極以建中俾應感而通者有所
理焉而不亂天敘之典顯而爲世變之綱維則
發皆中節而達道以行無有滅理而窮欲者矣
天理之秩闡而爲人事之儀則殆思必無邪而
彝敎允修無復情蕩而性鑿者矣蓋人情隱而
難測範之禮度而有制則一而可齊矣是則所
===
以治人情者豈不本天道而興哉夫天道至敎
因禮以示人聖人至德由禮以立敎其達天人
之際要非無因而强作者也禮之所以爲急而
三代之英所以必致謹者歟抑禮本諸天道而
寔出於人情蓋先王因而節文之以治乎人情
者此所以達之天下而無間也今考之先王冠
婚喪祭射御朝聘之儀歷萬世而無弊則夫子
所謂損益可知者不過其末節而大義則古今
不易也後世徒爲綿蕞野外之儀及知稽古禮
punctuated:
矣。是則所謂承天之道也，豈非爲人極而立哉？蓋人情有難制之欲，變僞由此而生矣。先王有以治之，觀會通以作則，使感物而動者有所防焉而不流；陳藝極以建中，俾應感而通者有所理焉而不亂。天敘之典顯而爲世變之綱維，則發皆中節而達道以行，無有滅理而窮欲者矣。天理之秩闡而爲人事之儀則，殆思必無邪而彝敎允修，無復情蕩而性鑿者矣。蓋人情隱而難測，範之禮度而有制，則一而可齊矣。是則所以治人情者，豈不本天道而興哉？
夫天道至敎，因禮以示人；聖人至德，由禮以立敎。其達天人之際，要非無因而强作者也。禮之所以爲急，而三代之英所以必致謹者歟！抑禮本諸天道，而寔出於人情。蓋先王因而節文之，以治乎人情者，此所以達之天下而無間也。
今考之先王冠婚喪祭、射御朝聘之儀，歷萬世而無弊，則夫子所謂損益可知者，不過其末節，而大義則古今不易也。後世徒爲綿蕞野外之儀，及知稽古禮
translation_en:
…Such is what is meant by following the Way of Heaven. Was this not established to provide the ultimate standard for humanity? Human feelings contain desires that are difficult to restrain, and aberration and deceit arise from them. The former kings had means of governing these: they observed how things converge and interconnect to establish rules, so that feelings stirred by external things would have safeguards and would not run unchecked. They set forth standards of conduct to establish the mean, so that responses to external stimuli would be ordered and would not fall into confusion. When the institutions embodying Heaven’s ordering become manifest and serve as the guiding framework amid changes in the world, every expression of feeling accords with its proper measure, and the universally applicable Way prevails. None then extinguishes principle in the pursuit of desire to its utmost. When the ordered distinctions of heavenly principle are elucidated and become standards for human affairs, thoughts will surely be without depravity and the constant teachings will truly be cultivated. No longer will feelings run wild and one’s nature be mutilated. Human feelings are hidden and difficult to fathom, but when shaped and restrained by ritual standards, they become unified and can be brought into harmony. How, then, could the means of governing human feelings arise without being rooted in the Way of Heaven?
The supreme teaching of the Way of Heaven is shown to people through ritual; through ritual, the supreme virtue of the sages establishes instruction. In connecting Heaven and humanity, ritual is certainly not something arbitrarily contrived without a basis. Is this not why ritual is an urgent concern, and why the outstanding rulers of the Three Dynasties invariably attended to it with such care? Moreover, ritual is rooted in the Way of Heaven, yet truly emerges from human feelings. The former kings followed these feelings and gave them measured expression in order to govern them. This is why ritual can extend throughout the world without obstruction.
If we now examine the former kings’ ceremonies of capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, archery, charioteering, court audiences, and diplomatic visits, they endure for ten thousand generations without becoming defective. Thus, what the Master meant when he said that additions and omissions could be known concerns only minor details; the fundamental principles remain unchanged from antiquity to the present. Later generations merely performed ceremonies in the open country using cords and bundles of reeds as markers; and those who knew how to investigate ancient ritual [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文者又惟事乎儀文度數之末先王之禮意不
傳于天下久矣噫豈其未聞性與天道者乎
四暢交於中而發作於外
祝世廉
同考試官教諭鄭批此題作者多為牽引上
文所累獨此篇承上簡當中間詞氣充暢善發中
外相因之妙殆深於樂者乎錄之
考試官教諭陳批平正愨實
考試官學正陳批文足表義
===
記者著和氣妙于中外見樂之所感者深也蓋
樂者天人之至理也和氣積中發外樂之所感
不旣深乎記樂記者以為先王本人情以作樂
夫旣立本而備文矣則其感化之妙當何如哉
是故天地之氣曰陰與陽樂以合之而不散不
密也則摩蕩之機雖隱而未顯而天地之中藹
然動靜之各得焉人心之德曰剛與柔樂以道
之而不怒不懾也則真純之懿雖微而未著而
人心之中粹然和平之浹洽焉太和元氣歡欣
punctuated:
文者，又惟事乎儀文度數之末，先王之禮意不傳于天下久矣。噫！豈其未聞性與天道者乎？

四暢交於中而發作於外
祝世廉

同考試官教諭鄭批：此題作者多為牽引上文所累，獨此篇承上簡當，中間詞氣充暢，善發中外相因之妙，殆深於樂者乎？錄之。
考試官教諭陳批：平正愨實。
考試官學正陳批：文足表義。

記者著和氣妙于中外，見樂之所感者深也。蓋樂者，天人之至理也。和氣積中發外，樂之所感不旣深乎？記樂記者以為先王本人情以作樂，夫旣立本而備文矣，則其感化之妙當何如哉？是故天地之氣曰陰與陽，樂以合之，而不散不密也，則摩蕩之機雖隱而未顯，而天地之中藹然動靜之各得焉。人心之德曰剛與柔，樂以道之，而不怒不懾也，則真純之懿雖微而未著，而人心之中粹然和平之浹洽焉。太和元氣歡欣
translation_en:
…those versed in the forms of ancient ritual, in turn, concern themselves only with the minutiae of ceremonial forms, measures, and numbers. The intent underlying the former kings’ rites has long ceased to be transmitted throughout the world. Alas! Can it be that they have not heard of human nature and the Way of Heaven?

“The four flow freely and mingle within, then manifest themselves without.”
Zhu Shilian

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor (jiaoyu): Most writers on this topic are encumbered by drawing in the preceding passage. This essay alone connects with it concisely and aptly. Throughout its central portion, the language and spirit are full and fluent, effectively revealing the subtle way in which the internal and external depend upon one another. Surely its author has a profound understanding of music! Selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor (jiaoyu): Balanced and correct, sincere and substantial.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor (xuezheng): The writing adequately expresses the meaning.

The recorder sets forth the subtle workings of harmonious qi within and without, showing how profound music’s influence is. For music embodies the ultimate principle of Heaven and humanity. Harmonious qi accumulates within and issues forth without: is music’s influence not indeed profound? The author of the Record of Music holds that the former kings based their creation of music on human feelings. Once they had established its foundation and fully provided its outward forms, how marvelous must its transforming influence have been!

Thus, the qi of Heaven and Earth are called yin and yang. Music brings them into accord, so that they are neither dispersed nor confined. Although the workings of their mutual interaction remain hidden and not yet manifest, within Heaven and Earth there is an abundant harmony in which movement and stillness each find their proper place. The qualities of the human heart are called firmness and softness. Music guides them, so that they are neither angry nor fearful. Although the excellence of their genuineness and purity remains subtle and not yet apparent, within the human heart harmony and peace thoroughly suffuse everything in their purity. The primordial qi of supreme harmony rejoices…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而交通合一不測也生生之原已在矣天性至
德順暢而不乖寂然不動也天下之本已敦矣
由是充積之理旣盛則發達之妙自章化工由
隱以之顯陰陽迭運而所以普美利于無方者
自爾成象而可見天機由微以至著剛柔相濟
而所以神變通于不窮者自爾時出而有徵推
行有漸達夫合一之神而仁厚嚴凝以致天下
之和者一陰陽化醇之迹也蓋化不可測者矣
泛應曲當通夫寂然之體而容執敬別以應天
===
下之感者一剛柔效法之能也蓋機不容禦者
矣是知天地人心之和積中發外之妙如此樂
之用大矣先王立學以為敎也宜哉吾於此而
知天氣人心與樂通也蓋其法天和以為體而
合天和以為能本人心以盡制而道人心以盡
神此其機之相協而道之相濟者如此也是故
明備而天地官無聲而天下和君子觀此而可
知本也若夫姦聲溺音則逆氣應之而天人之
和滯矣噫君天下者其尚建中和之極以為作
punctuated: 而交通，合一不測也，生生之原已在矣。天性至德，順暢而不乖，寂然不動也，天下之本已敦矣。由是充積之理旣盛，則發達之妙自章。化工由隱以之顯，陰陽迭運，而所以普美利于無方者，自爾成象而可見。天機由微以至著，剛柔相濟，而所以神變通于不窮者，自爾時出而有徵。推行有漸，達夫合一之神，而仁厚嚴凝以致天下之和者，一陰陽化醇之迹也，蓋化不可測者矣。泛應曲當，通夫寂然之體，而容執敬別以應天下之感者，一剛柔效法之能也，蓋機不容禦者矣。是知天地人心之和，積中發外之妙如此，樂之用大矣。先王立學以為敎也，宜哉！吾於此而知天氣人心與樂通也。蓋其法天和以為體，而合天和以為能；本人心以盡制，而道人心以盡神。此其機之相協，而道之相濟者如此也。是故明備而天地官，無聲而天下和。君子觀此而可知本也。若夫姦聲溺音，則逆氣應之，而天人之和滯矣。噫！君天下者，其尚建中和之極，以為作
translation_en:
…and circulate freely, uniting in unfathomable oneness: the source of ceaseless generation is already present. Innate nature and consummate virtue flow smoothly without discord, remaining still and unmoving: the foundation of all under Heaven is already firmly established. Thus, when the principle accumulated within becomes abundant, the wondrous efficacy of its outward expression naturally becomes manifest. The work of transformation proceeds from concealment to visibility. Yin and yang operate in alternation, and that which spreads blessings and benefits without bounds naturally takes visible form. The workings of Heaven proceed from the subtle to the manifest. Firmness and yielding sustain one another, and that which brings about inexhaustible, wondrous adaptation and transformation naturally emerges at the proper times and provides observable evidence. Advancing by degrees, it realizes the spiritual efficacy of oneness; through benevolent warmth and stern cold, it brings harmony to all under Heaven. These are all traces of yin and yang blending in transformation: transformation is indeed unfathomable. Responding broadly and fitting each particular circumstance, it communicates with the still and unmoving substance; through accommodation, adherence, reverence, and distinction [?], it responds to the impulses of all under Heaven. These are all manifestations of the capacity of firmness and yielding to provide effective patterns: their workings indeed cannot be checked.

From this we know that such is the harmony of Heaven, Earth, and the human heart, and such the wondrous process by which what accumulates within finds expression without. Great indeed is the efficacy of music! How fitting that the former kings established schools to teach it! From this I understand that the vital forces of Heaven and the human heart communicate with music. Music takes the harmony of Heaven as the model for its substance and accords with that harmony in exercising its powers; it grounds itself in the human heart to perfect its forms and guides the human heart to realize its spiritual efficacy fully. Such is the mutual accord of their workings and the mutual support of their ways. Thus, when they are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth perform their appointed functions; without a sound, all under Heaven is harmonious. By observing this, the gentleman can understand the foundation. But when there are depraved sounds and indulgent melodies, contrary vital forces respond to them, and the harmony of Heaven and humanity is obstructed. Ah! May those who rule all under Heaven establish the highest standard of equilibrium and harmony as the foundation for making…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
樂之本哉
第貳場
論
聖人合內外而成其仁
沈束
同考試官教諭王批場中多苦於內外之說
不泛則滯此作明快老成獨超眾見讀之宛然見
聖人氣象宜錄以式
同考試官教諭陳批內外成仁多體貼不真
===
而此作迺能始終發明其義誠傑作也
考試官教諭陳批善發聖人之蘊
考試官學正陳批說合內外處最為明盡
且詞弘而氣昌取之
聖人大公以為德而大同以為化者其達
天矣乎蓋天之於萬物也無弗仁也而萬
物無弗化也故語大德者莫大乎天語大
化者亦莫大乎天聖人神明其德而範圍
其化故其德則大公而無物無我也其化
punctuated:
樂之本哉！

第貳場
論
聖人合內外而成其仁
沈束

同考試官教諭王批：場中多苦於內外之說，不泛則滯。此作明快老成，獨超眾見，讀之宛然見聖人氣象，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭陳批：內外成仁，多體貼不真，而此作迺能始終發明其義，誠傑作也。

考試官教諭陳批：善發聖人之蘊。

考試官學正陳批：說合內外處，最為明盡，且詞弘而氣昌，取之。

聖人大公以為德，而大同以為化者，其達天矣乎！蓋天之於萬物也，無弗仁也，而萬物無弗化也。故語大德者，莫大乎天；語大化者，亦莫大乎天。聖人神明其德，而範圍其化，故其德則大公，而無物無我也；其化
