translation_en:
…the foundation for making music!

Second Session
Discourse
“The Sage Unites the Inner and Outer and Thus Perfects His Benevolence”
By Shen Shu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Candidates in this examination have generally struggled to explain the inner and outer: their accounts are either vague or constricted. This composition is lucid, incisive, and mature, uniquely surpassing the views of the other candidates. Reading it, one seems to behold the bearing of the sage himself. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: In discussing the inner and outer and the perfection of benevolence, most candidates fail to grasp the meaning truly. This composition, however, elucidates its meaning from beginning to end. It is indeed an outstanding work.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: It admirably brings out the sage’s profound meaning.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Director: Its explanation of uniting the inner and outer is exceptionally clear and thorough. Moreover, its language is expansive and its spirit abundant. Accept it.

The sage takes perfect impartiality as his virtue and universal unity as his transforming influence: surely he has attained an understanding of Heaven! For Heaven treats all things with benevolence, and there is nothing that does not undergo its transformation. Thus, when speaking of great virtue, nothing is greater than Heaven; when speaking of great transforming influence, likewise nothing is greater than Heaven. The sage brings numinous clarity to his virtue and comprehensively orders his transforming influence. Thus his virtue is perfectly impartial, admitting no distinction between things and self; his transforming influence…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則大同而無內無外也物我忘內外一德
至盛化至神非至聖之達天其孰能與於
此昔者孔子之志於天下也有曰老者安
之朋友信之少者懷之其天之仁乎其大
德大化乎故張載氏讀而賛之以為聖人
樂天合內外而成其仁蓋亦有見於此矣
易曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天言大德
也乾道變化各正性命保合太和乃利貞
言大化也大德者天之仁也大化者仁之
===
顯也仁則天之生生而不已者也生生而
不已者化化而無窮也故天道顯諸仁藏
諸用鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂聖人則體
天之撰成天之能財成其道而輔相其宜
者也故天道好生聖人亦好生天普萬物
而同仁聖人亦同仁以普天下故天下有
不得其所者則聖人有憂焉矣何也天生
聖人以賛化也聖人大公而應合同而化
以若天也今天地大矣萬物夥矣人民眾
punctuated: 則大同而無內無外也。物我忘，內外一，德至盛，化至神，非至聖之達天，其孰能與於此？昔者孔子之志於天下也，有曰：「老者安之，朋友信之，少者懷之。」其天之仁乎？其大德大化乎？故張載氏讀而賛之，以為聖人樂天，合內外而成其仁，蓋亦有見於此矣。《易》曰：「大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。」言大德也。「乾道變化，各正性命，保合太和，乃利貞。」言大化也。大德者，天之仁也；大化者，仁之顯也。仁則天之生生而不已者也。生生而不已者，化化而無窮也。故天道顯諸仁，藏諸用，鼓萬物而不與聖人同憂。聖人則體天之撰，成天之能，財成其道而輔相其宜者也。故天道好生，聖人亦好生；天普萬物而同仁，聖人亦同仁以普天下。故天下有不得其所者，則聖人有憂焉矣。何也？天生聖人以賛化也。聖人大公而應，合同而化，以若天也。今天地大矣，萬物夥矣，人民眾
translation_en:
…then his transforming influence brings great unity, with no distinction between inner and outer. When the distinction between things and self is forgotten and inner and outer become one, virtue reaches its fullest abundance and transformation its utmost spiritual efficacy. Who but the highest sage, who comprehends Heaven, could attain this? In former times, Confucius spoke of his aspirations for the world, saying: “To bring ease to the aged, to be trustworthy toward friends, and to cherish the young.” Is this not Heaven’s benevolence? Is this not great virtue and great transformation? Thus Zhang Zai, reading these words, praised them, holding that the sage delights in Heaven and unites inner and outer to perfect his benevolence. He too evidently had insight into this.

The Book of Changes says: “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! The myriad things draw upon it for their beginnings, and it governs Heaven.” This speaks of great virtue. “The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing attains its proper nature and destiny. Preserving and uniting supreme harmony, it thus brings benefit and constancy.” This speaks of great transformation. Great virtue is Heaven’s benevolence; great transformation is the manifestation of benevolence. Benevolence is Heaven’s ceaseless generation of life. Ceaseless generation means transformation succeeding transformation without end. Thus the Way of Heaven manifests itself in benevolence and conceals itself in its workings; it impels the myriad things but does not share the sage’s cares. The sage embodies Heaven’s works and brings Heaven’s capacities to fruition, regulating and completing its Way and assisting its appropriate operations.

Thus the Way of Heaven cherishes life, and the sage likewise cherishes life. Heaven extends to the myriad things and treats them with equal benevolence; the sage likewise extends equal benevolence throughout the world. Consequently, whenever anything under Heaven fails to find its proper place, the sage is concerned for it. Why is this? Heaven brings forth the sage to assist in transformation. The sage responds with utter impartiality and transforms through unity and concord, thereby conforming to Heaven. Now Heaven and Earth are vast, the myriad things abundant, and the people numerous…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣然其形異者其體同其勢殊者其理一
聖人會其同以統其異得其一以約其殊
非至仁其曷成之故因天心以布德順物
理而施化人有君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友
則爲之忠敬孝慈倡隨友恭睦信之化以
成之人有喜怒哀樂則爲之鍾磬刑罰燕
祀麻踊之化以成之人有飲食衣服男女
居處則爲之稼穡滋味布帛婚姻宮室駕
乗之化以成之人有禮樂文章則爲之庠
===
序學校詩書道藝以成之物有鳥獸魚鼈
昆蟲草木則爲之網罟斧斨山林川澤之
化以成之天秉陽垂日星地秉陰竅於山
川則爲之彌綸參贊節宣之化以成之由
是人得其理而以恬以熈物得其理而以
滋以茂天地得其理而以清以寧而聖人
之仁始大化乎天下而天下莫不同體於
仁是之謂大同然自有我者之溺情於內
也而不知萬物之同乎我於是乎執焉而
punctuated: 矣。然其形異者，其體同；其勢殊者，其理一。聖人會其同以統其異，得其一以約其殊，非至仁，其曷成之？故因天心以布德，順物理而施化。人有君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼、朋友，則爲之忠敬、孝慈、倡隨、友恭、睦信之化以成之；人有喜怒哀樂，則爲之鍾磬、刑罰、燕祀、麻踊之化以成之；人有飲食、衣服、男女、居處，則爲之稼穡、滋味、布帛、婚姻、宮室、駕乗之化以成之；人有禮樂文章，則爲之庠序、學校、詩書、道藝以成之；物有鳥獸、魚鼈、昆蟲、草木，則爲之網罟、斧斨、山林、川澤之化以成之。天秉陽，垂日星；地秉陰，竅於山川，則爲之彌綸、參贊、節宣之化以成之。由是人得其理而以恬以熈，物得其理而以滋以茂，天地得其理而以清以寧，而聖人之仁始大化乎天下，而天下莫不同體於仁，是之謂大同。然自有我者之溺情於內也，而不知萬物之同乎我，於是乎執焉而
translation_en:
…Yet those things that differ in form share the same substance; those that differ in circumstances have a single underlying principle. The sage brings together what they share to govern their differences, and grasps their unity to bring their diversity into order. Without consummate benevolence, how could he accomplish this? Thus he follows Heaven’s heart in extending virtue and accords with the principles of things in bringing about transformation.

Among people there are rulers and ministers, fathers and sons, husbands and wives, elders and juniors, and friends. To bring these relationships to fulfillment, he transforms people through loyalty and respect, filial devotion and parental kindness, leading and following, brotherly affection and deference, harmony and trustworthiness. People experience joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure. To bring these to fulfillment, he transforms people through bells and chime stones, punishments and penalties, feasts and sacrifices, and mourning hemp and ritual leaping. People need food and drink, clothing, relations between men and women, and places to dwell. To bring these to fulfillment, he transforms people through sowing and harvesting, the preparation of flavors, cloth and silk, marriage, houses, and conveyances. People have rites, music, and cultural accomplishments. To bring these to fulfillment, he provides local schools and other institutions of learning, the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, the Way and the arts. Among living things there are birds and beasts, fish and turtles, insects, grasses and trees. To bring these to fulfillment, he orders their transformation through nets and axes and the management of mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes.

Heaven holds yang and displays the sun and stars; Earth holds yin and opens its apertures in mountains and rivers. To bring these to fulfillment, he effects transformation by comprehensively ordering their workings, participating in and assisting them, and regulating and giving them expression. Thus people attain their proper principles and become tranquil and harmonious; living things attain their proper principles and flourish luxuriantly; Heaven and Earth attain their proper principles and become clear and peaceful. Only then does the sage’s benevolence bring about a great transformation throughout the world, so that all under Heaven share one substance in benevolence. This is what is called the Great Unity.

Yet those who maintain a separate self become immersed in their feelings within and fail to understand that the myriad things are one with themselves. Consequently they cling fast and…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不化自狥物者之溺情於外也而不知我
之同乎萬物於是乎推焉而不準夫不準
不化則物我俱病而違仁也遠矣何也私
意不足以成德小智非所以達天古之聖
人洞涵太虛全體萬物舉六合之廣萬有
之大而納之吾心而非有外也以吾之一
心通之六合之廣萬有之大而非有内也
充之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海而非
物也斂之而善乎一身藏之而遯乎一世
===
而非我也無物無我無内無外渾淪而徧
覆光溥而含弘夫是之爲大公公則同矣
同則化矣故大道之行天下爲公天施其
生而不匱聖廣其化而無違恩加乎百姓
則忠敬孝友之風行慈愛信義之俗作利
用厚生之和起老有所終壯有所用幼有
所長矜寡孤獨廢疾者皆有所養德格乎
天地澤流乎萬物則日月星辰不爽其行
寒暑四時不愆其序山陵不崩川谷不塞
punctuated: 不化。自狥物者之溺情於外也，而不知我之同乎萬物，於是乎推焉而不準。夫不準不化，則物我俱病，而違仁也遠矣。何也？私意不足以成德，小智非所以達天。古之聖人洞涵太虛，全體萬物，舉六合之廣、萬有之大而納之吾心，而非有外也；以吾之一心通之六合之廣、萬有之大，而非有内也。充之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，而非物也；斂之而善乎一身，藏之而遯乎一世，而非我也。無物無我，無内無外，渾淪而徧覆，光溥而含弘。夫是之爲大公，公則同矣，同則化矣。故大道之行，天下爲公。天施其生而不匱，聖廣其化而無違。恩加乎百姓，則忠敬孝友之風行，慈愛信義之俗作，利用厚生之和起。老有所終，壯有所用，幼有所長，矜寡孤獨廢疾者皆有所養。德格乎天地，澤流乎萬物，則日月星辰不爽其行，寒暑四時不愆其序，山陵不崩，川谷不塞。
translation_en: …and fail to transform. Those who surrender themselves to external things become absorbed in feelings directed outward, unaware that the self is one with the myriad things; thus their extension outward lacks a proper standard. When there is neither a proper standard nor transformation, both things and self suffer, and one departs far from benevolence. Why is this? Private intentions cannot perfect virtue, and petty cleverness is no means of comprehending Heaven. The sages of antiquity embraced the Great Void in its utter depth and embodied the myriad things in their entirety. They gathered the breadth of the six directions and the vastness of all existence into their own hearts, so that nothing lay outside; with their single heart they penetrated the breadth of the six directions and the vastness of all existence, so that nothing remained confined within. Expanded, it filled Heaven and Earth; spread abroad, it extended across the Four Seas, yet it was not confined to external things. Gathered in, it perfected their own persons; stored away, it withdrew from the world of their age, yet it was not confined to the self. There was neither thing nor self, neither inner nor outer: an undivided whole encompassing all, broadly radiant and capaciously inclusive. This is called supreme impartiality. Impartiality brings unity, and unity brings transformation. Thus, when the Great Way prevails, all under Heaven is held in common. Heaven bestows life without exhaustion; the sage extends transformation without departing from its course. When beneficence reaches the common people, a spirit of loyalty, reverence, filial devotion, and brotherly affection prevails; customs of kindness, love, trustworthiness, and righteousness arise; and harmony develops through making resources useful and enriching the people's livelihood. The aged have provision to the end of their lives, the able-bodied have scope to employ their abilities, and the young have nurture as they grow. Widowers, widows, orphans, the elderly without children, and those disabled or ill all receive support. When virtue reaches Heaven and Earth and beneficence flows to the myriad things, the sun, moon, and stars do not deviate from their courses; cold and heat and the four seasons do not stray from their sequence; mountains and hills do not collapse, and rivers and valleys are not obstructed…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不化自徇物者之溺情於外也而不知我
之同乎萬物於是乎推焉而不準夫不準
不化則物我俱病而違仁也遠矣何也私
意不足以成德小智非所以達天古之聖
人洞涵太虛全體萬物舉六合之廣萬有
之大而納之吾心而非有外也以吾之一
心通之六合之廣萬有之大而非有内也
充之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海而非
物也斂之而善乎一身藏之而遯乎一世
===
而非我也無物無我無内無外渾淪而徧
覆光溥而含弘夫是之為大公公則同矣
同則化矣故大道之行天下為公天施其
生而不匱聖廣其化而無違恩加乎百姓
則忠敬孝友之風行慈愛信義之俗作利
用厚生之和起老有所終壯有所用幼有
所長矜寡孤獨廢疾者皆有所養德格乎
天地澤流乎萬物則日月星辰不爽其行
寒暑四時不愆其序山陵不崩川谷不塞
punctuated: 不化。自徇物者之溺情於外也，而不知我之同乎萬物，於是乎推焉而不準。夫不準不化，則物我俱病，而違仁也遠矣。何也？私意不足以成德，小智非所以達天。古之聖人洞涵太虛，全體萬物，舉六合之廣、萬有之大而納之吾心，而非有外也；以吾之一心通之六合之廣、萬有之大，而非有内也。充之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，而非物也；斂之而善乎一身，藏之而遯乎一世，而非我也。無物無我，無内無外，渾淪而徧覆，光溥而含弘，夫是之為大公。公則同矣，同則化矣。故大道之行，天下為公。天施其生而不匱，聖廣其化而無違。恩加乎百姓，則忠敬孝友之風行，慈愛信義之俗作，利用厚生之和起；老有所終，壯有所用，幼有所長，矜寡孤獨廢疾者皆有所養。德格乎天地，澤流乎萬物，則日月星辰不爽其行，寒暑四時不愆其序，山陵不崩，川谷不塞。
translation_en:
…does not transform. Those who give themselves over to things drown their feelings in the external [?], without understanding that the self is one with the myriad things. Thus, when they extend themselves outward, they fail to accord with the proper standard. If there is neither conformity to the standard nor transformation, both things and self suffer, and one departs far from benevolence. Why is this? Selfish intentions cannot perfect virtue, and petty cleverness is no means of comprehending Heaven.

The sages of antiquity comprehensively embraced the Great Void and embodied the myriad things in their entirety. They gathered the vastness of the six directions and the immensity of all existence into their own hearts, so that nothing was external. With their single heart they penetrated the vastness of the six directions and the immensity of all existence, so that nothing was internal. Expanded, it filled Heaven and Earth; spread abroad, it extended across the Four Seas, yet it was not an external thing. Gathered inward, it perfected the individual; concealed, it withdrew from the world, yet it was not a separate self. There were neither things nor self, neither inside nor outside: an undivided whole, sheltering all, radiant and expansive, encompassing and capacious. This is what is called supreme impartiality. Impartiality brings unity, and unity brings transformation.

Thus, when the Great Way prevails, All-under-Heaven is held in common. Heaven bestows life without exhaustion; the sage extends transforming influence without departing from it. When gracious favor reaches the common people, a spirit of loyalty, reverence, filial devotion, and brotherly affection prevails; customs of kindness, love, trustworthiness, and righteousness arise; and harmony develops through making resources useful and enriching people's livelihoods. The old have provision for their remaining years, the able-bodied have employment, and the young have nurture. Widowers, widows, orphans, the childless elderly, and those disabled or ill all receive support. When virtue reaches Heaven and Earth and beneficence flows to the myriad things, the sun, moon, and stars do not deviate from their courses; cold, heat, and the four seasons do not depart from their sequence; mountains and hills do not collapse, and rivers and valleys are not obstructed…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同前
邵漳
同考試官教諭鄭批此作以內外物我推廣
題意可盡聖人合一之學且體製渾厚筆力高古
蓋出入秦漢六朝而歸諸時製者可占所蘊
考試官教諭陳批內外成仁處作者多影
響不切此作以理一二字該貫始末最爲真的且
詞氣醇典筆力古健其邃於理學者乎
考試官學正陳批意深而不晦詞約而有
===
章蓋自古文中變換出來者
論曰天下之理一也聖人之心一於理故
其通天下也無間而濟天下也不窮蓋天
下之理同具於人心聖人與天下一也本
無內外可言也而聖人之心渾融合一與
天同體者也聖人之心與天同體則聖人
之心天地之府也萬物之命也天下之理
皆會合於一身夫何有於彼此夫何有於
內外故聖人之盡人也非求之於人也以
punctuated:
同前。
邵漳。
同考試官教諭鄭批：此作以內外物我推廣題意，可盡聖人合一之學，且體製渾厚，筆力高古，蓋出入秦漢六朝而歸諸時製者，可占所蘊。
考試官教諭陳批：內外成仁處，作者多影響不切。此作以理一二字該貫始末，最爲真的，且詞氣醇典，筆力古健，其邃於理學者乎？
考試官學正陳批：意深而不晦，詞約而有章，蓋自古文中變換出來者。
論曰：天下之理一也。聖人之心一於理，故其通天下也無間，而濟天下也不窮。蓋天下之理同具於人心，聖人與天下一也，本無內外可言也。而聖人之心渾融合一，與天同體者也。聖人之心與天同體，則聖人之心，天地之府也，萬物之命也。天下之理皆會合於一身，夫何有於彼此？夫何有於內外？故聖人之盡人也，非求之於人也，以
translation_en:
Same topic as above.
Shao Zhang 邵漳.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor (jiaoyu): This composition develops the topic through the distinctions between inner and outer, things and self, fully conveying the sage’s learning of unity. Its form is substantial and rounded, and its writing lofty and antique. Drawing freely upon the Qin, Han, and Six Dynasties, it brings their styles into the contemporary examination form; from this one can discern the author’s intellectual resources.
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor (jiaoyu): On achieving humaneness through the inner and outer, writers often offer vague echoes that miss the point. This composition uses the two characters meaning “principle is one” to encompass and connect the argument from beginning to end, with exceptional authenticity and precision. Moreover, its diction and tone are pure and classical, and its writing antique and vigorous. Surely its author is deeply versed in the Learning of Principle?
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor (xuezheng): Its meaning is profound without being obscure; its wording is concise yet well ordered. It has evidently been fashioned through a transformation of ancient prose.
The discourse reads: Principle throughout the world is one. The sage’s mind is at one with principle; thus, in comprehending all under Heaven, it encounters no divisions, and in aiding all under Heaven, it is inexhaustible. For the principle of all under Heaven is equally present in human minds. The sage is one with all under Heaven: fundamentally, there is no inner or outer to speak of. The sage’s mind blends all into a harmonious unity and forms one body with Heaven. Since the sage’s mind forms one body with Heaven, it is the storehouse of Heaven and Earth and the life of the myriad things. All the principles of the world converge in his person. What distinction, then, can there be between that and this? What distinction between inner and outer? Thus, when the sage brings others to fulfillment, he does not seek it in others, but by…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吾心之理盡之也其盡已也非求之於已
也以人心之理盡之也是則內也而莫非
外外也而莫非內所謂性之德也合內外
之道也所謂聖人合內外而成其仁也今
夫天地之生萬物也大理而物博者天地
之理無乎不盡也而萬物之受生于天地
也性命各正者其理亦無乎不自足者也
故謂萬物之生乃萬物之理而非天地之
理不可也謂天地之生萬物乃天地之理
===
而非萬物之理不可也謂萬物有求於天
地天地有私於萬物亦不可也蓋惟天地
之道同也故無心而成化萬物之理公也
故無情而成能使天地之大而有一私之
隔則化機生息必有窒塞阻礙而不能通
者故曰合同而化天之道也知天地合同
之化則知聖人合內外之仁矣自今言之
老者少者朋友人之類也不與聖人等也
而安之信之懷之八之理也於聖人若無
punctuated:
吾心之理盡之也。其盡已也，非求之於已也，以人心之理盡之也。是則內也而莫非外，外也而莫非內。所謂「性之德也，合內外之道也」，所謂聖人合內外而成其仁也。
今夫天地之生萬物也，大理而物博者，天地之理無乎不盡也。而萬物之受生于天地也，性命各正者，其理亦無乎不自足者也。故謂萬物之生乃萬物之理而非天地之理，不可也；謂天地之生萬物乃天地之理而非萬物之理，不可也；謂萬物有求於天地，天地有私於萬物，亦不可也。蓋惟天地之道同也，故無心而成化；萬物之理公也，故無情而成能。使天地之大而有一私之隔，則化機生息必有窒塞阻礙而不能通者。故曰：「合同而化，天之道也。」知天地合同之化，則知聖人合內外之仁矣。
自今言之，老者、少者、朋友，人之類也，不與聖人等也。而安之、信之、懷之，八之理也，於聖人若無
translation_en:
…by bringing them to fulfillment through the principle in my own heart. In bringing himself to fulfillment [?], he does not seek this within himself, but brings himself to fulfillment through the principle in others’ hearts. Thus, what is internal is entirely external, and what is external is entirely internal. This is what is meant by “the virtue of one’s nature, the Way that unites the internal and external”; it is what is meant by the sage’s uniting the internal and external to perfect his benevolence.
Now, when Heaven and Earth give birth to the myriad things, the vastness of principle and abundance of things [?] mean that the principle of Heaven and Earth is nowhere left unfulfilled. When the myriad things receive life from Heaven and Earth, each attains its proper nature and allotted existence, and its principle is likewise everywhere sufficient in itself. Thus, one cannot say that the birth of the myriad things belongs to their own principle but not to the principle of Heaven and Earth. Nor can one say that Heaven and Earth’s giving birth to the myriad things belongs to the principle of Heaven and Earth but not to that of the myriad things. Nor can one say that the myriad things make demands upon Heaven and Earth, or that Heaven and Earth show partiality toward the myriad things. Precisely because the Way of Heaven and Earth is shared, they accomplish transformation without deliberate intention; because the principle of the myriad things is impartial, they realize their capacities without feeling. If, within the vastness of Heaven and Earth, even a single selfish separation existed, the generative activity of transformation would inevitably encounter blockage and obstruction and fail to flow freely. Hence the saying: “To unite in harmony and transform is the Way of Heaven.” Understanding the transformation accomplished through the harmonious union of Heaven and Earth, one understands the sage’s benevolence, which unites the internal and external.
To speak of this in present terms: the aged, the young, and friends are categories of people, and are not on a par with the sage. Yet to give them peace, to deal faithfully with them, and to cherish them are principles pertaining to people [?]; with regard to the sage, these seem to have no …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
與也所以安之所以信之所以懷之聖人
之理也亦無與於人也然而人之理各足
於人之身必待聖人而後盡聖人之理存
於吾心必待盡人而後成此可以觀其故
矣蓋理一也太極本然之妙無精粗本末
彼此假借者也而何有於內外惟夫吾心
之理有一毫之未盡則天者未融天者未
融則惟見我之爲內而天下皆外矣故於
是有老少朋友不相聯屬者有安之信之
===
懷之之理不相爲謀者雖欲强而合之不
可得也而聖人者理之管也天之命也人
之盡也道之極也其所付畀其所存主蓋
渾渾乎與天爲一者也所以謂之樂天也
故聖人之理卽天理理無內外心卽天心
心無內外化卽神化化無內外故聖人之
理合於天下卽盡已之性以盡人物之性
者也聖人之心合於天下卽一夫不被其
澤一民不得其所皆已憂者也聖人之化
punctuated: 與也。所以安之，所以信之，所以懷之，聖人之理也，亦無與於人也。然而人之理各足於人之身，必待聖人而後盡；聖人之理存於吾心，必待盡人而後成。此可以觀其故矣。蓋理一也，太極本然之妙，無精粗、本末、彼此假借者也，而何有於內外？惟夫吾心之理有一毫之未盡，則天者未融；天者未融，則惟見我之爲內，而天下皆外矣。故於是有老少朋友不相聯屬者，有安之、信之、懷之之理不相爲謀者，雖欲强而合之，不可得也。而聖人者，理之管也，天之命也，人之盡也，道之極也。其所付畀，其所存主，蓋渾渾乎與天爲一者也，所以謂之樂天也。故聖人之理卽天理，理無內外；心卽天心，心無內外；化卽神化，化無內外。故聖人之理合於天下，卽盡已之性以盡人物之性者也；聖人之心合於天下，卽一夫不被其澤、一民不得其所，皆已憂者也；聖人之化
translation_en:
…has no involvement. That by which the aged are brought to peace, friends are treated with good faith, and the young are cherished is the sage’s principle; it likewise has no involvement with other people. Yet although each person possesses principle in full within himself, it requires the sage for its complete realization. The sage’s principle resides in my own mind, yet it requires the full realization of others before it is complete. From this we can discern the reason. Principle is one: the inherent subtlety of the Supreme Ultimate admits no borrowing between the refined and the coarse, root and branch, or self and other. How, then, could there be an inside and an outside? If even the slightest part of the principle within my mind remains unrealized, what is of Heaven has not been fully integrated. If it has not been integrated, I see only myself as inside and all under Heaven as outside. Thus the aged, the young, and friends become disconnected from one another, and the principles of bringing them peace, treating them with good faith, and cherishing them fail to work together. Even if one wished to force them into unity, one could not.

The sage is the conduit of principle [?], the mandate of Heaven, the complete realization of humanity, and the utmost attainment of the Way. What is entrusted to him and what he preserves and holds fast within are wholly one with Heaven. This is why he is said to delight in Heaven. Thus the sage’s principle is Heaven’s principle, and principle has neither inside nor outside; his mind is Heaven’s mind, and mind has neither inside nor outside; his transforming influence is numinous transformation, and transformation has neither inside nor outside. Thus the sage’s principle accords with all under Heaven: by fully realizing his own nature, he fully realizes the natures of other people and things. The sage’s mind accords with all under Heaven: if a single man fails to receive his beneficence, or a single person fails to find his proper place, he regards it as his own concern. The sage’s transforming influence…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
合於天下即生養休息無所不周禮樂教
化無所不被綏來動和無所不足者也聖
人之仁其內也猶之萬物體統一太極者
也其外也猶之物物各具一太極者也故
天下之老少朋友安之懷之信之聖人也
聖人不得而與也而老者安其安少者懷
其懷朋友信其信亦不知其由於聖人也
非不知也蓋理本如是其在聖人者非有
餘在天下者非不足自聖人視之吾心非
===
內而天下非外自天下視之天下非內聖
人亦非外體用合一之謂聖變通不窮之
謂神神聖盡而聖人之仁畢矣大矣哉聖
人之仁乎易曰乾道變化各正性命夫乾
道變化天何私於物性命各正物何德於
天斯可以語聖人之仁矣彼管商之徒慕
聖人之仁而不知有內乃以力合之以法
把持之是謂無體佛老之學故遺其外乃
曰無爲而自化好靜而自治是謂無用要
punctuated:
合於天下，即生養休息無所不周，禮樂教化無所不被，綏來動和無所不足者也。聖人之仁，其內也，猶之萬物體統一太極者也；其外也，猶之物物各具一太極者也。故天下之老少朋友，安之、懷之、信之，聖人也；聖人不得而與也。而老者安其安，少者懷其懷，朋友信其信，亦不知其由於聖人也。非不知也，蓋理本如是。其在聖人者非有餘，在天下者非不足。自聖人視之，吾心非內，而天下非外；自天下視之，天下非內，聖人亦非外。體用合一之謂聖，變通不窮之謂神。神聖盡，而聖人之仁畢矣。大矣哉，聖人之仁乎！
易曰：「乾道變化，各正性命。」夫乾道變化，天何私於物？性命各正，物何德於天？斯可以語聖人之仁矣。彼管商之徒，慕聖人之仁，而不知有內，乃以力合之，以法把持之，是謂無體。佛老之學，故遺其外，乃曰：「無爲而自化，好靜而自治。」是謂無用。要
translation_en:
…accords with all under Heaven: in nurturing life and providing rest and recuperation, nothing is left uncared for; through ritual, music, instruction, and moral transformation, none are left untouched; in bringing peace, attracting others, stirring them to action, and bringing them into harmony, nothing is lacking. The sage’s benevolence, in its inward aspect, resembles the myriad things united in substance within a single Supreme Ultimate (taiji); in its outward aspect, it resembles each individual thing possessing a Supreme Ultimate of its own. Thus, it is the sage who brings repose to the old throughout the world, cherishes the young, and shows trustworthiness toward friends; yet the sage can claim no part in this. The old enjoy their repose, the young enjoy being cherished, and friends enjoy mutual trust, without knowing that these come from the sage. It is not really that they do not know: principle is inherently like this. As it exists in the sage, it is not excessive; as it exists throughout the world, it is not deficient. From the sage’s perspective, my mind is not internal and the world is not external; from the world’s perspective, the world is not internal and the sage is likewise not external. The unity of substance and function is called sageliness; inexhaustible transformation and adaptation are called spiritual efficacy. When spiritual efficacy and sageliness are fully realized, the sage’s benevolence is complete. How great is the sage’s benevolence!
The Book of Changes says: “The Way of Qian changes and transforms; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny.” As the Way of Qian changes and transforms, what partiality does Heaven show toward things? When each attains its proper nature and allotted destiny, what gratitude do things owe Heaven? Through this one may speak of the sage’s benevolence. Those who follow Guan Zhong and Shang Yang admire the sage’s benevolence but do not recognize its inward aspect. They therefore unite people by force and hold them in check through laws. This is called lacking substance. The teachings of the Buddhists and followers of Laozi deliberately discard its outward aspect, saying: “Through nonaction, the people transform themselves; through a fondness for stillness, the people bring order to themselves.” This is called lacking function. To sum up …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其所以一則狃於欲一則窒於理其不知
樂天一也不知樂天雖欲强合于内外祗
見其離矣奚其仁奚其仁善哉宋儒之言
曰孔子其太極乎曰其天乎語其道也曰
其四時行百物生乎語其仁也斯言也可
與識仁矣或者曰博施濟衆堯舜猶病則
内外成仁不尤難乎愚則曰博施之仁以
勢論之也以勢論則天地猶有憾内外成
仁以理言也以理言夫子猶堯舜也横渠
===
善言聖人者故西銘之書獨得此意乃以
理一分殊言之夫理之一者其分未嘗不
殊分之殊者其理未嘗不一此即内外成
仁之旨也故曰善言聖人者
表
擬
大本堂成宴東宮官及儒士各
賜冠服謝表洪武元年
王燾
punctuated:
其所以，一則狃於欲，一則窒於理，其不知樂天一也。不知樂天，雖欲强合于内外，祗見其離矣。奚其仁？奚其仁？善哉，宋儒之言曰：「孔子其太極乎！」曰：「其天乎！」語其道也；曰：「其四時行、百物生乎！」語其仁也。斯言也，可與識仁矣。或者曰：「博施濟衆，堯舜猶病，則内外成仁不尤難乎？」愚則曰：「博施之仁，以勢論之也。以勢論，則天地猶有憾；内外成仁，以理言也。以理言，夫子猶堯舜也。」横渠善言聖人者，故《西銘》之書獨得此意，乃以理一分殊言之。夫理之一者，其分未嘗不殊；分之殊者，其理未嘗不一。此即内外成仁之旨也，故曰善言聖人者。
表
擬大本堂成，宴東宮官及儒士，各賜冠服，謝表。洪武元年。
王燾
translation_en:
…as for the reasons behind this, the one is habituated to desire, while the other is obstructed in its understanding of principle. They are alike in not knowing how to delight in Heaven. Without knowing how to delight in Heaven, even if they seek forcibly to unite the inner and the outer, they will only see them come apart. Where is their benevolence? Where is their benevolence? Excellent indeed are the words of the Song Confucians: “Was Confucius not the Supreme Ultimate?” And: “Was he not Heaven?” These speak of his Way. “Was he not the movement of the four seasons and the generation of the myriad things?” This speaks of his benevolence. Through these words one may come to understand benevolence.
Someone asks: “Even Yao and Shun found it difficult to bestow benefits widely and bring relief to the multitude. Is it not still more difficult to perfect benevolence through the inner and the outer?” I, in my humble view, reply: “Benevolence as the wide bestowal of benefits is discussed in terms of the power afforded by circumstances. Judged in those terms, even Heaven and Earth leave grounds for regret. Perfecting benevolence through the inner and the outer is spoken of in terms of principle. Judged by principle, the Master was the equal of Yao and Shun.” Hengqu [Zhang Zai] was skilled at speaking of the sage. Thus his Western Inscription uniquely grasped this meaning, expressing it in terms of the unity of principle and the differentiation of particular relationships and duties. Though principle is one, its particular manifestations are invariably differentiated; though those manifestations are differentiated, their principle is invariably one. This is precisely the purport of perfecting benevolence through the inner and the outer. Hence I say that he was skilled at speaking of the sage.
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the completion of Daben Hall, when a banquet was held for the officials of the Heir Apparent’s establishment and the Confucian scholars, and each was granted a cap and robes. Set in the first year of Hongwu [1368].
Wang Tao.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭蔡批語麗而典意渾而厚誠
足以對揚
聖祖之休命矣
同考試官敎諭石批得駢麗之體見忠愛之
忱宜冠多士
考試官敎諭陳批敘事有製造詞有章婉
然寓規誨之意忠讜可嘉
考試官學正陳批不事雕鋉而典麗有則
允宜高薦
===
洪武元年十一月某日伏蒙
皇上大本堂成宴東宮官及儒士各
賜冠服者
德昭
聖訓
青宮宏懋學之規道啟人文
紫禁賁優賢之典沐
湛恩於俎豆佩
華寵於冠裳沾被有榮荷承無極臣等誠惶
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭蔡批：語麗而典，意渾而厚，誠足以對揚聖祖之休命矣。
同考試官敎諭石批：得駢麗之體，見忠愛之忱，宜冠多士。
考試官敎諭陳批：敘事有製，造詞有章，婉然寓規誨之意，忠讜可嘉。
考試官學正陳批：不事雕鋉，而典麗有則，允宜高薦。

洪武元年十一月某日，伏蒙皇上大本堂成，宴東宮官及儒士，各賜冠服者。
德昭聖訓，青宮宏懋學之規；道啟人文，紫禁賁優賢之典。沐湛恩於俎豆，佩華寵於冠裳，沾被有榮，荷承無極。臣等誠惶
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The language is elegant and classical; the meaning is integrated and profound. It is indeed worthy of acknowledging and extolling the Sagely Founder's gracious command.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: “It achieves the elegant form of parallel prose and reveals heartfelt loyalty and devotion. It deserves to rank first among the candidates.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The narration is well ordered, and the phrasing is well patterned. It subtly conveys admonition and instruction; its loyalty and candor merit praise.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: “Without resorting to elaborate verbal polishing, it is classically elegant and conforms to proper standards. It fully deserves recommendation at a high rank.”

On a certain day of the eleventh month of the first year of Hongwu [1368], we humbly received His Majesty's favor: upon the completion of the Hall of the Great Foundation, he banqueted the officials of the Eastern Palace and the Confucian scholars, bestowing caps and robes upon each.
Virtue shines forth in the sage instructions; the Crown Prince's palace enlarges its program of diligent learning. The Way brings forth human culture; the imperial precincts embellish the ceremony honoring worthy men. Amid the sacrificial vessels and dishes, we are bathed in abundant grace; in our caps and robes, we wear splendid marks of favor. To receive these blessings is an honor; our gratitude for bearing them knows no bounds. We, your servants, are truly awestruck…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
誠恐稽首頓首上言伏以唐虞繼世勳華
炳協德之輝文武承天謨烈闡重光之運
蓋大道之統傳不異故聖人之世守攸同
欲垂憲于無疆恒學古而有獲典樂敎冑
子職始虞夔制禮相成王法垂周旦齒學
具為子為弟為臣之道弼丞存太師太傅
太保之官仁義道德養其蒙恭敬溫文表
其懌故詩書禮樂列之上庠而羽籥干戈
詔於東序欲出入起居之皆善在前後左
===
右之必賢誠取師資用裨帝學蓋淑元良
而貞萬國自古為然重
大本以考三王於今不謬臣等材非棫樸業
忝章縫仰
日月於中天方同爝火俯滄江於大地僅比
涓涯敢意招延殊慚茂乂茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
睿智聰明
聖神文武
punctuated:
誠恐，稽首頓首上言：伏以唐虞繼世，勳華炳協德之輝；文武承天，謨烈闡重光之運。蓋大道之統傳不異，故聖人之世守攸同。欲垂憲于無疆，恒學古而有獲。典樂敎冑子，職始虞夔；制禮相成王，法垂周旦。齒學具為子、為弟、為臣之道，弼丞存太師、太傅、太保之官。仁義道德養其蒙，恭敬溫文表其懌。故詩書禮樂列之上庠，而羽籥干戈詔於東序。欲出入起居之皆善，在前後左右之必賢。誠取師資，用裨帝學。蓋淑元良而貞萬國，自古為然；重大本以考三王，於今不謬。
臣等材非棫樸，業忝章縫。仰日月於中天，方同爝火；俯滄江於大地，僅比涓涯。敢意招延，殊慚茂乂。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，睿智聰明，聖神文武。
translation_en:
…in profound fear, we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow, submitting these words: We humbly consider that when Tang and Yu succeeded one another in rule, Yao and Shun shone with the radiance of concordant virtue; when Kings Wen and Wu received Heaven’s mandate, their counsels and achievements manifested an age of renewed brilliance. Since the transmission of the great Way’s succession does not differ, what sages preserve from generation to generation is likewise the same. Wishing to bequeath enduring models without limit, they constantly learn from antiquity and thereby gain understanding. Directing music and teaching the sons of the nobility was a duty first entrusted to Kui of Yu; establishing ritual and assisting King Cheng were precedents handed down by Dan, the Duke of Zhou. Taking one’s place by age in the school comprehensively embodies the ways of being a son, a younger brother, and a subject. For guidance and assistance there are the offices of Grand Preceptor, Grand Mentor, and Grand Guardian. Benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue nurture the young in their unformed understanding; reverence, respect, gentleness, and refinement express their delight [?]. Thus poetry, documents, ritual, and music are set forth in the higher school, while dances with feathers and flutes, shields and halberds are taught in the eastern school. To ensure that all their movements and daily conduct are good, those before and behind them, to their left and right, must be worthy. Truly, teachers are chosen to assist imperial learning. To cultivate the heir apparent and thereby set the myriad states aright has been the practice since antiquity; to attach weight to the great foundation and test it against the Three Kings remains sound today.
We, your servants, lack the timber-like worth celebrated in “Yu pu,” and our learning is unworthy of our scholars’ caps. Looking up at the sun and moon in mid-heaven, we are no more than flickering torches; looking down upon the vast river across the earth, we scarcely compare to a tiny trickle [?]. How could we have imagined receiving your summons? We are deeply ashamed to be counted among the outstanding and able. This is because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, possessed of penetrating wisdom and clear understanding, sagely and divine, accomplished in civil and martial virtues …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
叙彝倫而立極造區夏以開天
曆數攸歸纘堯舜禹湯之大統
聖人有作丕高明博厚之洪基
道貫三靈
德含萬類念風愆而示敬思典則以詒謨早
建
皇儲聿端
聖範業構肯堂之義謀詒豐芑之仁謂植本有
區闢棟隆於
===
天府曰陪德在士攬法從於儒紳抽
金匱石室之藏闡東壁西奎之曜揭
璇題于銀榜名義有嚴窺
紫宸于太清對揚無斁道萬殊而一本禮前疑
而後丞博𡙇崇賢詎云勝事英聲茂實竊
慶榮逢惟
乾宮妥八柱之承見
離位協
重明之照
punctuated: 叙彝倫而立極，造區夏以開天。曆數攸歸，纘堯舜禹湯之大統；聖人有作，丕高明博厚之洪基。道貫三靈，德含萬類。念風愆而示敬，思典則以詒謨。早建皇儲，聿端聖範。業構肯堂之義，謀詒豐芑之仁。謂植本有區，闢棟隆於天府；曰陪德在士，攬法從於儒紳。抽金匱石室之藏，闡東壁西奎之曜。揭璇題于銀榜，名義有嚴；窺紫宸于太清，對揚無斁。道萬殊而一本，禮前疑而後丞。博𡙇崇賢，詎云勝事？英聲茂實，竊慶榮逢。惟乾宮妥八柱之承，見離位協重明之照。
translation_en:
…ordering the enduring human relationships and establishing the supreme standard, shaping the Chinese realm and opening a new heaven. The succession ordained by Heaven has come to you: you continue the great line of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang. A sage has arisen, magnifying the great foundation, lofty and luminous, broad and deep. Your Way pervades the three powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and your virtue embraces all kinds of beings. Mindful of admonitions against error, you demonstrate reverence; contemplating the established standards, you bequeath plans for the future. Early you designated the imperial heir, thereby setting the sagely example aright. Your undertaking embodies the duty of a son willing to build upon his father’s foundations; your planning transmits the benevolence figured by luxuriant millet, providing for descendants.
You declare that planting the foundation has its proper place, raising the ridgepole in Heaven’s storehouse [?]; you say that scholars must assist in cultivating virtue, and select attendant officials from among the Confucian gentry. You draw forth the treasures stored in golden coffers and stone chambers, revealing the radiance of the Eastern Wall and western Kui constellations, patrons of letters. You display the precious inscription upon a silver tablet, giving solemn weight to its name and meaning. We glimpse the Purple Palace in the clear heights of Heaven and respond to your commands with tireless praise. The Way, though manifold in its manifestations, has a single root; ritual places an Adviser in front and an Assistant behind. Broadly […] honoring the worthy [?]—could this be called merely a splendid occasion? Encountering such illustrious renown and abundant achievement, we privately rejoice in this honor. With the Palace of Qian securely supported by its eight pillars, we behold the position of Li—the imperial heir—joining in the radiance of doubled brightness.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明良喜起燕賞弘敷饌出太官鼎實衍醇醲之
惠衣頒織室宮袍分纖綺之章韋布增輝
鳧鷖飽德賓筵露湛豈豐草之無心峨弁
星環信戴天之有象幸延芳於芝苑遂挿
羽於瓊條飫虎觀給膳之恩惟圖獻納服
瀛洲賜衣之寵祇效論思臣等敢不忠勵
和羹義追補袞咨寅清而宣力協俊乂以
同心竭股肱之勞欽承
燕翼嚴冠裳之體丕闡
===
鴻猷晨昏講三至之儀夙夜謹十寒之戒紀
言紀動時承
翠蓋之臨養德養身日祇
彤庭之直伏願
致中和而位育
兼創守以顯承作者
聖而述者
明式廣重熙之化尊曰
君而親曰
punctuated: 明良喜起，燕賞弘敷。饌出太官，鼎實衍醇醲之惠；衣頒織室，宮袍分纖綺之章。韋布增輝，鳧鷖飽德。賓筵露湛，豈豐草之無心；峨弁星環，信戴天之有象。幸延芳於芝苑，遂挿羽於瓊條。飫虎觀給膳之恩，惟圖獻納；服瀛洲賜衣之寵，祇效論思。臣等敢不忠勵和羹，義追補袞，咨寅清而宣力，協俊乂以同心，竭股肱之勞，欽承燕翼，嚴冠裳之體，丕闡鴻猷。晨昏講三至之儀，夙夜謹十寒之戒。紀言紀動，時承翠蓋之臨；養德養身，日祇彤庭之直。伏願致中和而位育，兼創守以顯承。作者聖而述者明，式廣重熙之化；尊曰君而親曰
translation_en:
…The enlightened sovereign and his worthy ministers rejoice together and rouse one another to action; banquets and rewards are generously bestowed. Dishes come from the imperial kitchens, their rich contents extending the bounty of full-flavored fare; clothing is distributed from the imperial weaving workshop, court robes sharing the splendor of fine patterned silk. Even men in plain cloth gain luster; like the ducks and gulls of the ode, we feast upon your beneficence. At the guests’ banquet, dew lies heavy: could we, like luxuriant grass, remain insensible to it? Our lofty caps encircle you like stars, truly giving visible form to our reverence for Heaven above. Fortunately admitted to spread our fragrance in the garden of auspicious plants, we have found a perch upon its jeweled branches. Sated by the favor of meals provided at the Tiger Observatory, we seek only to offer counsel; clothed through the favor of robes bestowed upon the scholars of Yingzhou, we strive only to deliberate and reflect.

How could we, your servants, fail loyally to exert ourselves in blending the broth of government, or dutifully to emulate those who mend the sovereign’s ceremonial robe? We shall strive to serve with reverence and purity, joining worthy and talented men in common purpose. We shall exhaust our strength as your limbs and sinews, reverently carrying forward your plans for the welfare of your descendants, maintaining the dignity of our official dress and station, and greatly advancing your grand designs. From morning to evening we shall observe the ritual of attending three times daily; day and night we shall heed the warning against letting ten days of cold undo our efforts. Recording your words and deeds, we shall regularly receive the approach of your kingfisher-feather canopy; cultivating virtue and preserving our persons, we shall daily attend reverently to our duties in the vermilion court.

We humbly wish that you may bring equilibrium and harmony to their fullest realization, so that Heaven and Earth take their proper places and all things flourish; and that, combining the work of founding with that of preserving, you may gloriously carry on the inheritance. He who creates is a sage, and he who transmits is enlightened: may you thereby extend the transforming influence of successive splendid reigns. In reverence you are called sovereign, and in affection you are called…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乂共成有道之休海潤星暉延
本支於百世天長地久保
福祚於萬年臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第三場
===
策
第一問
沈束
同考試官教諭王批洪範理數天錫大禹自
蔡氏之後又幾無傳至我
列聖相傳心法之要千古一揆子能鋪張揚厲于篇豈嘗究心理學
而有得者乎
同考試官教諭陳批闡揚蔡氏家學精蘊如
指諸掌而始終歸重於皇極又有以發明我
punctuated:
乂，共成有道之休。海潤星暉，延本支於百世；天長地久，保福祚於萬年。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第三場
策
第一問
沈束

同考試官教諭王批：洪範理數，天錫大禹，自蔡氏之後，又幾無傳。至我列聖，相傳心法之要，千古一揆。子能鋪張揚厲于篇，豈嘗究心理學而有得者乎？

同考試官教諭陳批：闡揚蔡氏家學精蘊，如指諸掌，而始終歸重於皇極，又有以發明我
translation_en:
…governance [?], together bringing about the blessings of the Way. With the ocean’s bounty and the stars’ radiance, may the main line and branches of the imperial house endure for a hundred generations; enduring as Heaven and Earth, may imperial blessings last for ten thousand years. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty, overcome with fervent emotion and reverent trepidation. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Shen Shu 沈束

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The principles and numbers of the Great Plan were bestowed by Heaven upon the Great Yu. After Master Cai, their transmission again nearly ceased. Coming down to our successive sage emperors, the essentials of the teaching of the mind transmitted among them have followed one standard throughout the ages. You have elaborated and celebrated these in your essay. Have you perhaps devoted yourself to investigating the Learning of Principle and attained insight into it?

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: You elucidate the profound essentials of the Cai family’s learning as clearly as if pointing to something in your palm. From beginning to end, you place primary emphasis on the August Ultimate, and further illuminate our…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
朝
列聖心極相傳之妙可與言範矣
考試官教諭陳批數學不聞鮮究其旨子
推原作者之意深明
列聖之傳豈多學而識之者歟
考試官學正陳批以理揆數敷對詳明
聖人明於天之道也察於人之故也而後
立極於天下焉蓋聖人之立極也統天人
而為之者也是故包萬象於一身而其體
===
溥以博會萬理於一心而其源精以明夫
然後觀其會通以行其典禮以開天下之
物以成天下之務而天下無不會歸於極
夫是之謂觀乎天文以察時變觀乎人文
以化成天下而為天下之至聖而為皇建
之有極不然溺於數者其失則眇矣執於
象者其失則陋矣抑何以能立極而成化
也哉此我
太祖高皇帝繼天立極之初深有取於洪範之
punctuated:
朝列聖心極相傳之妙，可與言範矣。
考試官教諭陳批：數學不聞，鮮究其旨。子推原作者之意，深明列聖之傳，豈多學而識之者歟？
考試官學正陳批：以理揆數，敷對詳明。
聖人明於天之道也，察於人之故也，而後立極於天下焉。蓋聖人之立極也，統天人而為之者也。是故包萬象於一身，而其體溥以博；會萬理於一心，而其源精以明。夫然後觀其會通，以行其典禮，以開天下之物，以成天下之務，而天下無不會歸於極。夫是之謂觀乎天文以察時變，觀乎人文以化成天下，而為天下之至聖，而為皇建之有極。不然，溺於數者，其失則眇矣；執於象者，其失則陋矣。抑何以能立極而成化也哉？此我太祖高皇帝繼天立極之初，深有取於《洪範》之
translation_en:
…the subtlety with which the successive sage sovereigns of our dynasty transmitted to one another the supreme standard of the mind. You are someone with whom one may discuss the Great Plan.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: Learning concerning numbers has gone unheard of, and few have investigated its purport. You trace the author’s intentions to their source and clearly understand the transmission among our successive sage sovereigns. Can you be merely someone who has learned much and retained it?
Examiner Chen, School Director, comments: You assess numbers through principle; your exposition in reply is detailed and clear.
The sage understands the Way of Heaven and discerns the circumstances of human affairs; only then does he establish the supreme standard throughout the world. In establishing this standard, the sage unites Heaven and humanity. Thus he embraces the myriad phenomena within his own person, and his essential constitution is all-encompassing and broad; he gathers the myriad principles within a single mind, and their source is refined and luminous. Only then does he observe their convergence and interconnection, put into practice their prescribed rites, develop the things of the world, and accomplish the affairs of the world, so that nothing in the world fails to converge upon the supreme standard. This is what is meant by observing Heaven’s patterns to discern the changes of the seasons, and observing human patterns to transform and perfect the world: thus becoming the utmost sage of the world and establishing the sovereign’s supreme standard. Otherwise, those who immerse themselves in numbers err through abstruseness, while those who cling to images err through narrowness. How, then, could they establish the supreme standard and accomplish transformation? This is why our Emperor Taizu Gao, when first succeeding Heaven and establishing the supreme standard, drew deeply upon the Great Plan’s…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
一書也大哉
皇言乎敘彝倫而光紹千古建皇極而神統萬
方非天下之至聖孰能與於此蓋嘗讀尚
書洪範及宋儒蔡沈洪範皇極內篇而有
以知帝王治天下之大法矣請得而敬陳
之易曰天垂象見吉凶聖人象之河出圖
洛出書聖人則之是故宓羲氏繼天而王
則受河圖以畫八卦禹治洪水天錫洛書
則法而陳之以為九疇其洪範之昉乎然
===
聖人因象而知數察數以明理行其道而
寶其書故雖商之末世箕子猶在父師之
位而典之及周克殷以箕子歸武王乃親
虛己而問焉曰嗚呼箕子惟天陰隲下民
相協厥居我不知其彝倫攸敘箕子乃言
曰我聞在昔鯀堙洪水汩陳其五行帝乃
震怒弗畀洪範九疇彝倫攸斁鯀則殛死
禹乃嗣興天乃錫禹洪範九疇彝倫攸敘
是則洪範一書皆所以敘彝倫也故其文
punctuated: 一書也。大哉，皇言乎！敘彝倫而光紹千古，建皇極而神統萬方，非天下之至聖，孰能與於此？蓋嘗讀《尚書》〈洪範〉及宋儒蔡沈《洪範皇極內篇》，而有以知帝王治天下之大法矣。請得而敬陳之。《易》曰：「天垂象，見吉凶，聖人象之；河出圖，洛出書，聖人則之。」是故宓羲氏繼天而王，則受河圖以畫八卦；禹治洪水，天錫洛書，則法而陳之，以為九疇。其洪範之昉乎？然聖人因象而知數，察數以明理，行其道而寶其書，故雖商之末世，箕子猶在父師之位而典之。及周克殷，以箕子歸，武王乃親虛己而問焉，曰：「嗚呼！箕子，惟天陰隲下民，相協厥居。我不知其彝倫攸敘。」箕子乃言曰：「我聞在昔，鯀堙洪水，汩陳其五行，帝乃震怒，弗畀洪範九疇，彝倫攸斁。鯀則殛死，禹乃嗣興。天乃錫禹洪範九疇，彝倫攸敘。」是則《洪範》一書，皆所以敘彝倫也。故其文
translation_en:
…this single work. How great are the imperial words! To order the constant relationships and gloriously carry forward the legacy of ages, to establish the August Ultimate and wondrously unite all regions—who but the greatest sage under Heaven could accomplish this? I have read the “Great Plan” (Hongfan) in the Book of Documents, together with the Inner Chapters on the August Ultimate of the Great Plan by the Song Confucian scholar Cai Shen, and thereby come to understand the great principles by which emperors and kings govern the realm. Permit me respectfully to set them forth.

The Book of Changes says: “Heaven displays images that reveal good and ill fortune, and the sages model themselves upon them. The Yellow River brought forth the Chart, and the Luo River brought forth the Writing, and the sages took them as their rule.” Thus, when Fuxi succeeded Heaven as king, he received the River Chart and used it to draw the eight trigrams. When Yu brought the floodwaters under control, Heaven bestowed the Luo Writing; he took it as his model and arranged it into the Nine Categories. Was this not the beginning of the Great Plan? Yet the sages understood numbers through images, examined numbers to illuminate principles, practiced its Way, and treasured its text. Thus, even in the last days of the Shang, Jizi still held the position of Preceptor (fushi) and had charge of it. When the Zhou conquered the Yin and brought Jizi back with them, King Wu personally humbled himself and questioned him, saying: “Ah, Jizi! Heaven invisibly establishes the people below, assisting them to live together in harmony. I do not understand how the constant relationships are brought into order.”

Jizi then said: “I have heard that in ancient times Gun dammed the floodwaters and disrupted the orderly arrangement of the Five Phases. The Lord on High was greatly angered and did not grant him the Nine Categories of the Great Plan; the constant relationships consequently fell into disorder. Gun was put to death, and Yu arose to succeed him. Heaven then bestowed upon Yu the Nine Categories of the Great Plan, and the constant relationships were brought into order.” Thus, the entire Great Plan serves to order the constant relationships. Hence its text…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰初一曰五行次二曰敬用五事次三曰
農用八政次四曰協用五紀次五曰建用
皇極次六曰乂用三德次七曰明用稽疑
次八曰念用庶徵次九曰嚮用五福威用
六極夫五行者天之道也五事者人之故
也八政者人之所以因乎天也五紀者天
之所以示乎人也皇極者君之所以建極
也三德者治之所以應變也稽疑者以人
而聽於天也庶徵者推天而徵之人也福
===
極者人感而天應也聖人傳心之法帝王
致治之要莫加焉矣故西山真氏曰洪範
九疇六十有五字耳而天道人事無不該
焉原其本皆自人君一身始信哉言乎夫
由天之人而其理則已明自一之九而其
數則已具蔡沈乃曰易更四聖而象已著
範錫神禹而數不傳於是作洪範內篇八
十一卦以方圓擬圖以九九積數以為體
天地之撰者易之象紀天地之撰者易之
punctuated:
曰：「初一曰五行，次二曰敬用五事，次三曰農用八政，次四曰協用五紀，次五曰建用皇極，次六曰乂用三德，次七曰明用稽疑，次八曰念用庶徵，次九曰嚮用五福，威用六極。」夫五行者，天之道也；五事者，人之故也；八政者，人之所以因乎天也；五紀者，天之所以示乎人也；皇極者，君之所以建極也；三德者，治之所以應變也；稽疑者，以人而聽於天也；庶徵者，推天而徵之人也；福極者，人感而天應也。聖人傳心之法，帝王致治之要，莫加焉矣。故西山真氏曰：「洪範九疇，六十有五字耳，而天道人事無不該焉。原其本，皆自人君一身始。」信哉言乎！
夫由天之人，而其理則已明；自一之九，而其數則已具。蔡沈乃曰：「易更四聖而象已著，範錫神禹而數不傳。」於是作《洪範內篇》八十一卦，以方圓擬圖，以九九積數，以為體天地之撰者，易之象；紀天地之撰者，易之
translation_en:
…says: “First, the Five Phases; second, the reverent employment of the Five Activities; third, the diligent employment of the Eight Affairs of Government; fourth, the harmonizing employment of the Five Regulators of Time; fifth, the establishment of the August Standard; sixth, the governing employment of the Three Virtues; seventh, the discerning employment of the Examination of Doubts; eighth, the attentive employment of the Various Verifications; ninth, the encouraging employment of the Five Blessings and the deterrent employment of the Six Extremities.”
The Five Phases are the Way of Heaven; the Five Activities are the affairs of human beings. The Eight Affairs of Government are the means by which human beings follow Heaven; the Five Regulators of Time are the means by which Heaven gives indications to human beings. The August Standard is the means by which the ruler establishes the supreme standard; the Three Virtues are the means by which government responds to changing circumstances. The Examination of Doubts means listening to Heaven from the human standpoint; the Various Verifications mean investigating Heaven and seeking corroboration in human affairs. The Blessings and Extremities mean that human beings elicit a response and Heaven answers. Nothing surpasses these as the method by which sages transmit their understanding or as the essentials by which emperors and kings achieve good government. Thus Master Zhen of Xishan said: “The nine categories of the Great Plan comprise only sixty-five characters, yet there is nothing in the Way of Heaven or human affairs that they do not encompass. If we trace them to their root, all begin with the ruler’s own person.” How true these words are!
Now, proceeding from Heaven to human beings [?], their principles are already clear; proceeding from one to nine, their numbers are already complete. Yet Cai Shen said: “The Changes passed through four sages, and its images were made manifest; the Great Plan was bestowed upon the divine Yu, but its numbers were not transmitted.” Thereupon he composed the eighty-one configurations of the Inner Chapters on the Great Plan (Hongfan neipian), using squares and circles to devise diagrams and multiplying nine by nine to generate numbers. He held that what embodies the workings of Heaven and Earth is the imagery of the Changes; what orders the workings of Heaven and Earth is the Changes’ …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
數數者始於一象者成於二一者奇二者
偶奇者數之所以行偶者象之所以立故
二而四四而八者八卦之象也一而三三
而九者九疇之數也由是重之八八而六
十四六十四而四千九十六而象備矣九
九而八十一八十一而六千五百六十一
而數周矣其卦始於原濳守信訖於固移
墮終大抵專主於數以闡洛書之秘兼言
其象以比河圖之彰漢儒所謂河圖洛書
===
相為經緯八卦九章相為表裏者於是而
明之矣豈其數之不傳哉至於以溟漠之
間朕兆之先言數之原以有儀有象判一
而兩言數之分以日月星辰山嶽川澤言
數之著以四時五氣風雷雨露萬物形色
言數之化以君臣父子夫婦長幼朋友言
數之教以九野九州九品九族九禮九樂
九刑九筮九職九賦九府九服九命九儀
九法九貢之類言數之度以孔子告哀公
punctuated: 數。數者始於一，象者成於二。一者奇，二者偶。奇者數之所以行，偶者象之所以立。故二而四，四而八者，八卦之象也；一而三，三而九者，九疇之數也。由是重之，八八而六十四，六十四而四千九十六，而象備矣；九九而八十一，八十一而六千五百六十一，而數周矣。其卦始於原、濳、守、信，訖於固、移、墮、終。大抵專主於數，以闡洛書之秘，兼言其象，以比河圖之彰。漢儒所謂「河圖洛書相為經緯，八卦九章相為表裏」者，於是而明之矣。豈其數之不傳哉？至於以溟漠之間、朕兆之先言數之原，以有儀有象、判一而兩言數之分，以日月星辰、山嶽川澤言數之著，以四時五氣、風雷雨露、萬物形色言數之化，以君臣父子、夫婦長幼朋友言數之教，以九野九州、九品九族、九禮九樂、九刑九筮、九職九賦、九府九服、九命九儀、九法九貢之類言數之度，以孔子告哀公
translation_en:
…numbers. Numbers begin with one; images take form with two. One is odd; two is even. Oddness is what enables numbers to operate; evenness is what enables images to be established. Thus, proceeding from two to four and from four to eight gives the images of the eight trigrams; proceeding from one to three and from three to nine gives the numbers of the nine categories. By repeatedly combining these, eight times eight yields sixty-four, and sixty-four squared yields four thousand ninety-six: the images are then complete. Nine times nine yields eighty-one, and eighty-one squared yields six thousand five hundred sixty-one: the numbers are then comprehensive. His configurations begin with Yuan, Qian, Shou, and Xin, and end with Gu, Yi, Duo, and Zhong. In general, he concentrates on numbers to elucidate the mysteries of the Luo Writing, while also discussing their images to match the manifest patterns of the River Chart. The Han Confucians’ statement that “the River Chart and the Luo Writing serve as warp and weft to one another, and the eight trigrams and nine sections serve as exterior and interior to one another” is thereby clarified. How, then, could its numbers have failed to be transmitted?

As for his account, he discusses the origin of numbers in terms of the undifferentiated obscurity before any signs appear; their division in terms of the emergence of forms and images, with the one divided into two; their manifestation in terms of the sun, moon, stars, and constellations, mountains, rivers, and marshes; their transformations in terms of the four seasons and five forms of vital energy, wind, thunder, rain, and dew, and the shapes and colors of the myriad things; their instruction in terms of ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, and friends; and their measures in terms of such groupings as the nine celestial regions, nine provinces, nine grades, nine kinship groups, nine rites, nine kinds of music, nine punishments, nine methods of milfoil divination, nine occupations, nine levies, nine treasuries, nine service zones, nine ranks of appointment, nine ceremonial forms, nine regulations, and nine kinds of tribute. He then invokes what Confucius told Duke Ai…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
爲天下國家有九經所以行之者一而歸
之太極雖即理以明數其於洪範皇極之
理天人之道豈復有加也哉特儒者之學
不可以不講耳故先臣丘濬曰洪範者天
人之學也爲學而究乎此則能貫通天人
之理而爲學問之極功爲治而原乎此則
能和同天人之際而爲聖神之能事不其
然乎夫有禹之神智而後洪範之道昭有
商之仁聖而後洪範之旨存有武王之聰
===
明而後洪範之理悉是故三聖相授而其
守一三代相統而其治同秦漢而下蓋弗
究乎此矣洪惟我
太祖皇帝以
聖神文武之資接虞夏商周之統稽古正學顯
道神德故一讀尚書洪範而即歎其爲天
人之至理聖學之淵源於是特命儒臣表
揭座右朝夕觀覽乃親操
宸翰加以註疏
punctuated:
爲天下國家有九經，所以行之者一，而歸之太極，雖即理以明數，其於《洪範》皇極之理、天人之道，豈復有加也哉？特儒者之學不可以不講耳。故先臣丘濬曰：「洪範者，天人之學也。爲學而究乎此，則能貫通天人之理，而爲學問之極功；爲治而原乎此，則能和同天人之際，而爲聖神之能事。」不其然乎？夫有禹之神智，而後《洪範》之道昭；有商之仁聖，而後《洪範》之旨存；有武王之聰明，而後《洪範》之理悉。是故三聖相授而其守一，三代相統而其治同。秦漢而下，蓋弗究乎此矣。
洪惟我太祖皇帝，以聖神文武之資，接虞夏商周之統，稽古正學，顯道神德。故一讀《尚書》《洪範》，而即歎其爲天人之至理、聖學之淵源。於是特命儒臣表揭座右，朝夕觀覽，乃親操宸翰，加以註疏。
translation_en:
…there are nine guiding principles for governing all under Heaven, states, and families, but that by which they are put into practice is one; and he traces this back to the Supreme Ultimate. Although this elucidates numbers through principle, how could it add anything to the principle of the August Standard in the Great Plan, or to the Way of Heaven and humanity? It is simply something that students of Confucian learning cannot leave unexamined. Thus the late minister Qiu Jun said: “The Great Plan is the learning of Heaven and humanity. If, in pursuing learning, one investigates it thoroughly, one can comprehend the principles of Heaven and humanity as a connected whole and attain the highest achievement of scholarship. If, in governing, one takes it as the foundation, one can bring harmony to the relations between Heaven and humanity and accomplish the work of sagely and spiritual wisdom.” Is this not indeed so? Only with Yu’s spiritual wisdom was the Way of the Great Plan made manifest; only with the humane sage of Shang was its purport preserved; and only with King Wu’s perceptiveness were its principles fully understood. Thus the three sages transmitted it to one another, and what they upheld was one; the Three Dynasties succeeded one another, and their governance was alike. From the Qin and Han onward, however, it seems that this was no longer thoroughly investigated.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu, endowed with sagely and spiritual wisdom and civil and martial excellence, inherited the succession of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou. He examined antiquity, rectified learning, manifested the Way, and made his virtue wondrous. Thus, upon reading the Great Plan in the Book of Documents just once, he immediately praised it as the ultimate principles of Heaven and humanity and the wellspring of sagely learning. He therefore specially ordered his Confucian ministers to display it beside his seat, so that he could consult it morning and evening. He then personally took up the imperial brush and supplied annotations and explanations.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖謨洋洋嘉言孔彰真有以繼往聖之絕學開
萬世之太平矣何其盛哉又甞伏誦
召諭賛善劉三吾有曰朕觀洪範一篇帝王
為治之要道也所以敘彝倫立皇極保萬民
序四時成百穀本於天道而驗於人事箕子
為武王陳之武王猶自謙曰五帝之道我未
能焉朕每為惕然遂疏其旨是則
聖祖之於洪範蓋不徒註而實神會理解身體
力行故以之立言則煥乎其有文章以之
===
致治則巍巍乎其有成功惟天為大惟堯
則之其是之謂乎然愚又有說焉夫洪範
之旨莫大於敘倫敘倫之事莫切於建極
故箕子衍五之一疇尤拳拳焉其曰皇建
其有極斂時五福用敷錫厥庶民又曰皇
極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓則是君之
建極于上者以為民也故曰天子作民父
母以為天下王其曰惟時厥庶民于汝極
錫汝保極又曰凡厥庶民極之敷言是訓
punctuated:
聖謨洋洋，嘉言孔彰，真有以繼往聖之絕學，開萬世之太平矣。何其盛哉！又甞伏誦召諭賛善劉三吾，有曰：「朕觀洪範一篇，帝王為治之要道也。所以敘彝倫、立皇極、保萬民、序四時、成百穀，本於天道而驗於人事。箕子為武王陳之，武王猶自謙曰：『五帝之道，我未能焉。』朕每為惕然，遂疏其旨。」是則聖祖之於洪範，蓋不徒註，而實神會理解、身體力行。故以之立言，則煥乎其有文章；以之致治，則巍巍乎其有成功。「惟天為大，惟堯則之」，其是之謂乎？
然愚又有說焉。夫洪範之旨，莫大於敘倫；敘倫之事，莫切於建極。故箕子衍五之一疇，尤拳拳焉。其曰：「皇建其有極，斂時五福，用敷錫厥庶民。」又曰：「皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。」則是君之建極于上者，以為民也。故曰：「天子作民父母，以為天下王。」其曰：「惟時厥庶民，于汝極，錫汝保極。」又曰：「凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓
translation_en:
…His sagely counsels were abundant, his excellent words brilliantly manifest. Truly they could carry forward the interrupted learning of the sages of old and inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations. How magnificent! I have also reverently read the instructions he delivered when summoning Liu Sanwu, Adviser to the Heir Apparent: “I regard the ‘Great Plan’ (Hongfan) as the essential Way by which emperors and kings govern. Its means of ordering the constant human relationships, establishing the royal standard, protecting the myriad people, regulating the four seasons, and bringing the many grains to maturity are rooted in the Way of Heaven and verified in human affairs. Jizi expounded it to King Wu, yet King Wu modestly said, ‘I have not yet attained the Way of the Five Emperors.’ Whenever I reflect upon this, I am filled with apprehension; thus I have elucidated its meaning.” Our sagely founder’s engagement with the ‘Great Plan,’ then, was not merely a matter of annotation: he apprehended its spirit, understood its principles, embodied them personally, and earnestly put them into practice. Thus, when he drew upon it to set forth his teachings, his writings shone brilliantly; when he drew upon it to achieve good government, his accomplishments towered magnificently. “Heaven alone is great; Yao alone modeled himself upon it”—does this not describe him?
Yet I, in my humble judgment, have something further to say. No purpose of the ‘Great Plan’ is greater than ordering human relationships, and nothing is more essential to ordering those relationships than establishing the standard. Hence, when Jizi elaborated the fifth category, he was especially earnest. It says: “Let the sovereign establish his standard, gather these five blessings, and distribute them widely among his common people.” It also says: “The broadly proclaimed words of the royal standard are constant norms and instruction; they are the instruction of the Lord on High.” Thus, the ruler’s establishment of the standard above is for the sake of the people. Hence it says: “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, thereby becoming king of all under Heaven.” It says: “Then your common people will turn to your standard; they will enable you to preserve that standard.” It also says: “All the common people, regarding the broadly proclaimed words of the standard, take them as instruction…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是行以近天子之光則是民之保極于下
者以從君也故曰會其有極歸其有極夫
君民同極則彞倫叙彞倫叙則天地位而
萬物育矣故本之以五行敬之以五事厚
之以八政恊之以五紀者皇極之所以建
也乂之以三德明之以稽疑驗之以庶徵
勸懲之以福極者皇極之所以行也然以
五事參五行者其天人之大際乎以一敬
脩五事者其建極之大本乎故曰敬所以
===
誠身也故人君能恭以作肅則貌脩矣從
以作乂則言脩矣明以作哲則視脩矣哲
以作謀則聽脩矣睿以作聖則思脩矣貌
脩則水得其序而時雨若焉言脩則火得
其序而時暘若焉視脩則木得其序而時
燠若焉聽脩則金得其序而時寒若焉思
脩則土得其序而時風若焉夫五行旣得
其序則萬物無不各得其所矣故漢書載
五行咎徵曰田獵不宿飲食不享出入不
punctuated: 是行，以近天子之光」，則是民之保極于下者，以從君也。故曰：「會其有極，歸其有極。」夫君民同極則彞倫叙，彞倫叙則天地位而萬物育矣。故本之以五行，敬之以五事，厚之以八政，恊之以五紀者，皇極之所以建也；乂之以三德，明之以稽疑，驗之以庶徵，勸懲之以福極者，皇極之所以行也。然以五事參五行者，其天人之大際乎？以一敬脩五事者，其建極之大本乎？故曰：「敬所以誠身也。」故人君能恭以作肅，則貌脩矣；從以作乂，則言脩矣；明以作哲，則視脩矣；哲以作謀，則聽脩矣；睿以作聖，則思脩矣。貌脩則水得其序，而時雨若焉；言脩則火得其序，而時暘若焉；視脩則木得其序，而時燠若焉；聽脩則金得其序，而時寒若焉；思脩則土得其序，而時風若焉。夫五行旣得其序，則萬物無不各得其所矣。故《漢書》載五行咎徵曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不
translation_en: …and put it into practice, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven.” This means that the people below uphold the supreme standard in order to follow their ruler. Thus it says: “Gather around that supreme standard; return to that supreme standard.” When ruler and people share the same supreme standard, the enduring human relationships are properly ordered; when these relationships are properly ordered, Heaven and Earth take their proper places and the myriad things flourish. Thus, grounding it in the Five Phases, attending to it reverently through the Five Affairs, enriching it through the Eight Affairs of Government, and harmonizing it through the Five Regulators of Time are the means by which the August Supreme Standard is established. Governing through the Three Virtues, clarifying matters through the Examination of Doubts, testing them through the Various Signs, and encouraging and chastening through blessings and calamities are the means by which the August Supreme Standard is put into effect. Yet is not correlating the Five Affairs with the Five Phases the great point of connection between Heaven and humanity? Is not cultivating the Five Affairs through undivided reverence the great foundation for establishing the supreme standard? Thus it says: “Reverence is the means of making oneself sincere.” If the ruler can achieve solemnity through respectfulness, his demeanor will be cultivated; if he achieves order through compliance, his speech will be cultivated; if he achieves discernment through clarity, his sight will be cultivated; if he achieves deliberation through discernment, his hearing will be cultivated; and if he achieves sageliness through perspicacity, his thought will be cultivated. When demeanor is cultivated, water attains its proper order, and timely rain responds accordingly. When speech is cultivated, fire attains its proper order, and timely sunshine responds accordingly. When sight is cultivated, wood attains its proper order, and timely warmth responds accordingly. When hearing is cultivated, metal attains its proper order, and timely cold responds accordingly. When thought is cultivated, earth attains its proper order, and timely wind responds accordingly. Once the Five Phases have attained their proper order, all the myriad things attain their proper places. Thus the Book of Han records the baleful signs of the Five Phases, saying: “When hunting is conducted without overnight lodging [?], when food and drink are taken without offerings, when going out and coming in are not…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
節奪民農時及有姦謀則木不曲直曰棄
法律逐功臣奪嫡立庶則火不炎上曰治
宮室飭臺榭內淫亂犯親戚侮父兄則稼
穡不成曰好戰攻輕百姓飭城郭侵邊境
則金不從革曰簡宗廟不禱祠廢祭祀逆
天時則水不潤下凡若此者雖涉春秋事
應之詞陰陽災異之說要之敬怠之幾感
應之理不可誣也觀
聖祖諭疏範之意首言敘彝倫立皇極次言保
===
萬民序四時成百穀而終之以惕然之一
語則又知
聖人之所以立極於天下者有敬以為之本焉
矣非
睿智聰明剛健中正明於天之道而察於人
之故者能如是乎故神蔡之真圖丹書之
秘旨肇於夏傳於周微於歷代而興於我
朝
鴻休盛化廣大高明遐哉邈乎不可及焉
punctuated:
節，奪民農時，及有姦謀，則木不曲直。曰：「棄法律，逐功臣，奪嫡立庶，則火不炎上。」曰：「治宮室，飭臺榭，內淫亂，犯親戚，侮父兄，則稼穡不成。」曰：「好戰攻，輕百姓，飭城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。」曰：「簡宗廟，不禱祠，廢祭祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。」凡若此者，雖涉春秋事應之詞、陰陽災異之說，要之，敬怠之幾、感應之理，不可誣也。
觀聖祖諭疏範之意，首言敘彝倫、立皇極，次言保萬民、序四時、成百穀，而終之以惕然之一語，則又知聖人之所以立極於天下者，有敬以為之本焉矣。非睿智聰明、剛健中正、明於天之道而察於人之故者，能如是乎？故神蔡之真圖、丹書之秘旨，肇於夏，傳於周，微於歷代，而興於我朝。鴻休盛化，廣大高明，遐哉邈乎，不可及焉！
translation_en:
…without restraint, deprive the people of their time for farming, and engage in treacherous schemes, then wood fails to bend and straighten. It says: “If laws are abandoned, meritorious ministers expelled, and the heir by the principal wife displaced in favor of a son by a secondary consort, then fire fails to blaze upward.” It says: “If palaces and chambers are built, terraces and pavilions embellished, sexual disorder prevails within, relatives are violated, and fathers and elder brothers are treated with contempt, then crops fail to mature.” It says: “If rulers delight in warfare and attack, treat the common people lightly, strengthen city walls, and invade frontier territories, then metal fails to yield to transformation.” It says: “If ancestral temples are neglected, prayers are not offered, sacrifices are abandoned, and Heaven’s seasons are contravened, then water fails to moisten and descend.” Although statements such as these involve accounts of events and their corresponding portents in the Spring and Autumn period, and theories of calamities and anomalies arising from yin and yang, their essential point cannot be denied: reverence and negligence have incipient consequences, and stimulus and response follow a principle.
Considering the intent of the Sage Founder’s instruction elucidating the Great Plan [?], we see that it begins by speaking of ordering the constant human relationships and establishing the August Ultimate; it next speaks of protecting the myriad people, ordering the four seasons, and bringing the various grains to maturity; and it concludes with the single expression “vigilant apprehension.” Thus we further understand that reverence is the foundation upon which the sage establishes the ultimate standard for all under Heaven. Could anyone accomplish this without being discerning, wise, perceptive, strong, steadfast, balanced, and upright, understanding the Way of Heaven and examining the circumstances of human affairs? Thus the authentic diagram borne by the divine tortoise and the hidden purport of the cinnabar writing originated in the Xia, were transmitted in the Zhou, faded through successive dynasties, and flourished anew under our dynasty. Its immense blessings and abundant transforming influence are vast and lofty, far-reaching and remote—beyond all comparison!

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成祖文皇帝
繼統承天弘文闡化又取洪範內篇輯性理
書頒布學校佑啓人文卓乎錫極保民敷
言帝訓之義故
功光
聖祖業垂
嗣世今
上建極益勤古訓篤茂
前烈本敬一以爲化理之源合天人而盡倫
===
制之善泰道重煕福德累洽蓋不出善繼
善述之孝而有以成會極歸極之化矣書
曰有典有則以詒子孫詩曰儀式刑文王
之典日靖四方請以是爲
今日頌
第二問
王燾
同考試官教諭石批說我
天朝親親之仁忠厚之澤藹然可觀而抹偏起弊處置得宜足見實
punctuated:
成祖文皇帝繼統承天，弘文闡化，又取《洪範內篇》，輯《性理》書，頒布學校，佑啓人文，卓乎錫極保民、敷言帝訓之義。故功光聖祖，業垂嗣世。今上建極益勤，古訓篤茂前烈，本敬一以爲化理之源，合天人而盡倫制之善，泰道重煕，福德累洽。蓋不出善繼善述之孝，而有以成會極歸極之化矣。《書》曰：「有典有則，以詒子孫。」《詩》曰：「儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。」請以是爲今日頌。
第二問
王燾
同考試官教諭石批：說我天朝親親之仁、忠厚之澤，藹然可觀；而抹偏起弊，處置得宜，足見實
translation_en:
Emperor Wen, Chengzu, succeeded to the imperial line and received Heaven’s mandate. He promoted learning and spread transforming instruction. He also drew upon the Inner Chapters on the Great Plan (Hongfan neipian) and compiled the book on Nature and Principle (Xingli), distributing it to the schools to foster and advance human culture. This splendidly embodied the meaning of bestowing the supreme standard and protecting the people, and of setting forth imperial instruction. Thus his achievements brought glory to the sagely founding emperor, and his work was bequeathed to succeeding generations. Our present sovereign is ever more diligent in establishing the supreme standard; through the ancient teachings, he further enriches the glorious achievements of his predecessors. He takes reverent single-mindedness as the source of moral transformation and good government, unites Heaven and humanity, and brings human relationships and institutions to their fullest excellence. The way of peace flourishes anew, and blessings and virtue spread in abundance. All this proceeds from the filial devotion that skillfully carries forward predecessors’ undertakings and intentions, thereby bringing about a transformation in which all gather around and turn toward the supreme standard. The Book of Documents says: “There are established ordinances and rules to bequeath to descendants.” The Book of Odes says: “Follow and emulate King Wen’s statutes, daily bringing peace to the four quarters.” Let me offer these words in praise of the present reign.
Second Policy Question
Wang Tao
Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: His account vividly presents our heavenly dynasty’s benevolence in cherishing its imperial kinsmen and the gracious benefits of its loyalty and generosity. In addressing partiality and abuses [?], his proposed measures are appropriate, amply demonstrating practical …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
學
考試官敎諭陳批
國朝封建宗室功臣之事仁義相維之道也此作區畫曲盡事宜
老成長慮可以占適用之才矣
考試官學正陳批說盡親親賢賢之典允
宜高薦
帝王親親報功之道仁義而已矣何也仁
以篤恩也恩篤則情維而天下之元氣固
義以正法也法正則度昭而天下之神氣
===
振茲二者皆不可倚也昔者先王之創業
垂統也體國經野列藩建侯財親疎之宜
定大小之等宗庶星羅豪傑並奮將與天
下同其安而享其樂者豈止固磐石之基
哉抑亦親賢之心固有所不能自已耳是
故堯睦九族而急尊賢周厚本支而庸旦
仲成湯以有衆而成南巢之舉武王以十
臣而致牧野之功溥恩弘制並行不悖三
代以後稱得統者莫如漢焉漢高得國之
punctuated:
學。
考試官敎諭陳批：國朝封建宗室功臣之事，仁義相維之道也。此作區畫曲盡事宜，老成長慮，可以占適用之才矣。
考試官學正陳批：說盡親親賢賢之典，允宜高薦。
帝王親親報功之道，仁義而已矣。何也？仁以篤恩也，恩篤則情維，而天下之元氣固；義以正法也，法正則度昭，而天下之神氣振。茲二者皆不可倚也。昔者先王之創業垂統也，體國經野，列藩建侯，財親疎之宜，定大小之等，宗庶星羅，豪傑並奮。將與天下同其安而享其樂者，豈止固磐石之基哉？抑亦親賢之心，固有所不能自已耳。是故堯睦九族而急尊賢，周厚本支而庸旦仲，成湯以有衆而成南巢之舉，武王以十臣而致牧野之功。溥恩弘制，並行不悖。三代以後，稱得統者，莫如漢焉。漢高得國之
translation_en:
…learning.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: Our dynasty’s enfeoffment of imperial clansmen and meritorious officials embodies the way in which benevolence and righteousness sustain one another. This composition’s proposals address every aspect of the practical circumstances. Its mature judgment and farsighted deliberation reveal a talent suited to practical employment.
Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: This fully expounds the established principles of cherishing one’s kin and honoring the worthy. It certainly deserves recommendation with a high ranking.
The way in which emperors and kings cherish their kin and reward meritorious service consists simply of benevolence and righteousness. Why is this? Benevolence deepens gracious favor: when favor is deep, bonds of affection hold firm, and the vital energy of all under Heaven is secured. Righteousness rectifies the laws: when the laws are correct, standards are manifest, and the spirit of all under Heaven is invigorated. Neither of these two may receive one-sided emphasis. In former times, when the ancient kings founded their enterprises and transmitted their rule, they laid out the capital and demarcated the countryside, established regional bulwarks and enfeoffed lords, assessed what was appropriate for closer and more distant kin, and determined distinctions between greater and lesser domains. The principal and collateral lineages were arrayed like stars, and outstanding men rose together to exert themselves. In seeking to share peace and enjoyment with all under Heaven, were they merely securing a foundation as firm as a great rock? Their affection for kin and regard for the worthy were also feelings they could not restrain. Thus Yao brought harmony to the nine degrees of kinship and made honoring the worthy an urgent concern; the Zhou generously supported the main and collateral branches of their lineage and employed Dan and Zhong [?]. Cheng Tang, through having the support of the multitude, accomplished the expedition to Nanchao; King Wu, through his ten ministers, achieved victory at Muye. Extending favor broadly and enlarging institutions proceeded together without conflict. After the Three Dynasties, none surpassed the Han among those said to have secured the legitimate succession. When Gaozu of Han acquired the realm…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
初戒孤立之弊割裂强土大封功臣尊王
子孫而封建之義備矣故班固作漢書著
諸侯王表以究漢家强弱之變著異姓諸
侯王表以戒暴秦棄賢之非著王子侯表
與功臣及恩澤侯表則又無非所以隆支
庶重輔弼辨功能固本章化以爲後人勸
焉馳騁古今上下數百載誠有得於古之
道矣然王者親賢仁義之實則固或未盡
也我
===
太祖高皇帝平定中原大啓分封延選天下儒
俊以充輔導而又著
儲君昭鑒錄以教
諸王故賢哲輝映用承永休而當時貔虎鷹
揚之士感風雲之會以成廓清之功者亦
皆封爵申盟親賢並建思深慮遠恩溥德
弘盖上埒虞周而漢代不足言矣劉向曰
公族者國之枝葉枝葉落而本根無所庇
蔭故根盛而葉茂源深而流長者理也今
punctuated:
初，戒孤立之弊，割裂强土，大封功臣，尊王子孫，而封建之義備矣。故班固作《漢書》，著《諸侯王表》，以究漢家强弱之變；著《異姓諸侯王表》，以戒暴秦棄賢之非；著《王子侯表》與《功臣及恩澤侯表》，則又無非所以隆支庶、重輔弼、辨功能、固本章化，以爲後人勸焉。馳騁古今，上下數百載，誠有得於古之道矣。然王者親賢仁義之實，則固或未盡也。
我太祖高皇帝平定中原，大啓分封，延選天下儒俊以充輔導，而又著《儲君昭鑒錄》以教諸王。故賢哲輝映，用承永休。而當時貔虎鷹揚之士，感風雲之會，以成廓清之功者，亦皆封爵申盟。親賢並建，思深慮遠，恩溥德弘，盖上埒虞周，而漢代不足言矣。劉向曰：「公族者，國之枝葉。枝葉落，而本根無所庇蔭。」故根盛而葉茂，源深而流長者，理也。今
translation_en:
…at the outset, he guarded against the dangers of standing alone, divided up powerful territories [?], lavishly enfeoffed meritorious officials, and honored his sons and descendants by making them kings. Thus the principles of enfeoffment were fully realized. Accordingly, when Ban Gu compiled the History of the Han, he composed the “Table of the Feudatory Kings” to investigate changes in the strength and weakness of the Han ruling house; the “Table of the Feudatory Kings of Different Surnames” to warn against the error of violent Qin in rejecting worthy men; and the “Table of the Kings’ Sons Enfeoffed as Marquises,” together with the “Table of Marquises Enfeoffed for Merit and Imperial Favor,” all intended to exalt the collateral branches, give weight to supporting ministers, distinguish achievements and abilities, strengthen the foundation, and make moral transformation manifest, thereby encouraging later generations. Ranging across past and present, over several hundred years, he truly grasped something of the way of antiquity. Yet he may still not have fully encompassed the substance of a true king’s benevolence and righteousness in cherishing his kin and honoring the worthy.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao pacified the Central Plain and greatly expanded enfeoffment. He invited and selected outstanding Confucian scholars from throughout the realm to serve as advisers and instructors, and also composed the Record of the Shining Mirror for the Heir Apparent (Chujun zhaojian lu) to instruct the princes. Thus worthy and wise men lent one another brilliance, sustaining enduring blessings. The warriors of that time, fierce as tigers and soaring like hawks, who responded to the auspicious conjunction of ruler and ministers and accomplished the pacification of the realm, likewise all received noble titles and solemnly renewed covenants. Kin and worthy men were established together: his thought was profound, his foresight far-reaching, his favor widespread, and his virtue vast. Indeed, he ranked with Yu and Zhou of antiquity; the Han dynasty scarcely merits mention beside him. Liu Xiang said: “The ruling lineage is the branches and leaves of the state. When the branches and leaves fall, the trunk and roots have nothing to shelter them.” Thus luxuriant roots produce flourishing leaves, and deep sources produce long-flowing streams: this is the natural principle. Now …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國家宗室蕃衍其麗不億所以治平長久而
遠過周曆者正在於此然祿予日增田賦
有額支費不足後將何繼說者有謂立學
以開仕籍者矣然科目雜於羣臣之列恐
未安也有謂分派以立公籍者矣然差賦
混於凡民之中恐難行也或許自試以效
才能或許諸王自主婚姻不以德義相維
而以親戚相制則又恐非可久之策傷恩
則失本廢法則貽憂矣我
===
國家之大典洪猷盡倫盡制夫孰得而擬之
哉愚以為
宗藩之祿自弘治中會議之後
親王
郡王自有畫一之規本色折色已備中正之
制會典品序之等具在諫垣駁奏之疏見
存而或有變更者非舊法也今當原其定
祿之典而及其缺欠之由考其等殺之差
以察其冒濫之弊於其所當裁者節以成
punctuated: 國家宗室蕃衍，其麗不億，所以治平長久而遠過周曆者，正在於此。然祿予日增，田賦有額，支費不足，後將何繼？說者有謂立學以開仕籍者矣，然科目雜於羣臣之列，恐未安也。有謂分派以立公籍者矣，然差賦混於凡民之中，恐難行也。或許自試以效才能，或許諸王自主婚姻，不以德義相維，而以親戚相制，則又恐非可久之策。傷恩則失本，廢法則貽憂矣。我國家之大典洪猷，盡倫盡制，夫孰得而擬之哉？愚以為，宗藩之祿，自弘治中會議之後，親王、郡王自有畫一之規，本色、折色已備中正之制。《會典》品序之等具在，諫垣駁奏之疏見存，而或有變更者，非舊法也。今當原其定祿之典，而及其缺欠之由，考其等殺之差，以察其冒濫之弊。於其所當裁者，節以成
translation_en:
The imperial clan of our dynasty has multiplied beyond counting. It is precisely here that the basis lies for lasting peace and orderly government, and for a dynastic span far exceeding that of Zhou. Yet stipend payments increase daily, while land-tax revenue has a fixed limit. If funds are insufficient to meet expenditure, how will payments be sustained in the future? Some commentators propose establishing schools to open access to official careers. Yet for clan members to enter through the examination system and mingle in the ranks of the ministers seems inappropriate. Others propose dividing them into branches and placing them on public registers [?]. Yet mingling them with ordinary commoners for service obligations and taxation would, I fear, be difficult to implement. Some would allow them to prove themselves and put their talents to use; others would allow the princes to arrange their own marriages. Binding them through the constraints of kinship rather than maintaining their bonds through virtue and righteousness would, I fear, offer no enduring policy. To injure familial affection is to lose the foundation; to abandon the law is to bequeath trouble. The great institutions and grand policies of our dynasty fully embody the proper human relationships and institutional arrangements. Who could presume to devise their equal?

In my humble view, since the deliberations held during the Hongzhi reign, uniform rules have governed the stipends of princes and commandery princes, and balanced provisions already exist for payments in kind and their commuted equivalents. The gradations of rank are fully recorded in the Collected Statutes, and the remonstrance officials’ memorials contesting proposals remain extant. Any alterations that may have occurred do not represent the established law. We should now trace the original regulations fixing stipends and investigate the causes of shortfalls and arrears, examining the gradations in entitlement to detect abuses involving fraudulent claims and excessive awards. Where reductions are warranted, expenditure should be restrained according to established…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
規不敢過焉於其所當供者處以其時不
敢後焉若會典品序之意時當變通則辨
以九族紀以五宗量為差殺以開其自給
之道亦或一道耳至若今之王官乏遠大
之志而輔導之德匡弼之忠不多見焉是
蓋臣下之過非職輕之故也今當重俊傑
之選求端良之士俾之久任成功而寵擢
加焉豈有長沙賈誼之嘆歟夫賈誼之疏
以定經制為本蓋以豪植太强漢法不得
===
行也通達國體稱忠讜矣今之王官有所
謂賈誼其人而不大用於時者乎吾未之
多見也昔者景帝用鼂錯之計武帝施主
父之策下推恩之令使諸侯王得分戶邑
於子孫諸臣之策已見行矣然鼂錯之計
褊而靡恩不足法也此說一行其後作左
官之律嚴附益之法方其縱恣也畏之同
敵國及其猜防也抑之如謫徙此亦非漢
之初法而其弊至此矣今王官舉察之條
punctuated: 規，不敢過焉；於其所當供者，處以其時，不敢後焉。若會典品序之意，時當變通，則辨以九族，紀以五宗，量為差殺，以開其自給之道，亦或一道耳。至若今之王官乏遠大之志，而輔導之德、匡弼之忠不多見焉，是蓋臣下之過，非職輕之故也。今當重俊傑之選，求端良之士，俾之久任成功，而寵擢加焉，豈有長沙賈誼之嘆歟？夫賈誼之疏，以定經制為本，蓋以豪植太强，漢法不得行也。通達國體，稱忠讜矣。今之王官，有所謂賈誼其人而不大用於時者乎？吾未之多見也。昔者景帝用鼂錯之計，武帝施主父之策，下推恩之令，使諸侯王得分戶邑於子孫，諸臣之策已見行矣。然鼂錯之計，褊而靡恩，不足法也。此說一行，其後作左官之律，嚴附益之法。方其縱恣也，畏之同敵國；及其猜防也，抑之如謫徙。此亦非漢之初法，而其弊至此矣。今王官舉察之條，
translation_en:
…the established regulations, not daring to exceed them; as for what must be supplied, arrange it at the proper time, not daring to fall behind. If the provisions on ranks in the Collected Statutes require adaptation to present circumstances, distinguish kinship according to the nine degrees of kin and organize descent according to the five lineage divisions, setting appropriately graded allowances to open a way for them to support themselves. This, too, might be one approach.

As for the present officials serving the princes, they lack far-reaching aspirations, and the virtue of guidance and the loyalty of corrective counsel are seldom seen among them. This is surely the fault of the servants, not a consequence of their offices carrying little weight. We should now attach importance to selecting outstanding men and seek upright and worthy scholars, allowing them to remain long in office and accomplish their work, and then bestowing favor and promotion upon them. How, then, could there be lamentations like those of Jia Yi in Changsha? Jia Yi’s memorial took the establishment of enduring institutions as its foundation, because the powerful magnates were too firmly entrenched [?] for the laws of the Han to be enforced. He understood the essential principles of governing the state and deserved to be called loyal and forthright. Among today’s officials serving the princes, are there men comparable to Jia Yi who have not been given important employment in their own time? I have not seen many.

Formerly, Emperor Jing adopted Chao Cuo’s plan, and Emperor Wu implemented Zhufu’s proposal, issuing the decree for extending imperial favor so that the princes could divide the households and territories of their fiefs among their sons and grandsons. The proposals of these ministers were thus put into practice. Yet Chao Cuo’s plan was narrow-minded and devoid of benevolence, and is unworthy of emulation. Once this approach was adopted, the statute against serving the princes was subsequently enacted, and the law against attaching oneself to them and augmenting their power was made stricter. When the princes were allowed free rein, they were feared like rival states; when they became objects of suspicion and precaution, they were held down like banished convicts. This, too, was not the original system of the Han, yet its abuses reached this point. Now, the regulations for recommending and scrutinizing officials serving the princes…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
憲臣一體行之輔衞臧否之實監司一體
治之皆所以培旣茂之休而思衍其盛蓋
將以廣仁固本也而豈以蹈釁也哉陸機
曰弘海惟川崇山惟壤明明衆哲同濟天
網夫錫爵報功君上之恩也盡職承業烈
士之忠也今世祿之子藉慶門資因仍習
俗罕有先哲之風豈異才無從見哉抑亦
不學之過與處之未盡其道也卽今武學
雖存未見禮射之敎武舉雖設尚襲叨冒
===
之風考課校才何繇得其實用哉夫武舉
始於唐而郭子儀輩大勳偉績身係安危
皆此途出焉不可槩謂無其人也但人之
才各有所長而其長各有所用長於弓矢
者或守禦之無策長於運籌者或劔戟之
未閑若專限以弓馬一夫之勇則智出萬
人之敵皆遺之矣故唐薛謙光曰夫武能
制敵祗尚弓矢使樊噲居蕭何之任必失
指蹤之機使蕭何入戲下之軍亦無免主
punctuated: 憲臣一體行之，輔衞臧否之實，監司一體治之，皆所以培旣茂之休而思衍其盛，蓋將以廣仁固本也，而豈以蹈釁也哉？陸機曰：「弘海惟川，崇山惟壤，明明衆哲，同濟天網。」夫錫爵報功，君上之恩也；盡職承業，烈士之忠也。今世祿之子，藉慶門資，因仍習俗，罕有先哲之風，豈異才無從見哉？抑亦不學之過與處之未盡其道也。卽今武學雖存，未見禮射之敎；武舉雖設，尚襲叨冒之風。考課校才，何繇得其實用哉？夫武舉始於唐，而郭子儀輩，大勳偉績，身係安危，皆此途出焉，不可槩謂無其人也。但人之才各有所長，而其長各有所用。長於弓矢者，或守禦之無策；長於運籌者，或劔戟之未閑。若專限以弓馬一夫之勇，則智出萬人之敵，皆遺之矣。故唐薛謙光曰：「夫武能制敵，祗尚弓矢，使樊噲居蕭何之任，必失指蹤之機；使蕭何入戲下之軍，亦無免主
translation_en:
…the censorial officials implement them uniformly; the surveillance commissioners likewise investigate the actual merits and faults of the princely advisers and guards. These measures all nurture an already flourishing excellence and seek to extend its prosperity. Their purpose is to spread benevolence and secure the foundations; how could it be to invite discord? Lu Ji said: “Rivers enlarge the sea; soil raises mountains. The illustrious company of wise men together sustain Heaven’s ordering net.” Bestowing noble rank to reward achievement is the sovereign’s grace; fulfilling one’s duties and carrying on an inherited charge is the loyal service of men of resolve.
