Nowadays, the sons of families holding hereditary emoluments rely on the advantages of their fortunate lineage and follow established habits and customs; few possess the spirit of the wise men of old. Is it that exceptional talent has no means of making itself known? Or is this also the fault of their failure to study, and of a failure to deal with them in the proper way? Today, although military schools exist, instruction in ritual archery is nowhere evident; although military examinations have been established, the practice of improperly obtaining qualifications persists. How can assessments of performance and evaluations of talent yield men of practical usefulness?

Military examinations began under the Tang. Men such as Guo Ziyi, whose great achievements and outstanding services made the realm’s security depend upon them, all emerged through this route. One cannot categorically say that it produces no worthy men. Yet each person has particular strengths, and each strength has its particular use. Those skilled with bows and arrows may lack plans for defense; those skilled in strategic planning may be unpracticed with swords and halberds. If selection is confined exclusively to archery and horsemanship—the courage of a single fighting man—then those whose intelligence makes them a match for ten thousand men will all be overlooked. Thus Xue Qianguang of the Tang said: “Military ability lies in overcoming the enemy, yet only skill with bows and arrows is valued. If Fan Kuai were placed in Xiao He’s position, he would surely fail to grasp the crucial task of directing operations; if Xiao He entered the army’s camp at Xi, neither would he succeed in saving his lord…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之效願降明制循名責實此責名實之論
也不亦可行矣乎至若天下所貴乎宿將
者以其起於微賤而望在四夷如漢韓信
衛青下拔行伍而陟大將之類是也若夫
蹈常襲故徒席先資以加於羣將之上歷
邊任者曾無寸勞薄效而幾幸遷易至有
地形山川未及知軍情土俗未及諳而復
去者則非計也故必宮府一體內外均重
爵祿之襲可仍其舊而關於營閫者不可
===
輕授也金帛之賜可隆以恩而關於邊境
者不可輕任也如此則材否以別擢任之
法斯過半矣昔宋淳熈中有以勳閥定遣
而臣僚建言則曰古之行法必自貴近始
捨貴近而行於疎遠則天下不服而法廢
矣自今除授未察其中否者許給舍繳駁
臺諫彈罷此察勳閥之議也不亦可行矣
乎是蓋念其鋒鏑之艱而求以安全之者
旣無不至則思翼戴之勤而盡所以培養
punctuated:
之效。願降明制，循名責實。」此責名實之論也，不亦可行矣乎？至若天下所貴乎宿將者，以其起於微賤而望在四夷，如漢韓信、衛青，下拔行伍而陟大將之類是也。若夫蹈常襲故，徒席先資，以加於羣將之上，歷邊任者曾無寸勞薄效，而幾幸遷易，至有地形山川未及知、軍情土俗未及諳而復去者，則非計也。故必宮府一體，內外均重。爵祿之襲，可仍其舊；而關於營閫者，不可輕授也。金帛之賜，可隆以恩；而關於邊境者，不可輕任也。如此則材否以別，擢任之法斯過半矣。
昔宋淳熈中，有以勳閥定遣，而臣僚建言則曰：「古之行法，必自貴近始。捨貴近而行於疎遠，則天下不服而法廢矣。自今除授未察其中否者，許給舍繳駁、臺諫彈罷。」此察勳閥之議也，不亦可行矣乎？是蓋念其鋒鏑之艱，而求以安全之者旣無不至，則思翼戴之勤，而盡所以培養
translation_en:
…the achievement of rescuing his lord. I ask that a clear decree be issued, requiring actual performance to match the stated designation.” This is an argument for holding men accountable for the correspondence between designation and performance. Could it not also be put into practice? As for the value the realm places upon veteran generals, it is because they rose from humble circumstances and acquired reputations among the peoples beyond the frontiers. Such were Han Xin and Wei Qing of the Han, men raised from the ranks to become great generals. But to follow established routines and precedents, relying solely on inherited standing to be placed above the other commanders, and then to pass through frontier appointments without the slightest service or achievement, hoping by good fortune to secure a transfer—so that some depart again before learning the terrain, mountains, and rivers, or becoming familiar with military conditions and local customs—is no sound policy. Thus the palace and the government must act as one, and service within and outside the capital must receive equal weight. The inheritance of titles and emoluments may continue as before, but military commands must not be granted lightly. Gifts of gold and silk may be made more generous as an expression of favor, but responsibilities concerning the frontiers must not be entrusted lightly. In this way, the capable and incapable will be distinguished, and the task of establishing proper promotion and appointment will be more than halfway accomplished.
Formerly, during the Chunxi reign of the Song, there were assignments determined by meritorious lineage [?], and officials submitted this proposal: “In antiquity, enforcement of the law necessarily began with the powerful and those close to the throne. If these are passed over and the law is enforced upon those distant from power, the realm will not submit, and the law will fall into disuse. Henceforth, when an appointment has been made without determining whether the appointee is suitable, Supervising Secretaries and Secretariat Drafters should be permitted to return and reject the appointment, and censorial and remonstrance officials should be permitted to impeach the appointee and secure his dismissal.” This is a proposal for scrutinizing men of meritorious lineage. Could it not also be put into practice? Thus, since every effort has been made to consider the hardships they endured amid blades and arrows and to seek their safety and preservation, one must also remember their devoted service in supporting the throne and exhaust every means of nurturing…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之者自不容於不周也已我
皇上禮樂明備教化大行推恩
宗室
詔補祿米而
敕賜慰勞屢有加焉至若納諸臣之請重錄元
勳之後追思鴻猷申嚴賞罰真所謂如天
地之於萬物愛養而曲成之者也愚嘗竊
謂元臣有非常之功則有非常之報
國家有無疆之業斯有無疆之休故觀三代
===
之利建藩屏保乂王家而一時君臣純佑
以治可知也已詩曰本支百世施於孫子
又曰思皇多士生此王國今
聖明在上敦本隆化協氣橫流含生庶類莫不
漸被膏澤而況世祿之子有不思自奮以
揚先德者非夫也天下
宗藩體道輸忠崇廣被之美宣緝熈之德以
共培億萬年無疆之休吾見功業配乎天
地雍熈比於唐虞皆仁義之化也執事以
punctuated: 之者，自不容於不周也已。我皇上禮樂明備，教化大行，推恩宗室，詔補祿米，而敕賜慰勞屢有加焉。至若納諸臣之請，重錄元勳之後，追思鴻猷，申嚴賞罰，真所謂如天地之於萬物，愛養而曲成之者也。愚嘗竊謂：元臣有非常之功，則有非常之報；國家有無疆之業，斯有無疆之休。故觀三代之利建藩屏，保乂王家，而一時君臣純佑以治，可知也已。《詩》曰：「本支百世，施於孫子。」又曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。」今聖明在上，敦本隆化，協氣橫流，含生庶類莫不漸被膏澤。而況世祿之子，有不思自奮以揚先德者，非夫也。天下宗藩體道輸忠，崇廣被之美，宣緝熈之德，以共培億萬年無疆之休。吾見功業配乎天地，雍熈比於唐虞，皆仁義之化也。執事以
translation_en:
…for them likewise cannot but be thorough. Our Emperor has brought rites and music to manifest completeness, and his moral instruction prevails widely. He has extended his bounty to the imperial clan, issuing an edict to supplement their stipends in grain and repeatedly increasing the gifts and expressions of solicitude bestowed by imperial command. As for accepting his ministers’ requests, once again recognizing the descendants of the founding men of merit, recalling their grand designs, and reaffirming the strict administration of rewards and punishments—this truly is like Heaven and Earth nurturing all things and bringing each to fulfillment according to its particular needs. I have ventured to think that outstanding ministers who render extraordinary service receive extraordinary recompense; a state whose enterprise knows no bounds thus enjoys blessings without end. Hence, by observing how the Three Dynasties advantageously established feudatories as protective bulwarks to safeguard and govern the royal house, we may understand how rulers and ministers of those times aided one another wholeheartedly in government.

The Book of Odes says: “The main line and its branches shall endure for a hundred generations, extending to sons and grandsons.” It also says: “Those many splendid men were born in this royal kingdom.” Now our sagely and enlightened sovereign reigns above, strengthening the foundations and elevating moral instruction. Harmonious influences flow everywhere, and every kind of living being is gradually imbued with his generous bounty. How much more does this apply to the sons of families enjoying hereditary stipends! Anyone among them who does not think to exert himself and make manifest his ancestors’ virtue is no worthy man. Let the imperial feudatories throughout the realm embody the Way and offer their loyalty, enhance the excellence of beneficence broadly extended, and proclaim the virtue of continuing enlightenment, together fostering boundless blessings for countless millions of years. I foresee achievements matching Heaven and Earth, and harmony and prosperity comparable to the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun—all brought about through the transforming influence of benevolence and righteousness. You, sir, consider…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
爲何如
第三問
呂穆
同考試官教諭孫批剖析諸家得失如辨黒
白前後推原求心會道尤得十三經要旨不可徒
以涉獵之工目之
同考試官教諭李批博稽六籍之淵源詳訂
諸家之旨要志存復古學擬通方庸掇賢科以鳴
世盛
===
考試官教諭陳批註疏源流條答不爽而
又能訂定得失可謂博雅君子
考試官學正陳批經疏得失研究詳盡
知聖人之心者然後可以明道會聖人之
道者然後可以談經蓋心者道之蘊也不
得其心而欲求道者謂之固道者經之本
也不明其道而欲談經者謂之迂况經非
聖人弗作而亦非諸儒弗傳故作之者所
以明道也而傳之者亦所以明道也夫苟
punctuated:
爲何如？

第三問
呂穆

同考試官教諭孫批：剖析諸家得失，如辨黒白；前後推原，求心會道，尤得十三經要旨，不可徒以涉獵之工目之。

同考試官教諭李批：博稽六籍之淵源，詳訂諸家之旨要，志存復古，學擬通方，庸掇賢科，以鳴世盛。

考試官教諭陳批：註疏源流，條答不爽，而又能訂定得失，可謂博雅君子。

考試官學正陳批：經疏得失，研究詳盡。

知聖人之心者，然後可以明道；會聖人之道者，然後可以談經。蓋心者，道之蘊也；不得其心而欲求道者，謂之固。道者，經之本也；不明其道而欲談經者，謂之迂。况經非聖人弗作，而亦非諸儒弗傳。故作之者所以明道也，而傳之者亦所以明道也。夫苟
translation_en:
…what do you think of this?

Third Question
Lü Mu 呂穆

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: He analyzes the merits and faults of the various scholars as clearly as distinguishing black from white. Throughout, he traces matters to their origins, seeking the sages’ minds and comprehending the Way. He has especially grasped the essential meaning of the Thirteen Classics; his achievement must not be regarded as merely that of wide reading.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He broadly investigates the origins of the Six Classics and carefully assesses the essential purport of the various scholars. His ambition is to restore antiquity, and his learning aspires to comprehensive understanding. Thus he wins selection among the worthy and gives voice to the flourishing of the age.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: His answers systematically address the origins and development of the commentaries and subcommentaries without error. He can also assess their merits and faults: he may well be called a learned and cultivated gentleman.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Instructor: His investigation of the merits and faults of the subcommentaries on the Classics is thorough and detailed.

Only those who understand the minds of the sages can illuminate the Way; only those who comprehend the Way of the sages can discuss the Classics. For the mind holds the inner substance of the Way. To seek the Way without grasping their minds is called being blinkered. The Way is the foundation of the Classics. To discuss the Classics without understanding their Way is called being misguided. Moreover, the Classics could not have been composed without the sages, nor could they have been transmitted without the various Confucian scholars. Thus those who composed them did so to illuminate the Way, and those who transmitted them likewise did so to illuminate the Way. Now, if…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
知所以明道則因言以求其心因心以求
其理是故經之蘊可得而稽聖人之道可
得而會矣苟不能虛心以研之而徒恃已
見以求勝乎人則支離之說逞而附會之
失多非惟無以明道而反以叛道烏在其
爲說經也哉知乎此則漢晉諸儒之學可
得而論矣請因明問而敬陳之粵自周室
旣衰王綱弗振夫子慨道之不行與羣弟
子講明斯道取六經而刪述之上明天文
===
下脩人紀前繼往聖後開來學生民以來
未之有也文王旣沒文不在玆自遭秦火
之亂斯道不絕如縷漢興而至武帝始建
學校明禮樂求遺書而表章六經自是人
知慕學矣及宣帝繼之招選茂材立五經
博士講論異同由是教化大行一時諸儒
彬彬嚮風而經術振矣是故以十三經註
疏言之作於羣聖而述於諸儒至精且備
其來已遠究其淵源則莫盛於兩漢蓋六
punctuated: 知所以明道，則因言以求其心，因心以求其理。是故經之蘊可得而稽，聖人之道可得而會矣。苟不能虛心以研之，而徒恃已見以求勝乎人，則支離之說逞，而附會之失多，非惟無以明道，而反以叛道，烏在其爲說經也哉？知乎此，則漢晉諸儒之學可得而論矣。請因明問而敬陳之。粵自周室旣衰，王綱弗振，夫子慨道之不行，與羣弟子講明斯道，取六經而刪述之，上明天文，下脩人紀，前繼往聖，後開來學，生民以來未之有也。「文王旣沒，文不在玆？」自遭秦火之亂，斯道不絕如縷。漢興，而至武帝始建學校，明禮樂，求遺書，而表章六經，自是人知慕學矣。及宣帝繼之，招選茂材，立五經博士，講論異同，由是教化大行，一時諸儒彬彬嚮風，而經術振矣。是故以《十三經註疏》言之，作於羣聖，而述於諸儒，至精且備，其來已遠。究其淵源，則莫盛於兩漢。蓋六
translation_en:
…understand how to illuminate the Way, then through the words they may seek the sages’ minds, and through their minds seek their principles. Thus the inner meaning of the classics can be investigated and the Way of the sages apprehended. If, however, they cannot study with an open mind, but merely rely on their own views to prevail over others, then fragmented interpretations proliferate and errors of forced association multiply. Not only do they fail to illuminate the Way; they turn against it. How can this count as explaining the classics? Understanding this, we can assess the scholarship of the Confucian scholars of the Han and Jin. Allow me respectfully to set it forth in response to your discerning question.
When the house of Zhou had declined and royal authority no longer prevailed, the Master lamented that the Way was not being practiced. Together with his disciples he expounded this Way, editing and transmitting the Six Classics. Above, he clarified the patterns of Heaven; below, he cultivated the ordering principles of human relations. He carried forward the legacy of earlier sages and opened the way for later learners. Since humankind first existed, there had never been his like. “With King Wen now dead, does not this cultural heritage reside here in me?” After the upheaval of the Qin book burning, this Way survived by a thread. The Han arose, but only under Emperor Wu were schools established, rites and music elucidated, surviving writings sought out, and the Six Classics honored and brought to prominence. From then on, people knew to aspire to learning. When Emperor Xuan subsequently continued this work, he recruited outstanding talent, established Erudites for the Five Classics, and had points of agreement and difference debated. Moral instruction consequently spread widely. The scholars of the age, cultivated and accomplished, responded to his example, and classical learning flourished.
Thus, to speak of the Commentaries and Subcommentaries on the Thirteen Classics: the classics were composed by the sages and expounded by the scholars; this exceedingly refined and comprehensive tradition reaches far back into the past. If we investigate its origins and development, nowhere did it flourish more than under the two Han dynasties. For the six [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
時諸儒專門名家者不復旁及他書而咸
尊之以為經是故言易則始於田何之十
二篇傳於梁丘而未盛至王弼之學主理
略數獨冠古今其傳遂流江左韓康伯邢
璹之徒因而疏之雜取老莊終貽不經之
誚以致異端競起學之者疑而難稽則又
何貴於疏義為也言書則古文得之壁中
以巫蠱而復廢至皇甫謐獨得其書歷隋
宋而始流江北巢猗費𣁽劉焯之徒雖經
===
註釋然旨趣多乖終蹈淺略之弊使人煩
而多惑勞而鮮功則又何必於註釋為也
言詩則始於毛公而盛於韋賢鄭康成為
之箋之其宣釐正風仰窺奧室不可貶也
嗣後疏之者何胤全緩輩而惟劉焯兄弟
為殊絕觀其秀拔一時騁轡千里其諸儒
之所揖讓者乎言春秋則始於丘明杜元
凱為之訓之其引經明義如子應母不可
議也厥後疏之者沈文何蘇寬而惟劉炫
punctuated:
時諸儒專門名家者，不復旁及他書，而咸尊之以為經。是故言易，則始於田何之十二篇，傳於梁丘而未盛。至王弼之學，主理略數，獨冠古今，其傳遂流江左。韓康伯、邢璹之徒因而疏之，雜取老莊，終貽不經之誚，以致異端競起，學之者疑而難稽，則又何貴於疏義為也？
言書，則古文得之壁中，以巫蠱而復廢。至皇甫謐獨得其書，歷隋宋而始流江北。巢猗、費𣁽、劉焯之徒，雖經註釋，然旨趣多乖，終蹈淺略之弊，使人煩而多惑，勞而鮮功，則又何必於註釋為也？
言詩，則始於毛公而盛於韋賢。鄭康成為之箋之，其宣釐正風，仰窺奧室，不可貶也。嗣後疏之者，何胤、全緩輩，而惟劉焯兄弟為殊絕。觀其秀拔一時，騁轡千里，其諸儒之所揖讓者乎？
言春秋，則始於丘明。杜元凱為之訓之，其引經明義，如子應母，不可議也。厥後疏之者，沈文何、蘇寬，而惟劉炫
translation_en:
…the scholars of that time who won renown as specialists no longer extended their studies to other books, and all revered their chosen texts as classics. Thus, speaking of the Book of Changes, its transmission began with Tian He's twelve chapters and passed to Liangqiu, but had not yet flourished. With Wang Bi, whose learning emphasized principles and gave less weight to numbers, it attained an eminence unmatched in ancient or modern times; his commentary subsequently circulated in Jiangzuo. Han Kangbo, Xing Shu, and others then composed subcommentaries upon it, incorporating miscellaneous teachings of Laozi and Zhuangzi. In the end, they incurred the reproach of departing from the classics, causing heterodox teachings to spring up in competition. Students were left doubtful and found it difficult to establish what was sound. What value, then, was there in these explanatory subcommentaries?
Speaking of the Book of Documents, the ancient-script text was recovered from within a wall, but was again set aside because of the witchcraft affair. Later, Huangfu Mi alone obtained the book; only after passing through the Sui and Song dynasties [?] did it begin to circulate north of the Yangzi. Although Chao Yi, Fei [?; given name transcribed as 𣁽], Liu Zhuo, and others annotated it, their interpretations frequently diverged from its meaning. They ultimately fell into the fault of superficiality and brevity, leaving readers troubled and full of doubts, laboring much but accomplishing little. What need, then, was there for these annotations?
Speaking of the Book of Odes, its transmission began with Master Mao and flourished with Wei Xian. Zheng Kangcheng supplied explanatory notes. His elucidation and rectification of the Airs [?], reaching upward to glimpse the innermost chamber of meaning, cannot be disparaged. Among those who subsequently composed subcommentaries were He Yin, Quan Huan [?], and others, but only Liu Zhuo and his brother were truly outstanding. Consider how they rose above their contemporaries and galloped a thousand li: were they not men before whom the other scholars would bow and yield precedence?
Speaking of the Spring and Autumn Annals, its commentary began with Qiuming. Du Yuankai supplied explanatory glosses, citing the classic to illuminate its meaning with a correspondence as close as a child's response to its mother; this cannot be faulted. Those who subsequently composed subcommentaries included Shen Wenhe [?] and Su Kuan, but only Liu Xuan …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
為最觀其辨博罕儔鉤深致遠其諸子之
翹楚乎公羊墨守何休師之戴宏者也膏
肓之攻厥辨已力其師作解疑以難賈逵
之長義惜乎持論太過反致失據使逵緣
隙而奪之觀德不决重致兩創君子有餘
恨矣穀梁集解范寗父子之家學也創名
例百餘條以規諸儒同異之說似亦為世
所重者然學不經師終竊二傳之緒是安
得為通方之理乎儀禮始於高堂生之十
===
七篇以授徐生歷蕭奮后蒼至兩戴而厥
旨斯暢鄭玄註之賈逵疏之至宋楊復又
為二百一十八圖以附之用補大禮之缺
其制精而弗漏朱子亟稱之宜矣周禮作
於周公經畫明備誠哉致太平之書也漢
初無聞至劉歆而始著通其說者杜氏子
春也自後冬官獨缺而全書莫見于天下
故何休以為戰國陰謀之書林孝存以為
瀆亂不經之說復作十論七難以排之不
punctuated:
為最。觀其辨博罕儔，鉤深致遠，其諸子之翹楚乎？《公羊墨守》，何休師之戴宏者也。膏肓之攻，厥辨已力。其師作《解疑》，以難賈逵之《長義》，惜乎持論太過，反致失據，使逵緣隙而奪之。觀德不决，重致兩創，君子有餘恨矣。《穀梁集解》，范寗父子之家學也。創名例百餘條，以規諸儒同異之說，似亦為世所重者。然學不經師，終竊二傳之緒，是安得為通方之理乎？

《儀禮》始於高堂生之十七篇，以授徐生，歷蕭奮、后蒼，至兩戴而厥旨斯暢。鄭玄註之，賈逵疏之。至宋，楊復又為二百一十八圖以附之，用補大禮之缺，其制精而弗漏，朱子亟稱之宜矣。《周禮》作於周公，經畫明備，誠哉致太平之書也！漢初無聞，至劉歆而始著。通其說者，杜氏子春也。自後冬官獨缺，而全書莫見于天下。故何休以為戰國陰謀之書，林孝存以為瀆亂不經之說，復作《十論》《七難》以排之。不
translation_en:
…was the foremost. Considering his unrivaled breadth of argument, his probing of profound meanings and pursuit of far-reaching implications, was he not outstanding among these scholars? The Impregnable Defense of Gongyang was what He Xiu learned from Dai Hong. In the attack on the Incurable Malady, his arguments were already forceful. His teacher composed Resolving Doubts to challenge Jia Kui’s Superior Interpretations. Regrettably, he pressed his claims too far and thereby lost his grounding, allowing Jia Kui to exploit the opening and defeat him. “Observing virtue without reaching a decision” [?], he brought injury upon both sides once again, leaving gentlemen with lingering regret. The Collected Explanations of Guliang embodied the family learning of Fan Ning and his son. They established more than a hundred rules concerning terminology and interpretive conventions to regulate the scholars’ divergent and shared interpretations; this, too, seems to have been esteemed in its day. Yet their learning had not been transmitted through a teacher, and in the end they merely appropriated strands from the other two commentaries. How could this amount to principles of comprehensive understanding?

The Ceremonies and Rites began with Gaotang Sheng’s seventeen chapters, which he transmitted to Xu Sheng. Passed down through Xiao Fen and Hou Cang, their meaning was fully elucidated with the two Dais. Zheng Xuan annotated the text, and Jia Kui supplied a subcommentary. In the Song, Yang Fu further appended 218 illustrations to remedy gaps in the great ritual system. Their design was precise and omitted nothing: it was fitting that Master Zhu praised them repeatedly. The Rites of Zhou was composed by the Duke of Zhou. Its institutional arrangements are clear and complete; truly, it is a book for bringing about Great Peace! Unheard of at the beginning of the Han, it first became known through Liu Xin. The man who mastered its teachings was Du Zichun. Thereafter, the Office of Winter alone was missing, and no complete text was to be found anywhere in the realm. Thus He Xiu regarded it as a book of covert schemes from the Warring States period, while Lin Xiaocun considered its teachings corrupt, disorderly, and contrary to the classics; he also composed Ten Discourses and Seven Challenges to refute it. Had it not been for…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有鄭玄篤信考古則聖經幾於滅熄矣禮
記則二戴同師后蒼而其氏分門王鄭率
本二戴而同經異說南北之派凡數十家
而表表者惟皇甫侃熊安而已熊則背本
經而援外義較之皇甫近勝也孝經倡於
河間顔芝而註之者凡百家孔安國尚古
文劉炫宗之不改鄭玄主今文而陸澄致
譏其說不一要之安國家傳之學其庶幾
也論語一書有古文今文之異張禹兼通
===
魯論而包氏周氏章句出焉孔安國獨解
魯論而馬融爲之訓鄭玄益以齊古義說
甚彰王肅之徒相爲羽翼實何晏之所宗
也孟子註於趙岐而陸善經宗之其音釋
則張謚丁公著兩家張氏徒分章句而遺
漏頗多丁氏稍識㫖歸時有僞謬惟趙爲
近之爾雅倡於周公而成於子夏誠九流
之奥㫖也中道寖微世罕聞之自終軍豹
鼠之辨其書始行郭景純究心一十八載
punctuated: 有鄭玄篤信考古，則聖經幾於滅熄矣。禮記則二戴同師后蒼，而其氏分門；王、鄭率本二戴，而同經異說。南北之派凡數十家，而表表者惟皇甫侃、熊安而已。熊則背本經而援外義，較之皇甫近勝也。孝經倡於河間顔芝，而註之者凡百家。孔安國尚古文，劉炫宗之不改；鄭玄主今文，而陸澄致譏。其說不一，要之安國家傳之學，其庶幾也。論語一書，有古文、今文之異。張禹兼通魯論，而包氏、周氏章句出焉。孔安國獨解魯論，而馬融爲之訓。鄭玄益以齊、古義，說甚彰。王肅之徒相爲羽翼，實何晏之所宗也。孟子註於趙岐，而陸善經宗之。其音釋則張謚、丁公著兩家。張氏徒分章句，而遺漏頗多；丁氏稍識㫖歸，時有僞謬，惟趙爲近之。爾雅倡於周公，而成於子夏，誠九流之奥㫖也。中道寖微，世罕聞之。自終軍豹鼠之辨，其書始行。郭景純究心一十八載。
translation_en:
…had Zheng Xuan not steadfastly devoted himself to investigating antiquity, the sages’ classics would nearly have died out. As for the Record of Rites, the two Dais both studied under Hou Cang, yet their lines formed separate schools. Wang and Zheng generally based their work on the two Dais, but offered different interpretations of the same classic. The northern and southern traditions numbered several dozen schools; the outstanding figures were Huangfu Kan and Xiong An [?]. Xiong departed from the classic itself and drew upon meanings from other sources; by comparison, Huangfu was somewhat superior [?].

The Classic of Filial Piety was first promoted by Yan Zhi of Hejian, and fully a hundred scholars wrote commentaries on it. Kong Anguo favored the Old Text, and Liu Xuan followed him without alteration. Zheng Xuan upheld the New Text, but Lu Cheng criticized him. Their interpretations differed; on balance, Anguo’s family tradition of learning probably came closest to the truth.

The Analects exists in differing Old Text and New Text versions. Zhang Yu also mastered the Lu Analects, and the chapter-and-sentence commentaries of Bao and Zhou emerged from this tradition. Kong Anguo interpreted only the Lu Analects [?], and Ma Rong supplied explanatory glosses for it. Zheng Xuan added interpretations from the Qi and Old Text versions, and his explanations became widely renowned. Wang Su and his followers provided mutual support; these were indeed the authorities followed by He Yan.

Zhao Qi annotated the Mencius, and Lu Shanjing followed him. Its pronunciation glosses came from two scholars, Zhang Shi [?] and Ding Gongzhu. Zhang merely divided the text into chapters and sentences, leaving many omissions. Ding had some understanding of its essential meaning, but occasionally made errors. Zhao alone came close to it.

The Erya was initiated by the Duke of Zhou and completed by Zixia; it truly contains the profound meanings of the nine schools of learning. Along the way, its transmission gradually declined, and few in the world knew of it. Only after Zhong Jun’s distinction concerning the leopard and the rat did the book begin to circulate. Guo Jingchun devoted himself to its study for eighteen years…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而草木魚虫訓詁名物昭然具舉考古之
學其彬彬焉此其源流之迹授受之傳各
有所自而非妄為之說使聖經散而復傳
絕而復續者諸儒之力居多雖然務訓詁
而遺心得之功專探索而忘附會之失者
亦不能無也文中子曰九師興而易道微
三傳作而春秋散齊魯毛韓詩之末也大
戴小戴禮之衰也不亦有見乎至唐孔穎
達輩校定羣經而於諸儒多所譏駁譏之
===
誠是也蓋以務特達者而開奬失路其失
也誣負雄才者輕鄙先達其失也謬尚辨
博者時乖正義其失也迂他如義例粗可
者而於經傳則疎旁攻賈服者而於本文
則背口習師教而反規其失者能免蠹食
其母之失乎綜織經文而詭異前儒者能
逃穿鑿孔穴之譏乎之數子者皆不能據
理談經以心悟道故人持己見而各私其
說彼此互相攻伐而穿鑿益甚其優劣得
punctuated: 而草木魚虫訓詁名物昭然具舉，考古之學其彬彬焉。此其源流之迹、授受之傳，各有所自，而非妄為之說。使聖經散而復傳、絕而復續者，諸儒之力居多。雖然，務訓詁而遺心得之功，專探索而忘附會之失者，亦不能無也。文中子曰：「九師興而易道微，三傳作而春秋散。齊魯毛韓，詩之末也；大戴小戴，禮之衰也。」不亦有見乎？至唐孔穎達輩校定羣經，而於諸儒多所譏駁，譏之誠是也。蓋以務特達者而開奬失路，其失也誣；負雄才者輕鄙先達，其失也謬；尚辨博者時乖正義，其失也迂。他如義例粗可者，而於經傳則疎；旁攻賈服者，而於本文則背。口習師教而反規其失者，能免蠹食其母之失乎？綜織經文而詭異前儒者，能逃穿鑿孔穴之譏乎？之數子者，皆不能據理談經，以心悟道，故人持己見而各私其說，彼此互相攻伐，而穿鑿益甚，其優劣得
translation_en:
…and the glosses and names of plants, trees, fish, and insects were all clearly set forth. How richly cultivated was this learning devoted to investigating antiquity! These traces of its origins and development, and these traditions of teaching and transmission, each had their own source; they were not arbitrarily invented explanations. That the sages’ classics were transmitted again after being scattered, and that their transmission resumed after being broken off, was largely due to the efforts of these scholars. Nevertheless, some inevitably devoted themselves to textual glosses while neglecting the work of attaining understanding in their own minds, or concentrated on investigation while overlooking the faults of forced interpretation. Master Wenzhong said: “When the nine masters arose, the Way of the Changes declined; when the three commentaries were composed, the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals became dispersed. The Qi, Lu, Mao, and Han traditions represent the latter-day decline of the Odes; the Elder Dai and Younger Dai represent the decline of ritual learning.” Was this not an insightful judgment?

In the Tang, Kong Yingda and his colleagues collated and established the texts of the classics, frequently criticizing and refuting earlier scholars. Their criticisms were indeed justified. Those intent on exceptional insight encouraged mistaken paths [?]; their fault was misrepresentation. Those who relied upon their outstanding abilities slighted their eminent predecessors; their fault was error. Those who prized disputation and extensive learning sometimes departed from the correct meaning; their fault was tortuousness. Others offered interpretive principles that were tolerable in outline, yet were poorly versed in the classics and their commentaries; or attacked Jia and Fu on subsidiary points while departing from the original text. Those who repeated their teachers’ instruction by rote, yet turned around to criticize their faults—could they avoid the fault of a grub devouring its own mother? Those who wove together passages of the classics to produce strange interpretations at odds with earlier scholars—could they escape the charge of boring holes through forced interpretation? These several scholars [?] were all unable to discuss the classics on the basis of principle or to apprehend the Way in their own minds. Thus each clung to his own views and favored his own explanations. They attacked one another, and their forced interpretations became ever more extreme. Their relative strengths and weaknesses, their successes …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
失見矣安望其能明斯道也耶逮宋文運
復興真儒輩出振道學之風以繼千古不
傳之緒程正叔傳易而陰陽之道著蔡元
定註書而政事之典彰胡安國註春秋而
名分之紀定朱子註詩傳而性情之義正
議三禮而中和之極立論語有註而傳心
之法明孟子有註而義利之辨决其他經
傳無不究索使聖人之道復明於天下後
世者凡以諸儒潛心于精微之奧而不役
===
志于糟粕之末也何者經之所載者理也
理之所寓者心也心者經之本而聖學之
源也學者能以心觀理以理窮經通吾心
之神化則盡乎易之變而潔淨精微之教
得矣公吾心之好惡則發乎詩之情而溫
柔敦厚之教得矣達吾心之政體則貫乎
書之事而疏通知遠之教得矣揆吾心之
典常則守乎禮之經而恭儉莊敬之教得
矣秉吾心之權衡則斷乎春秋之是非而
punctuated:
失見矣，安望其能明斯道也耶？逮宋，文運復興，真儒輩出，振道學之風，以繼千古不傳之緒。程正叔傳易，而陰陽之道著；蔡元定註書，而政事之典彰；胡安國註春秋，而名分之紀定；朱子註詩傳，而性情之義正；議三禮，而中和之極立；論語有註，而傳心之法明；孟子有註，而義利之辨决。其他經傳，無不究索。使聖人之道復明於天下後世者，凡以諸儒潛心于精微之奧，而不役志于糟粕之末也。
何者？經之所載者，理也；理之所寓者，心也。心者，經之本而聖學之源也。學者能以心觀理，以理窮經，通吾心之神化，則盡乎易之變，而潔淨精微之教得矣；公吾心之好惡，則發乎詩之情，而溫柔敦厚之教得矣；達吾心之政體，則貫乎書之事，而疏通知遠之教得矣；揆吾心之典常，則守乎禮之經，而恭儉莊敬之教得矣；秉吾心之權衡，則斷乎春秋之是非，而
translation_en:
…their shortcomings are apparent. How could one hope that they could illuminate this Way? With the advent of the Song, literary culture flourished anew, and true Confucian scholars emerged in succession. They invigorated the Learning of the Way, continuing a thread whose transmission had been broken for a thousand years. Cheng Zhengshu expounded the Changes, making manifest the Way of yin and yang; Cai Yuanding annotated the Documents, bringing to light the canons of government; Hu Anguo annotated the Spring and Autumn Annals, establishing the ordering principles of status and proper roles; Master Zhu annotated the Commentary on the Odes, setting right the meaning of human nature and feelings. Discussion of the Three Ritual Classics established the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony; annotations to the Analects clarified the method of transmitting the mind; annotations to the Mencius settled the distinction between righteousness and profit. They investigated all the other classics and commentaries without exception. That they made the sages’ Way shine forth again throughout the world and for later generations was entirely because these scholars immersed their minds in its profound subtleties, rather than wearing out their resolve over the incidental dregs.
Why is this so? What the classics contain is principle; where principle resides is the mind. The mind is the root of the classics and the source of sagely learning. If learners can contemplate principle through the mind and fathom the classics through principle, then, by comprehending the wondrous transformations of their own minds, they will fully grasp the transformations of the Changes and acquire its teaching of purity and subtle discernment. By making their minds’ likes and dislikes impartial, they will give expression to the feelings of the Odes and acquire its teaching of gentleness and sincerity. By understanding within their minds the essential form of government, they will comprehend the affairs recorded in the Documents and acquire its teaching of broad understanding and knowledge of the distant past. By examining the constant norms within their minds, they will uphold the enduring principles of the Rites and acquire its teaching of respect, frugality, dignity, and reverence. By holding fast to the scales of judgment within their minds, they will judge right and wrong in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
屬詞比事之教得矣其他如論語之道德
孟子之仁義周禮之制度爾雅之文物皆
在所具舉而註疏之功可無事焉已否則
徒泥其迹求之詞章訓詁之餘而所學抑
末耳雖然莫為於前雖美弗彰莫為於後
雖盛弗傳漢儒之功亦不可少也時當秦
火之餘羣經散而莫存斯道廢而莫講不
有諸儒為之考究則後之學者將何所依
據雖有宋儒心得之學亦恐無所施其能
===
矣註疏之功其可盡廢之耶由是觀之漢
儒之學尚文其究也詳而博宋儒之學尚
理其究也約而精二者皆不可廢也後之
學者能由博以之約由粗以入精則經無
不明理無不究而聖學可幾矣疎狂之言
惟執事進而教之
第四問
邵漳
同考試官教諭王 批 周公立法精意發明殆盡
punctuated:
屬詞比事之教得矣。其他如《論語》之道德、《孟子》之仁義、《周禮》之制度、《爾雅》之文物，皆在所具舉，而註疏之功可無事焉已。否則，徒泥其迹，求之詞章訓詁之餘，而所學抑末耳。雖然，莫為於前，雖美弗彰；莫為於後，雖盛弗傳。漢儒之功亦不可少也。時當秦火之餘，羣經散而莫存，斯道廢而莫講，不有諸儒為之考究，則後之學者將何所依據？雖有宋儒心得之學，亦恐無所施其能矣。註疏之功，其可盡廢之耶？由是觀之，漢儒之學尚文，其究也詳而博；宋儒之學尚理，其究也約而精。二者皆不可廢也。後之學者能由博以之約，由粗以入精，則經無不明，理無不究，而聖學可幾矣。疎狂之言，惟執事進而教之。

第四問
邵漳
同考試官教諭王批：「周公立法精意，發明殆盡」
translation_en:
…and the teaching of arranging words and comparing events will be attained. Other matters, such as the Way and virtue in the Analects, benevolence and righteousness in the Mengzi, institutions in the Rites of Zhou, and cultural forms and objects in the Erya (Approaching Elegance), will likewise all be comprehensively grasped, so that the work of commentaries and subcommentaries may be dispensed with. Otherwise, one merely clings to outward traces, seeking understanding among the remnants of literary composition and textual glosses; what one learns is, after all, only peripheral. Nevertheless, without those who worked before, even what is beautiful would not become manifest; without those who worked afterward, even what flourished would not be transmitted. The contribution of the Han Confucian scholars was also indispensable. In the aftermath of the Qin book burning, the Classics lay scattered and unpreserved, and this Way had fallen into disuse and was no longer expounded. Had those scholars not investigated these matters, what would later students have had to rely upon? Even with the Song Confucians’ learning grounded in personal apprehension, I fear they would have had nowhere to apply their abilities. Can the contribution of commentaries and subcommentaries, then, be wholly discarded? Viewed in this light, Han Confucian learning prized the texts, pursuing detailed and extensive inquiry; Song Confucian learning prized principle, pursuing concise and refined inquiry. Neither can be discarded. If later students can proceed from breadth to essentials and from the coarse to the refined, no Classic will remain unclear and no principle unexplored, and the learning of the sages may be approached. These are my ill-considered and presumptuous words; I ask you, sir, to take them up and instruct me.

Fourth Question
Shao Zhang
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “The subtle intent of the Duke of Zhou in establishing institutions is elucidated almost completely…”

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無餘蘊真有以得聖人之心於千載之上
同考試官教諭鄭批周官漢制損益大略具
在方冊子能究心之邃於學者也可録
考試官教諭陳批識周官相維之法探兩
漢興廢之由敷演詳明詞華炳蔚佳士佳士
考試官學正陳批周官本意漢制近古皆
能詳言其實稽古之學也敬服敬服
先王以賢用人故任相也重以敬行政故
立法也嚴任相重則體統一而謨弼諧上
===
下交而德業泰而天下之治功于此乎成
立法嚴則幾微審而事為慎內外合而綱
紀隆而天下之化源于此乎起然非先王
能辨賢于任用之初主敬于法制之始則
賢否或至于混淆公私不免于交錯治功
之理亂化源之通塞于此乎分欲明良感
而上下交時幾勅而內外合也難矣此先
王之治所以為盛者無他焉亦惟用人行
政之間得其道焉爾矣執事策士秋闈以
punctuated:
無餘蘊，真有以得聖人之心於千載之上。
同考試官教諭鄭批：周官、漢制，損益大略具在方冊。子能究心之，邃於學者也，可録。
考試官教諭陳批：識周官相維之法，探兩漢興廢之由，敷演詳明，詞華炳蔚。佳士！佳士！
考試官學正陳批：周官本意，漢制近古，皆能詳言其實，稽古之學也。敬服！敬服！
先王以賢用人，故任相也重；以敬行政，故立法也嚴。任相重，則體統一而謨弼諧，上下交而德業泰，而天下之治功于此乎成。立法嚴，則幾微審而事為慎，內外合而綱紀隆，而天下之化源于此乎起。然非先王能辨賢于任用之初，主敬于法制之始，則賢否或至于混淆，公私不免于交錯，治功之理亂、化源之通塞，于此乎分。欲明良感而上下交，時幾勅而內外合也，難矣。此先王之治所以為盛者，無他焉，亦惟用人行政之間得其道焉爾矣。執事策士秋闈，以
translation_en:
…leaving no meaning unexplored. He has truly grasped the sage’s mind across a thousand years.

Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: The broad outlines of the modifications to the Offices of Zhou and the institutions of the Han are all recorded in books. You have investigated them thoroughly and are a man of profound learning. Worthy of acceptance.

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: He understands the mutually sustaining arrangements of the Offices of Zhou and explores the reasons for the rise and decline of the two Han dynasties. His exposition is detailed and clear, his language brilliant and richly ornamented. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!

Examiner Chen, School Director, comments: He explains fully the underlying intent of the Offices of Zhou and how Han institutions approximated those of antiquity, setting out the actual circumstances of both. This is learning grounded in the investigation of antiquity. I admire him! I admire him!

The former kings employed men for their worthiness, and therefore treated the appointment of chief ministers as a weighty matter; they conducted government with reverence, and therefore established laws with rigor. When the appointment of chief ministers is treated as weighty, the structure of authority is unified and counsel and assistance are harmonious; those above and below communicate, and virtue and achievement flourish. Thus the accomplishments of orderly government throughout the realm are realized. When laws are established with rigor, the slightest incipient developments are carefully scrutinized and affairs are handled cautiously; those within and without work together, and the governing framework is strengthened. Thus the source of moral transformation throughout the realm arises.

Yet had the former kings not been able to distinguish the worthy at the outset of making appointments and to take reverence as their guiding principle from the beginning of establishing institutions, the worthy and unworthy might have become confused, and public and private interests would inevitably have become entangled. Here lies the distinction between order and disorder in the work of government, and between the free flow and obstruction of the source of moral transformation. It would then be difficult to bring an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers into mutual accord, to secure communication between those above and below, to attend vigilantly to the incipient developments of the times, and to unite those within and without. There was no other reason for the flourishing government of the former kings: they simply attained the proper Way in employing men and conducting government.

You, sir, examine scholars through policy questions in the autumn Provincial Examination, taking as your subject…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周禮太宰之官與王論道經邦兼統內外
為問並舉兩漢之事而確揚之豈非以先
王用人行政之道後世治忽興覆之理不
可以不講乎然嘗遠稽周禮近覽漢書而
得其槩焉請紬繹其義而敬陳之今夫天
生蒸民無主乃亂故立其君以統之以出
治也明王奉若天道匪人弗乂故立其臣
以輔之以成治也其用人行政之本乎易
敘宓犧神農黃帝作敎化民而傳述其官
===
書稱唐虞夏商稽古建官而記言其數遐
哉邈乎不可及矣若夫體國經野設官分
職寅亮天工輔理物宜光明正大之體紀
綱法度之施蓋莫盛于成周莫備于周禮
莫詳于六卿之分職莫專于太宰之總統
故自其大者而考之則有六典以佐邦國
有八法以治官府有八則以治都鄙有八
柄以御羣臣有九職以任萬民有九賦以
斂財賄有九式以節財用有九貢以致邦
punctuated:
周禮太宰之官，與王論道經邦，兼統內外為問，並舉兩漢之事而確揚之，豈非以先王用人行政之道、後世治忽興覆之理，不可以不講乎？然嘗遠稽《周禮》，近覽《漢書》，而得其槩焉。請紬繹其義而敬陳之。
今夫天生蒸民，無主乃亂，故立其君以統之，以出治也。明王奉若天道，匪人弗乂，故立其臣以輔之，以成治也。其用人行政之本乎！《易》敘宓犧、神農、黃帝作敎化民，而傳述其官；《書》稱唐虞夏商稽古建官，而記言其數。遐哉邈乎，不可及矣！若夫體國經野，設官分職，寅亮天工，輔理物宜，光明正大之體，紀綱法度之施，蓋莫盛于成周，莫備于《周禮》，莫詳于六卿之分職，莫專于太宰之總統。
故自其大者而考之，則有六典以佐邦國，有八法以治官府，有八則以治都鄙，有八柄以御羣臣，有九職以任萬民，有九賦以斂財賄，有九式以節財用，有九貢以致邦
translation_en:
…you have posed a question about the office of Grand Steward in the Rites of Zhou: his discussion of the Way with the king, his ordering of the realm, and his overarching authority over both inner and outer affairs. You have also adduced events from the two Han dynasties to establish and elucidate the matter [?]. Is this not because the former kings’ methods of employing men and conducting government, and the principles underlying order and disorder, rise and collapse in later ages, must be examined? I have consulted the Rites of Zhou for the more distant past and surveyed the History of the Han for the more recent, thereby gaining a general understanding. Allow me to draw out their meaning and respectfully set it forth.
Heaven brought forth the multitude of the people; without a ruler, they fell into disorder. Thus it established their sovereign to unite them and initiate orderly government. The enlightened king reverently follows Heaven’s Way, yet without the right men there can be no good government. Thus he appoints ministers to assist him and bring that government to fruition. Is this not the foundation of employing men and conducting government? The Book of Changes recounts how Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor instituted teachings and transformed the people, and transmits accounts of their officials. The Book of Documents tells how Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang examined antiquity and established offices, recording their numbers. How distant and remote—beyond our reach! As for laying out the capital and demarcating the countryside, establishing offices and allocating duties, reverently assisting Heaven’s work and helping order all things appropriately: in the establishment of an illustrious and upright order and the application of governing principles, laws, and institutions, nothing surpassed the Zhou at its height. Nothing was more comprehensive than the Rites of Zhou, more detailed than the division of duties among the six ministers, or more unified in authority than the Grand Steward’s overall direction.
Thus, examining its major provisions, we find six canons for assisting the states; eight regulations for governing the administrative offices; eight rules for governing the domains and appanages; eight instruments of authority for controlling the assembled ministers; nine occupations through which to assign work to all the people; nine levies for collecting wealth and goods; nine standards for regulating expenditure; and nine categories of tribute for securing the states’…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
國之用有九兩以繫邦國之民夫是十者
皆政之弘綱國之重典固宜太宰而司之
矣然太史內史掌六典八法八則八柄之
貳春官之屬也而典法之正則在于大宰
太僕掌諸侯之復逆小臣掌三公及孤卿
之復逆御僕掌羣吏之逆及庶民之復夏
官之屬也而臣民之總則掌于宰夫司士
掌朝儀之位秋官之屬也而治朝之位則
宰夫掌之泉府廩人倉人掌財用地官之
===
屬也而貨賄之出入則太府掌之凡此類
者其事已列于五官而其機猶屬之太宰
不亦煩冗而紛更耶自其小者而考之則
有宮正宮伯以為之屬有膳夫庖人內饔
外饔亨人以為之屬有甸師獸人獻人鼈
人腊人以為之屬有醫師食醫疾醫瘍醫
獸醫以為之屬有酒正酒人漿人凌人籩
人醢人醯人鹽人冪人以為之屬有宮人
掌舍幕人掌次以為之屬有大府玉府內
punctuated:
國之用，有九兩以繫邦國之民。夫是十者，皆政之弘綱、國之重典，固宜太宰而司之矣。然太史、內史掌六典、八法、八則、八柄之貳，春官之屬也，而典法之正則在于大宰；太僕掌諸侯之復逆，小臣掌三公及孤卿之復逆，御僕掌羣吏之逆及庶民之復，夏官之屬也，而臣民之總則掌于宰夫；司士掌朝儀之位，秋官之屬也，而治朝之位則宰夫掌之；泉府、廩人、倉人掌財用，地官之屬也，而貨賄之出入則太府掌之。凡此類者，其事已列于五官，而其機猶屬之太宰，不亦煩冗而紛更耶？
自其小者而考之，則有宮正、宮伯以為之屬，有膳夫、庖人、內饔、外饔、亨人以為之屬，有甸師、獸人、獻人、鼈人、腊人以為之屬，有醫師、食醫、疾醫、瘍醫、獸醫以為之屬，有酒正、酒人、漿人、凌人、籩人、醢人、醯人、鹽人、冪人以為之屬，有宮人、掌舍、幕人、掌次以為之屬，有大府、玉府、內
translation_en:
…the requirements of the states; there are the nine bonds by which the people of the states are held together. These ten are all broad principles of government and major institutions of the state, so it is certainly fitting that the Grand Steward administer them. Yet the Grand Scribe and Interior Scribe keep duplicate records of the six canons, eight regulations, eight rules, and eight instruments of authority. They are subordinate to the Ministry of Spring, while the authoritative canons and regulations reside with the Grand Steward. The Grand Equerry handles reports and submissions from the feudal lords; the Minor Servitor handles those from the Three Dukes, Junior Guardians, and ministers; and the Imperial Equerry handles submissions from the various officials and reports from the common people. These officers are subordinate to the Ministry of Summer, yet general oversight of officials and people rests with the Assistant Steward. The Director of Officers manages positions in court ceremonies and is subordinate to the Ministry of Autumn, yet positions at the administrative court are managed by the Assistant Steward. The Treasury Office, Granary Officers, and Storehouse Officers manage financial resources and are subordinate to the Ministry of Earth, yet receipts and disbursements of goods and valuables are managed by the Grand Treasury. In all such cases, the business is already assigned among the five ministries, while its controlling authority still belongs to the Grand Steward. Does this not entail cumbersome duplication and confused interference?
Examining the lesser matters, he has as his subordinates the Palace Commandant and Palace Overseer; the Provisioner, Cooks, Inner Cooks, Outer Cooks, and Boiling Cooks; the Director of Royal Fields, Game Officers, Offering Officers [?], Turtle Officers, and Dried-Meat Officers; the Chief Physician, Dietetic Physicians, Physicians, Surgeons, and Veterinarians; the Director of Wine, Wine Officers, Beverage Officers, Ice Officers, Bamboo-Vessel Officers, Meat-Paste Officers, Vinegar Officers, Salt Officers, and Vessel-Cover Officers; the Palace Attendants, Lodging Officers, Tent Officers, and Officers of Royal Encampments; and the Grand Treasury, Jade Treasury, and Inner…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
府外府以為之屬有司會司書職內職歲
職幣司裘掌皮以為之屬有內宰小臣閹
人寺人以為之屬有嬪御祝史典婦功典
絲枲內司服縫人染人追師屨人夏采以
為之屬夫是十者皆政之細務邦之小物
亦宜太宰而司之矣然官府次舍什伍道
藝有宮正以掌之庶子宿衛秩敘徒役有
宮伯以掌之珍貨之祕藏王后世子之好
用有內府以掌之宮寢嬪御之儀閹寺使
===
令之節有內宰以掌之而小宰宰夫又得
以佐太宰而兼統其司以外職而糾禁于
中不曰建邦之宮刑則曰治王宮之政令
不曰憲禁于王宮則曰令脩宮中之職事
凡此類者其事皆切于內庭而其權猶屬
之太宰不幾侵擾而僭逼耶是不然也蓋
太宰之職內統百官外均四海上撫五辰
下凝庶績故論道經邦燮理陰陽謂之三
公分職率屬倡牧阜民謂之六卿至于百
punctuated:
府、外府以為之屬，有司會、司書、職內、職歲、職幣、司裘、掌皮以為之屬，有內宰、小臣、閹人、寺人以為之屬，有嬪御、祝史、典婦功、典絲枲、內司服、縫人、染人、追師、屨人、夏采以為之屬。夫是十者，皆政之細務，邦之小物，亦宜太宰而司之矣。然官府、次舍、什伍、道藝，有宮正以掌之；庶子宿衛、秩敘、徒役，有宮伯以掌之；珍貨之祕藏，王后、世子之好用，有內府以掌之；宮寢嬪御之儀，閹寺使令之節，有內宰以掌之。而小宰、宰夫又得以佐太宰而兼統其司，以外職而糾禁于中。不曰「建邦之宮刑」，則曰「治王宮之政令」；不曰「憲禁于王宮」，則曰「令脩宮中之職事」。凡此類者，其事皆切于內庭，而其權猶屬之太宰，不幾侵擾而僭逼耶？
是不然也。蓋太宰之職，內統百官，外均四海，上撫五辰，下凝庶績。故論道經邦，燮理陰陽，謂之三公；分職率屬，倡牧阜民，謂之六卿。至于百
translation_en:
…the Inner Treasury and Outer Treasury as his subordinates; the Accounting Director, Director of Records, Controller of Receipts, Controller of Annual Expenditures, Controller of Surplus Goods, Director of Furs, and Keeper of Hides as his subordinates; the Director of the Inner Palace, Minor Attendants, Eunuchs, and Palace Attendants as his subordinates; and the palace consorts and attendants, invocators and scribes, Director of Women’s Work, directors of silk and hemp, Director of Inner Robes, seamsters, dyers, makers of ceremonial headdresses, shoemakers, and the Xia Cai officer responsible for summoning the departed soul as his subordinates. These ten groups all concern minor affairs of government and small matters of the state: it is indeed fitting that the Grand Steward should oversee them. Yet the Palace Commandant manages the palace offices, lodgings, groups of five and ten, and instruction in proper conduct and skills; the Palace Earl manages the night guards drawn from sons of noble families, their ranks and precedence, and their labor duties; the Inner Treasury manages the secret storage of precious goods and supplies things desired by the queen and heir apparent; and the Director of the Inner Palace manages the ceremonial observances of the consorts and attendants in the palace apartments and the rules governing the service of eunuchs. Moreover, the Vice Steward and Assistant Steward assist the Grand Steward and jointly supervise these offices, exercising correction and restraint within the palace through offices belonging to the outer administration. They speak either of ‘establishing the state’s palace penal regulations’ or of ‘administering the governmental commands of the royal palace’; either of ‘promulgating prohibitions in the royal palace’ or of ‘ordering the performance of duties within the palace.’ All such duties intimately concern the inner court, yet authority over them still belongs to the Grand Steward. Does this not verge on intrusive interference and presumptuous encroachment?
This is not so. The Grand Steward’s duties are to direct all officials within, bring order throughout the realm without, accord above with the five celestial markers, and consolidate below the achievements of every undertaking. Thus those who deliberate on the Way, order the state, and harmonize yin and yang are called the Three Dukes; those who apportion duties, lead their subordinates, guide and nurture the people, and enrich their lives are called the Six Ministers. As for the various…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
司庶府之官則惟承事奉職而已故外而
無所不統者非以多事也太宰既與王論
道經邦則凡經理乎外者皆道之所關况
設官分職如彼其衆立經陳紀如彼其殷
官衆則事勢異宜政殷則物理殊致門多
則紛擾易滋位異則聯比難屬不有太宰
以統之則無以一其典則而約其功能詔
其廢置而行其誅賞非所以正百官矣百
官正而萬民有不正乎內而無所不統者
===
非以擅權也太宰既與王論道經邦則凡
經理乎內者皆道之所關况宿衛器用之
司皆近侍于王宦寺嬪御之列悉承寵于
內宴安怠惰肇荒淫之基竒巧珍玩發奢
泰之端投間抵隙啓僥倖之塗憑威藉福
萌僭竊之漸不有太宰以統之則無以施
其憲制而正其服位禁其竒袤而考其藝
業非所以正朝廷矣朝廷正而百官有不
正乎是可以見先王任相之重焉立法之
punctuated:
司庶府之官，則惟承事奉職而已。故外而無所不統者，非以多事也。太宰既與王論道經邦，則凡經理乎外者，皆道之所關。况設官分職，如彼其衆；立經陳紀，如彼其殷。官衆則事勢異宜，政殷則物理殊致；門多則紛擾易滋，位異則聯比難屬。不有太宰以統之，則無以一其典則而約其功能，詔其廢置而行其誅賞，非所以正百官矣。百官正，而萬民有不正乎？
內而無所不統者，非以擅權也。太宰既與王論道經邦，則凡經理乎內者，皆道之所關。况宿衛器用之司，皆近侍于王；宦寺嬪御之列，悉承寵于內。宴安怠惰，肇荒淫之基；竒巧珍玩，發奢泰之端；投間抵隙，啓僥倖之塗；憑威藉福，萌僭竊之漸。不有太宰以統之，則無以施其憲制而正其服位，禁其竒袤而考其藝業，非所以正朝廷矣。朝廷正，而百官有不正乎？是可以見先王任相之重焉，立法之
translation_en:
…the officials of the various offices and repositories merely carry out their duties and discharge their functions. Thus, the Grand Steward’s comprehensive authority over external affairs is not a matter of meddling in everything. Since the Grand Steward discusses the Way and orders the state together with the king, everything administered outside the palace falls within the concerns of the Way. Moreover, the offices established and duties apportioned are so numerous, and the guiding principles instituted and regulations laid out so extensive. With many officials, circumstances call for different measures; with extensive governmental business, matters require different approaches. With many channels of authority, confusion readily grows; with differing positions, coordination is difficult to maintain. Without the Grand Steward to oversee them, there would be no means to unify their statutes and rules, hold them to account for their accomplishments, direct their dismissal or appointment, and administer their punishments and rewards. This would be no way to set the hundred officials right. When the hundred officials are upright, could any among the myriad people fail to be upright?
His comprehensive authority over internal affairs is not a matter of usurping power. Since the Grand Steward discusses the Way and orders the state together with the king, everything administered within the palace falls within the concerns of the Way. Moreover, the offices responsible for palace guards and furnishings all serve close to the king, while the ranks of eunuchs and consorts all receive favor within the palace. Ease and indolence lay the foundations of dissipation; ingenious curiosities and precious playthings initiate extravagance; exploiting openings and insinuating oneself through gaps opens the path to unmerited advancement; relying on borrowed authority and favor gives rise to the beginnings of usurpation. Without the Grand Steward to oversee them, there would be no means to enforce the governing regulations and properly order their dress and rank, prohibit their aberrant excesses [?], and assess their skills and work. This would be no way to set the court right. When the court is upright, could any of the hundred officials fail to be upright? From this one can see how weighty a charge the former kings entrusted to their chief minister, and how their establishment of laws…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嚴焉惟其任相之重也故于事之大小無
弗統也惟其立法之嚴也故于國之内外
無弗兼也尤可以見用人之賢焉行政之
敬焉惟其用人之賢也故舉天下之權而
歸之相以闡大同之化而主上不嫌臣下
不嫉大臣亦以身任而不辭書曰明王立
政不惟其官惟其人其是之謂乎惟其行
政之敬也故舉宫中之事而歸之相以端
萬化之源而内不為褻外不為僭大臣亦
===
以身任而不辭書曰安汝止惟幾惟康勅
天之命惟時惟幾其是之謂乎是則三代
之治莫盛于周而周制之善莫良于太宰
蓋當文武成康之為君周公召公之為相
上下同心内外一體出入起居罔有弗欽
侍御僕從罔有弗正故宋儒葉時謂以立
政無逸之規模而植立鳧鷖既醉之事業
以蓼蕭行葦之恩義而講明洛誥周官之
典刑不其然哉然自幽厲傷之而王綱遂
punctuated:
嚴焉。惟其任相之重也，故于事之大小無弗統也；惟其立法之嚴也，故于國之内外無弗兼也。尤可以見用人之賢焉，行政之敬焉。惟其用人之賢也，故舉天下之權而歸之相，以闡大同之化，而主上不嫌，臣下不嫉，大臣亦以身任而不辭。《書》曰：「明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。」其是之謂乎？惟其行政之敬也，故舉宫中之事而歸之相，以端萬化之源，而内不為褻，外不為僭，大臣亦以身任而不辭。《書》曰：「安汝止，惟幾惟康。勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」其是之謂乎？
是則三代之治莫盛于周，而周制之善莫良于太宰。蓋當文武成康之為君，周公召公之為相，上下同心，内外一體，出入起居罔有弗欽，侍御僕從罔有弗正。故宋儒葉時謂：「以立政無逸之規模，而植立鳧鷖既醉之事業；以蓼蕭行葦之恩義，而講明洛誥周官之典刑。」不其然哉？然自幽厲傷之，而王綱遂
translation_en:
…the strictness with which they established laws. Precisely because they entrusted such weighty responsibilities to the chief minister, no matter, great or small, lay outside his oversight; precisely because their legislation was strict, it encompassed both the inner court and the outer administration. Here we can see especially their wisdom in employing worthy men and their reverence in conducting government. Because they employed worthy men, they vested the authority of all under Heaven in the chief minister, to extend the transforming influence of Great Unity. The sovereign felt no suspicion, subordinate officials no jealousy, and the great minister himself accepted the responsibility without demur. The Book of Documents says: “When an enlightened king establishes government, his concern is not merely with the offices, but with the men.” Does this not express precisely that? Because they conducted government with reverence, they entrusted all palace affairs to the chief minister, to rectify the source of all transforming influence. Those within did not regard this as an intrusion upon intimate affairs, nor did those outside regard it as a usurpation; the great minister himself accepted the responsibility without demur. The Book of Documents says: “Be secure in your proper resting place; consider the incipient signs and consider well-being. Diligently attend to Heaven’s mandate; consider the times and consider the incipient signs.” Does this not express precisely that?
Thus, among the Three Dynasties, none surpassed the Zhou in good government; and among the excellent institutions of the Zhou, none was better than the office of Grand Steward. When Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang were rulers, and the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao were chief ministers, those above and below shared one purpose, and the inner court and outer administration formed a single body. In going out and coming in, in rising and resting, there was nothing they did without reverence; among attendants and servants, none failed to be upright. Thus the Song Confucian scholar Ye Shi said: “Through the framework of ‘Establishing Government’ and ‘Against Idleness,’ they established the achievements celebrated in ‘Wild Ducks and Gulls’ and ‘Already Drunk’; through the benevolence and right relations expressed in ‘The Tall Southernwood’ and ‘Reeds by the Wayside,’ they expounded the exemplary institutions of ‘The Announcement at Luo’ and ‘The Officers of Zhou.’” Was this not indeed so? Yet after Kings You and Li damaged this order, the guiding principles of royal government thereupon…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
漸以隳戰國亂之而周禮遂益以泯秦政
建號立官盡不師古漢興因循雖未遑禮
樂然其官職亦猶有古意焉蓋嘗即西漢
之百官公卿表而考之三公九卿雖列職
于外而皆有屬以居其内故御史大夫之
屬有兩丞一曰中丞居殿中蘭臺掌圖籍
秘書日近天子之尊朝廷有事則下之中
丞中丞白之御史大夫御史大夫白之丞
相是中丞在内丞相御史在外外得以統
===
内也内領侍御史外督部刺史刺史掌奉
詔例察州郡治狀黜陟能否以六條問事
而奏事復上于中丞是部史在外中丞在
内内得以統外也至若少府一官乃掌國
之山海池澤之稅以給王之共養者也然
其内自尚書而下符節大醫太官湯官及
左右司空東西織室胞人三長丞上林十
池監以至中書謁者黄門鉤盾尚方御府
之屬皆屬焉又自大長秋而下私府永巷
punctuated: 漸以隳，戰國亂之，而周禮遂益以泯。秦政建號立官，盡不師古。漢興因循，雖未遑禮樂，然其官職亦猶有古意焉。蓋嘗即西漢之《百官公卿表》而考之，三公九卿雖列職于外，而皆有屬以居其内。故御史大夫之屬有兩丞，一曰中丞，居殿中蘭臺，掌圖籍秘書，日近天子之尊。朝廷有事，則下之中丞，中丞白之御史大夫，御史大夫白之丞相。是中丞在内，丞相、御史在外，外得以統内也。内領侍御史，外督部刺史。刺史掌奉詔例，察州郡治狀，黜陟能否，以六條問事，而奏事復上于中丞。是部史在外，中丞在内，内得以統外也。至若少府一官，乃掌國之山海池澤之稅，以給王之共養者也。然其内自尚書而下，符節、大醫、太官、湯官及左右司空、東西織室、胞人三長丞、上林十池監，以至中書謁者、黄門、鉤盾、尚方、御府之屬，皆屬焉。又自大長秋而下，私府、永巷……
translation_en:
…gradually fell into decay; the Warring States brought further disorder, and the rites of Zhou consequently faded still more. The Qin regime established titles and offices entirely without taking antiquity as its model. When the Han arose, it followed existing practices. Although it had not yet found time to attend to rites and music, its official institutions still retained something of the ancient conception.

I have examined this in the “Table of the Hundred Officials, Dukes, and Ministers” for the Western Han. Although the Three Dukes and Nine Ministers held offices in the outer administration, all had subordinates stationed within the palace. Thus the Censor-in-chief had two assistants, one called the Palace Aide to the Censor-in-chief. Stationed at the Orchid Terrace within the palace, he supervised maps, registers, and confidential documents, remaining daily close to the august Son of Heaven. Whenever the court had business, it referred it to the Palace Aide, who reported it to the Censor-in-chief; the Censor-in-chief in turn reported it to the Counselor-in-chief. Thus the Palace Aide was within, while the Counselor-in-chief and Censor-in-chief were outside: the outer administration could thereby govern the inner.

Within, the Palace Aide directed the Attendant Censors; outside, he supervised the Regional Inspectors. The Inspectors were charged with acting in accordance with imperial edicts and regulations, examining the state of administration in the regions and commanderies, demoting the incompetent and promoting the capable, and conducting inquiries under the Six Articles. Their reports were then submitted to the Palace Aide. Thus the regional officials were outside and the Palace Aide within: the inner administration could thereby govern the outer.

As for the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues, this official supervised the taxes from the realm’s mountains, seas, ponds, and marshes to provide for the sovereign’s maintenance. Yet within his administration, from the Masters of Writing downward, the offices responsible for credentials, imperial medicine, imperial food, and delicacies, together with the Left and Right Directors of Works, the Eastern and Western Weaving Offices, the three directors and assistants of the cooks [?], and the superintendents of the ten ponds at Shanglin [?], extending to the Palace Secretariat Receptionists and the offices of the Yellow Gates, Palace Gardens, Imperial Manufactures, and Imperial Wardrobe, were all subordinate to him. Furthermore, from the Chamberlain for the Empress downward, the Privy Treasury and the Palace Lanes …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
倉廄祠祀食官宦官之屬皆屬焉是漢之
內庭之事未嘗不攝于外而少府之官亦
以統乎內也夫尚書大長秋屬少府少府
中丞屬丞相御史然則丞相其周之太宰
乎御史大夫其周之小宰乎御史之中丞
少府之尚書其周之宰夫乎大長秋其周
之內宰乎是西漢官制雖襲秦故而先王
之遺意猶有存者故高惠文景之時羣臣
數得宴見而奏事有由然也至武帝晚年
===
遊宴內庭用宦者主中書而典尚書之章
奏則尚書之官于是廢矣旣以中書居中
而受事又置諸吏居中而舉法故當時奏
下諸事則自中書遞送兩府自兩府下九
卿自九卿下郡國而不由中丞則中丞之
官虛矣至于三公無加官之號大將軍領
尚書之職則丞相御史之官不得復預內
庭之政而其權亦輕矣故宣帝中興魏相
爲御史大夫乃奏封事而白去副封加官
punctuated:
倉廄、祠祀、食官、宦官之屬皆屬焉。是漢之內庭之事，未嘗不攝于外，而少府之官亦以統乎內也。夫尚書、大長秋屬少府，少府、中丞屬丞相、御史，然則丞相其周之太宰乎？御史大夫其周之小宰乎？御史之中丞、少府之尚書，其周之宰夫乎？大長秋其周之內宰乎？是西漢官制雖襲秦故，而先王之遺意猶有存者。故高、惠、文、景之時，羣臣數得宴見而奏事，有由然也。
至武帝晚年，遊宴內庭，用宦者主中書，而典尚書之章奏，則尚書之官于是廢矣。旣以中書居中而受事，又置諸吏居中而舉法。故當時奏下諸事，則自中書遞送兩府，自兩府下九卿，自九卿下郡國，而不由中丞，則中丞之官虛矣。至于三公無加官之號，大將軍領尚書之職，則丞相、御史之官不得復預內庭之政，而其權亦輕矣。故宣帝中興，魏相爲御史大夫，乃奏封事而白去副封，加官
translation_en:
…those responsible for granaries and stables, sacrifices, food provisioning, and eunuch service were all subordinate to him. Thus, under the Han, the affairs of the inner court were always subject to oversight from the outer administration, and the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues also exercised authority over the inner court. The Masters of Writing and the Chamberlain for the Empress were subordinate to the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues; the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues and the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief were subordinate to the Chief Councilor and the Censor-in-chief. Was the Chief Councilor, then, the equivalent of the Zhou Grand Steward? Was the Censor-in-chief the equivalent of the Zhou Junior Steward? Were the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate and the Masters of Writing under the Chamberlain for Palace Revenues the equivalents of the Zhou Stewards? Was the Chamberlain for the Empress the equivalent of the Zhou Palace Steward? Thus, although the Western Han system of offices inherited Qin precedents, something of the intentions of the ancient kings still survived. There was therefore a reason why, in the reigns of Emperors Gao, Hui, Wen, and Jing, officials frequently obtained informal audiences to report on affairs.
By Emperor Wu’s later years, he took his recreation and held banquets in the inner court, employing eunuchs to direct the Palace Secretariat and handle the memorials previously managed by the Masters of Writing. The office of Master of Writing was consequently rendered defunct. Having placed the Palace Secretariat within the palace to receive business, he also stationed various officials there to enforce the laws. Thus, whenever matters submitted to the throne were sent down for action, they passed from the Palace Secretariat to the two chief offices, from those offices to the Nine Chamberlains, and from the Nine Chamberlains to the commanderies and kingdoms, without passing through the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief. That office was therefore emptied of substance. Moreover, the Three Dukes held no supplementary court titles, while the General-in-chief took charge of the duties of the Masters of Writing. The Chief Councilor and Censor-in-chief could consequently no longer participate in the government of the inner court, and their authority too was diminished. Thus, during the restoration under Emperor Xuan, Wei Xiang, serving as Censor-in-chief, submitted a sealed memorial requesting that the duplicate sealed copy be abolished, and received a supplementary appointment as …

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
給事而得宴見故霍山方秉樞機則得以
訟言其過杜延年居中用事則得以列奏
其姦中外之政復合于一但中丞之權猶
未能復迨于石顯用事則丞相之權盡歸
于尚書哀平之際又歸于外戚則内外不
足以相統綱紀遂至于寖亡矣光武之興
用懲前轍于是取三公之官以為閣職而
取尚書及中丞以為臺閣之長以舉法歸
中丞而以奏事歸尚書雖兼用二官以救
===
偏弊然不知其疎外庭而親内庭矣捨大
臣而近小臣矣變置三公而事歸臺閣矣
不用詩書而專任刑餘矣故桓靈之季御
史之權盡移于尚書尚書之權又移于宦
官宰相則疎隔于外御史則緘默于内事
權紛裂而四出内外閼塞而不通則政令
不離于房闥威柄已授于權奸而漢道遂
不可為是其用人行政豈惟不得周禮之
遺意即之西漢亦已遠甚焉矣是知大小
punctuated: 給事而得宴見，故霍山方秉樞機，則得以訟言其過；杜延年居中用事，則得以列奏其姦。中外之政復合于一，但中丞之權猶未能復。迨于石顯用事，則丞相之權盡歸于尚書；哀平之際，又歸于外戚，則内外不足以相統，綱紀遂至于寖亡矣。光武之興，用懲前轍，于是取三公之官以為閣職，而取尚書及中丞以為臺閣之長，以舉法歸中丞，而以奏事歸尚書。雖兼用二官以救偏弊，然不知其疎外庭而親内庭矣，捨大臣而近小臣矣，變置三公而事歸臺閣矣，不用詩書而專任刑餘矣。故桓靈之季，御史之權盡移于尚書，尚書之權又移于宦官。宰相則疎隔于外，御史則緘默于内，事權紛裂而四出，内外閼塞而不通，則政令不離于房闥，威柄已授于權奸，而漢道遂不可為。是其用人行政，豈惟不得《周禮》之遺意，即之西漢，亦已遠甚焉矣。是知大小
translation_en:
…in attendance, and thereby obtained private audiences. Thus, when Huo Shan held the levers of government, he could openly denounce Huo’s faults; when Du Yannian exercised power within the court, he could submit itemized accusations of Du’s wrongdoing. The administration of the inner and outer courts was once again united, but the authority of the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief had still not been restored. When Shi Xian came to wield power, the authority of the Counselor-in-chief passed entirely to the Masters of Writing. During the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, it passed in turn to the imperial consorts’ relatives. The inner and outer courts could no longer coordinate their authority, and the governing order gradually disintegrated.

When Guangwu rose to power, he took warning from these earlier failures. He therefore made the offices of the Three Excellencies into secretariat posts [?], and made the Masters of Writing and the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief heads of the central bureaus, assigning enforcement of the law to the Palace Assistant Censor-in-chief and the presentation of matters to the throne to the Masters of Writing. Although he employed both offices to remedy the abuses of an unbalanced arrangement, he did not realize that he was distancing himself from the outer court and drawing close to the inner court; setting aside senior ministers and favoring lesser officials; reorganizing the Three Excellencies while transferring affairs to the central bureaus; and abandoning the teachings of the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents while relying exclusively on men who had suffered castration.

Thus, in the latter years of Emperors Huan and Ling, the authority of the Censors passed entirely to the Masters of Writing, whose authority then passed to the eunuchs. The chief ministers were kept at a distance outside, while the Censors remained silent within. Authority over affairs was fragmented and exercised from every quarter; communication between the inner and outer courts was blocked. Government commands consequently issued only from the palace chambers, and the power to command obedience had already been handed to powerful, treacherous men. Han government could therefore no longer be sustained. In its employment of men and administration of government, it did not merely fail to preserve the principles handed down in the Rites of Zhou: even measured against the Western Han, it had fallen very far indeed. From this we know that the greater and lesser…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
相維内外合一其體則公平而博大其業
則光明而俊偉周之所以盛也推而行之
不失其意漢之所以興也更而張之其意
漸失漢之所以亡也夫用人行政之間世
道之盛衰國祚之興亡繫焉則立法誠不
可以不嚴任相誠不可以不重故辨賢者
用人之階也篤敬者行政之本也故用人
非難得一相而百官治矣行政非難運一
敬而萬化理矣傳曰正其本萬事理差之
===
毫氂謬以千里言貴始也然苟非其人道
不虛行道有汙隆政由俗革周禮設官分
職興道致治固非後世所能及矣然嘗伏
讀
皇明祖訓而有以知
太祖之神聖立極高明配天定制設官越虞周
而邁漢唐遠矣夫罷丞相之官重卿佐之
選百僚師師分理于下
一人元良統治于上朝廷無紛更之弊臣宰無
punctuated:
相維，内外合一，其體則公平而博大，其業則光明而俊偉，周之所以盛也。推而行之，不失其意，漢之所以興也；更而張之，其意漸失，漢之所以亡也。夫用人行政之間，世道之盛衰、國祚之興亡繫焉，則立法誠不可以不嚴，任相誠不可以不重。故辨賢者，用人之階也；篤敬者，行政之本也。故用人非難，得一相而百官治矣；行政非難，運一敬而萬化理矣。傳曰：「正其本，萬事理；差之毫氂，謬以千里。」言貴始也。然苟非其人，道不虛行。道有汙隆，政由俗革。《周禮》設官分職，興道致治，固非後世所能及矣。
然嘗伏讀《皇明祖訓》，而有以知太祖之神聖，立極高明配天，定制設官，越虞周而邁漢唐遠矣。夫罷丞相之官，重卿佐之選，百僚師師，分理于下；一人元良，統治于上。朝廷無紛更之弊，臣宰無
translation_en:
…sustain one another, and those within and outside the court form a single whole. In structure, this arrangement is impartial and comprehensive; in its accomplishments, it is brilliant and outstanding. This is why the Zhou flourished. Extending it and putting it into practice without losing its intent was how the Han rose; altering and refashioning it, gradually losing its intent, was how the Han fell. The flourishing or decline of the age, and the rise or fall of the dynasty, depend upon the employment of men and the conduct of government. Thus, establishing institutions must indeed be treated with rigor, and appointing chief councilors must indeed be given great weight. Discerning the worthy is therefore the first step in employing men; earnest reverence is the foundation of governing. Hence employing men is not difficult: obtain a single chief councilor, and the hundred officials will be well ordered. Governing is not difficult: put wholehearted reverence into practice, and the myriad transformations will proceed in due order. A commentary says: “Set the root right, and all affairs will be ordered; a deviation of a hair’s breadth leads to an error of a thousand li.” This means that beginnings must be valued. Yet without the right person, the Way does not put itself into practice. The Way has its declines and ascents, and government changes with prevailing customs. The Rites of Zhou established offices and apportioned duties, promoted the Way and brought about good government: these were achievements that later ages could certainly not match.
Yet I have reverently read the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming (Huang Ming Zuxun), and thereby come to understand Taizu’s sagely wisdom. He established the highest standard, lofty and luminous enough to match Heaven; in determining institutions and establishing offices, he surpassed Yu and Zhou and far outstripped Han and Tang. He abolished the office of chief councilor and placed great weight upon selecting ministers and their assistants. The hundred officials took one another as models, separately administering their responsibilities below; the sovereign, foremost in goodness, exercised unified rule above. The court was free from the ill effects of incessant changes, and its ministers were free from…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
專擅之虞
成祖卽位之初又選文學之臣俾居
內閣專掌
制誥凡中外之幾務
國家之典儀罔不咨議謨謀旣審然後施行
蓋無丞相之名而有弼諧之實
列聖相承鴻業丕茂今
上憲天崇敬開世迪賢
明良際而泰階以平綱紀肅而萬方攸賴愚也
===
何幸躬逢其
盛
第五問
王宗沐
同考試官敎諭鄭批邊防重務方今所急諸
作勦說率無定見晚閱此卷條陳利害纖悉不遺
而區畫有條綽如宿構是留心於當世之務者
同考試官敎諭蔡批備邊一策往往多騁虛
詞此篇成文寸晷發舒良猷兩浙奇才允宜高薦
punctuated:
專擅之虞。成祖卽位之初，又選文學之臣，俾居內閣，專掌制誥。凡中外之幾務、國家之典儀，罔不咨議謨謀，旣審然後施行。蓋無丞相之名，而有弼諧之實。列聖相承，鴻業丕茂。今上憲天崇敬，開世迪賢，明良際而泰階以平，綱紀肅而萬方攸賴。愚也何幸，躬逢其盛！

第五問
王宗沐

同考試官敎諭鄭批：邊防重務，方今所急。諸作勦說，率無定見。晚閱此卷，條陳利害，纖悉不遺，而區畫有條，綽如宿構，是留心於當世之務者。

同考試官敎諭蔡批：備邊一策，往往多騁虛詞。此篇成文寸晷，發舒良猷，兩浙奇才，允宜高薦。
translation_en:
…the danger of ministers arrogating power. At the beginning of his reign, Chengzu further selected ministers of literary learning to serve in the Grand Secretariat, with particular responsibility for drafting imperial decrees and proclamations. All critical affairs within the court and beyond, and all the state's ceremonial institutions, were discussed and deliberated upon; only after careful consideration were they put into effect. Thus, although the title of Grand Councilor had been abolished, the substantive work of assisting the sovereign and harmonizing government remained. Successive sage emperors carried on this inheritance, and the great imperial enterprise flourished abundantly. Our present sovereign models himself on Heaven and esteems reverence, inaugurates a new age and advances the worthy. An enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet, and the Three Steps—the celestial emblem of political harmony—are at peace; order and discipline are upheld, and all regions find their support therein. How fortunate I, in my humble ignorance, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Fifth Policy Question
Wang Zongmu

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Frontier defense is a weighty responsibility and an urgent concern at present. The other essays borrow others' arguments and generally lack firm judgments of their own. Reading this script late in the reviewing process, I found that it sets out advantages and disadvantages point by point, omitting not even the smallest detail. Its proposed measures are orderly, and it proceeds with such ease that it seems to have been composed long beforehand. Here is someone who pays close attention to the affairs of our age.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: Policy essays on frontier defense all too often indulge in empty rhetoric. This piece, composed in a brief span of time, unfolds excellent plans. An exceptional talent from the Two Zhe regions, he truly deserves recommendation at a high rank.

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭陳批經略不凡可以覘先憂
之志矣
考試官學正陳批經濟之猷忠愛之真具
見之
帝王之禦夷狄也承天之道也察地之宜
也盡人之謀也以防患於無事奮武於有
警以為中國久安長治計者也是故四時
異氣五方異俗內陽而外陰者天之道也
河海異界山谷異限內剛而外柔者地之
===
宜也順四時寒暑之令察五方風俗之由
詳山河委絡之源備川谷險阨之實內中
國而外夷狄者聖人所以盡謀也故天之
道以氣運為盛衰也地之宜以主客為難
易也人之謀以得失為勝負也世之論者
謂南北異勢不盡其謀而徒諉之曰邊事
難為則天下之事可任其因循而莫之振
以起乎執事以九邊事宜下詢承學紓猷
攄悃臣子所感激而不容已者也敢不悉
punctuated:
考試官敎諭陳批：經略不凡，可以覘先憂之志矣。

考試官學正陳批：經濟之猷，忠愛之真，具見之。

帝王之禦夷狄也，承天之道也，察地之宜也，盡人之謀也，以防患於無事，奮武於有警，以為中國久安長治計者也。是故四時異氣，五方異俗，內陽而外陰者，天之道也；河海異界，山谷異限，內剛而外柔者，地之宜也。順四時寒暑之令，察五方風俗之由，詳山河委絡之源，備川谷險阨之實，內中國而外夷狄者，聖人所以盡謀也。故天之道，以氣運為盛衰也；地之宜，以主客為難易也；人之謀，以得失為勝負也。世之論者謂南北異勢，不盡其謀，而徒諉之曰邊事難為，則天下之事可任其因循而莫之振以起乎？執事以九邊事宜下詢承學，紓猷攄悃，臣子所感激而不容已者也。敢不悉
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: His strategic planning is exceptional; from it one can discern his resolve to be the first to take thought for troubles.

Comment by Examiner Chen, School Director: Plans for ordering the realm and sincerity of loyal devotion are both fully evident here.

When emperors and kings defend against the barbarians, they follow the Way of Heaven, examine the advantages of the terrain, and exhaust the possibilities of human planning. They guard against trouble in times of peace and deploy military might when alarms arise, thereby planning for China's enduring peace and lasting good order. Thus, the four seasons differ in their vital influences, and the five regions differ in their customs. To place yang within and yin without is the Way of Heaven. Rivers and seas mark different boundaries; mountains and valleys establish different limits. To be firm within and yielding without accords with the advantages of the earth. To follow the seasonal ordinances of cold and heat, investigate the origins of the customs of the five regions, thoroughly examine the sources and ramifications of mountains and rivers, make provision for the actual conditions of perilous terrain and narrow passes among streams and valleys, and keep China within and the barbarians without: these are the means by which the sage exhausts the possibilities of planning. Thus, in the Way of Heaven, flourishing and decline depend on the cycles of vital forces; in the advantages of the earth, difficulty and ease depend on whether one is defending one's own ground or entering another's; in human planning, victory and defeat depend on sound and mistaken decisions. Those who discuss these matters today say that conditions differ between north and south. Rather than exhaust the possibilities of planning, they merely excuse themselves by saying that frontier affairs are difficult to manage. Can the affairs of the realm then be left to drift in habitual inaction, with no one exerting himself to set them right?

You, honored examiners, have condescended to consult us students about the affairs of the Nine Frontier Garrisons. To unfold our plans and express our heartfelt sincerity is something that we, as subjects, are moved to do and cannot refrain from doing. How could I dare not set forth fully…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其愚心夫中國之有夷狄猶君子之有小
人三代以還爲患已乆載諸史冊昭然可
考逮至胡元入主中國天地之變極矣我
太祖高皇帝起淮泗以拯水火提劔而麾之
成祖文皇帝又申北伐之威三犁其庭窮虜餘
魄喙息靡存揆之天道可知也已
國初以遼東大寧宣大寧肅爲六鎭其後更
置薊州榆林固原而九邊聯絡建帥屯兵
城守特重觀之地勢可察也已是故明於
===
天地之故而後防禦之策可得而施也夫
遼陽城衞勢成藩蔽三岔河南北舊城在
焉薊州外邊大寧鎭立而山海關羽翼三
衞在焉自舊城三衞棄去宣薊隔涉從此
多事朶顏部落累肆侵噬漸不可長雖然
舊地之復未易議也若黃花鎭擁護
陵寢潮河川密邇邊關非召兵墾田積石建橋
難以守矣宣府漢之上谷土木之變獨石
不支而此地益重形勢旣殊經畫宜備若
punctuated:
其愚心。夫中國之有夷狄，猶君子之有小人。三代以還，爲患已乆，載諸史冊，昭然可考。逮至胡元入主中國，天地之變極矣。我太祖高皇帝起淮泗以拯水火，提劔而麾之；成祖文皇帝又申北伐之威，三犁其庭，窮虜餘魄，喙息靡存。揆之天道，可知也已。國初以遼東、大寧、宣、大、寧、肅爲六鎭，其後更置薊州、榆林、固原，而九邊聯絡，建帥屯兵，城守特重。觀之地勢，可察也已。是故明於天地之故，而後防禦之策可得而施也。
夫遼陽城衞，勢成藩蔽，三岔河南北舊城在焉。薊州外邊，大寧鎭立，而山海關羽翼三衞在焉。自舊城、三衞棄去，宣薊隔涉，從此多事。朶顏部落累肆侵噬，漸不可長。雖然，舊地之復，未易議也。若黃花鎭擁護陵寢，潮河川密邇邊關，非召兵墾田、積石建橋，難以守矣。宣府，漢之上谷，土木之變，獨石不支，而此地益重。形勢旣殊，經畫宜備。若
translation_en:
…my humble thoughts. The presence of the Yi and Di among the Central Kingdom’s concerns is like that of petty men among a gentleman’s. Since the Three Dynasties, they have long been a source of trouble, clearly documented in the histories for all to examine. When the foreign Yuan entered and ruled the Central Kingdom, the upheaval of Heaven and Earth reached its utmost extreme. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose in the Huai and Si region to rescue the people from fire and flood, raising his sword to drive them out. Emperor Chengzu Wen then displayed anew the might of northern campaigns, thrice laying waste their court and exhausting the routed enemy’s remaining spirit, until not a breath remained. Considered against the Way of Heaven, this is readily understood. At the dynasty’s founding, Liaodong, Daning, Xuanfu, Datong, Ningxia, and Gansu constituted the six frontier commands. Subsequently, Jizhou, Yulin, and Guyuan were also established, linking the Nine Frontiers together. Commanders were appointed and troops stationed, with particular importance attached to defending fortified places. Examined in light of the terrain, this too is readily apparent. Thus, only after understanding the workings of Heaven and Earth can measures for defense be devised and implemented.
The fortified city and guards at Liaoyang form a protective barrier by virtue of their position; the old cities north and south of the Sancha River are situated there. Beyond the frontier at Jizhou stood the Daning command, and there were the Three Guards that served as wings protecting Shanhai Pass. Since the old cities and the Three Guards were abandoned, communications between Xuanfu and Jizhou have been obstructed [?], and troubles have multiplied. The Duoyan tribes have repeatedly indulged in incursions and encroachments; this growing tendency must not be allowed to continue. Nevertheless, recovering the former territory is no easy matter to propose. Huanghua Zhen shields the imperial mausoleums, while the Chao River valley lies very close to the frontier passes. Unless troops are recruited to cultivate fields and stone is gathered to build bridges, these places will be difficult to defend. Xuanfu was Shanggu under the Han. During the Tumu disaster, Dushi could not hold out, and this region consequently became still more important. Since its strategic circumstances are distinctive, planning must be comprehensive. As for…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
補長峪城以鎮邊城之募軍修浮圖峪以
插箭嶺之防守不可已也大同古雲中之
地川原平行大寇屢至今五堡旣經修築
高山聚落亦增戍加舊矣若及其時申久
廢之法補失額之糧革搶兌之馬則偏頭
寧武鴈門三關平定平遠長勝諸堡與東
長峪之修築固可得而議也延綏襟帶千
里當一面之險自徙鎮榆林內地乂安後
虜據河套邊境漸嚴軍用告窘議者謂青
===
山隘口爲虜寇必由之地若屯置軍器修
築邊城而綏德近境沿河郡縣皆徵芻糧
本色水陸竝運輸林可長無事矣寧夏古
之朔方花馬池一帶舊爲虜衝近因前後
大臣建議戶曹設官撫臣駐兵亦旣得地
利矣若賀蘭山諸口盡建墩堡鐵柱泉近
地設兵據守不惟得扼吭先制之策且榆
寧應援相及亦常山蛇勢也甘肅漢之河
西四郡孤懸幾二千里經制長策自古已
punctuated: 補長峪城以鎮邊城之募軍，修浮圖峪以插箭嶺之防守，不可已也。大同，古雲中之地，川原平行，大寇屢至。今五堡旣經修築，高山、聚落亦增戍加舊矣。若及其時申久廢之法，補失額之糧，革搶兌之馬，則偏頭、寧武、鴈門三關，平定、平遠、長勝諸堡，與東長峪之修築，固可得而議也。延綏襟帶千里，當一面之險。自徙鎮榆林，內地乂安。後虜據河套，邊境漸嚴，軍用告窘。議者謂青山隘口爲虜寇必由之地，若屯置軍器，修築邊城，而綏德近境沿河郡縣皆徵芻糧本色，水陸竝運，輸林可長無事矣。寧夏，古之朔方，花馬池一帶舊爲虜衝。近因前後大臣建議，戶曹設官，撫臣駐兵，亦旣得地利矣。若賀蘭山諸口盡建墩堡，鐵柱泉近地設兵據守，不惟得扼吭先制之策，且榆寧應援相及，亦常山蛇勢也。甘肅，漢之河西四郡，孤懸幾二千里，經制長策，自古已
translation_en:
…reinforcing Changyu Fort with troops recruited at Zhenbian Fort, and repairing Futu Valley to support the defense of Chajian Ridge, are measures that cannot be dispensed with. Datong occupies the ancient territory of Yunzhong. Its rivers and plains offer level passage, and major raiding forces have repeatedly arrived there. The five forts have now been repaired and built up, and the garrisons at Gaoshan and Juluo have also been increased beyond their former strength [?]. If timely action is taken to enforce long-neglected regulations, make good the shortfall in grain quotas, and abolish the forcible requisition and exchange of horses [?], then repairs and construction at the three passes of Piantou, Ningwu, and Yanmen, the forts of Pingding, Pingyuan, and Changsheng, and Dongchangyu can certainly be considered.

Yansui commands a thousand li of territory and holds the strategic approaches on one front. After its military headquarters was moved to Yulin, the interior enjoyed peace. Later, the northern foes occupied the Hetao region; conditions on the frontier grew increasingly grave, and military supplies ran short. Those discussing the matter say that the Qingshan defile is a place through which enemy raiders must pass. If military equipment is stockpiled there and the frontier fortifications are repaired, while the prefectures and counties along the river near Suide all collect fodder and grain in kind and transport them by both water and land, Yulin [?] can long remain free of trouble.

Ningxia is the ancient region of Shuofang. The area around Huamachi formerly lay directly in the path of enemy incursions. Recently, following proposals by successive high officials, the Ministry of Revenue has stationed officials there and the Grand Coordinator has stationed troops, thus taking advantage of the terrain. If watchtowers and forts are built at all the openings through the Helan Mountains, and troops are posted near Tie zhu Quan to hold the ground, this will not only provide a means of seizing the enemy by the throat and forestalling him; it will also enable Yulin and Ningxia to come to each other’s aid, forming a disposition like that of the snake of Changshan, whose head and tail support one another when attacked.

Gansu, comprising the four Han commanderies west of the Yellow River, stretches in isolation for nearly two thousand li. As for a lasting plan for its administration and defense, since ancient times this has already…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
難哈密藩籬陷於土魯番久矣恢復之議
自
先朝大臣馬文升許進討平之後又經彭澤經
略王瓊撫綏竟不能復蓋在彼則喪亡殆
盡而在我則勞費無貲此當在所緩也明
矣其議復本色以給邊寨之儲則憲臣之
策是也增修嘉峪關以為內外之防則輔
臣之策是也固原古開城之地一自火篩
入掠遂為要衝隸以三衛而守之重臣屹
===
然為巨鎮矣然山後之虜踏氷馳踐則蘭
靖安會之間便為厲階而西鳳臨鞏之卒
多未經戰說者謂不添沿河之堡不屯常
戍之兵則固原未可息肩也真知言哉夫
天地之形勝略備於此矣然必明於防禦
之策而後天地之勢可得而用也近者胡
虜倡獗屢犯雲中突寇三晉震驚中原軍
書幅至羽檄交馳豈獫狁內侵盛世不能
無警者歟究其防禦之策執事所云者具
punctuated:
難。哈密藩籬陷於土魯番久矣。恢復之議，自先朝大臣馬文升、許進討平之後，又經彭澤經略、王瓊撫綏，竟不能復。蓋在彼則喪亡殆盡，而在我則勞費無貲，此當在所緩也明矣。其議復本色以給邊寨之儲，則憲臣之策是也；增修嘉峪關以為內外之防，則輔臣之策是也。固原，古開城之地，一自火篩入掠，遂為要衝，隸以三衛而守之，重臣屹然為巨鎮矣。然山後之虜踏氷馳踐，則蘭靖安會之間便為厲階，而西鳳臨鞏之卒多未經戰。說者謂不添沿河之堡，不屯常戍之兵，則固原未可息肩也，真知言哉！

夫天地之形勝略備於此矣。然必明於防禦之策，而後天地之勢可得而用也。近者胡虜倡獗，屢犯雲中，突寇三晉，震驚中原，軍書幅至，羽檄交馳，豈獫狁內侵，盛世不能無警者歟？究其防禦之策，執事所云者具
translation_en:
…difficult. Hami, our protective outer barrier, has long been lost to Turfan. As for plans to recover it, after the great ministers Ma Wensheng and Xu Jin campaigned against and pacified it in the preceding reign, Peng Ze undertook strategic operations and Wang Qiong worked to pacify and reassure it; yet in the end it could not be recovered. On their side, losses have brought them close to extinction; on ours, the toil and expense have been beyond measure. Clearly, this undertaking ought to be deferred. As for the proposal to restore payment of taxes in kind to provision the frontier forts, the censorial official’s plan is sound. As for enlarging and repairing Jiayu Pass to provide defenses against threats from within and without, the grand secretary’s plan is sound. Guyuan occupies the site of ancient Kaicheng. Ever since Huoshai raided it, it has become a strategic thoroughfare. Three guards were assigned to defend it, and under a high minister it has become a formidable major garrison. Yet when the barbarians beyond the mountains ride across the ice and trample through the region, the area between Lan, Jing, An, and Hui becomes a source of calamity, while most troops from Xi, Feng, Lin, and Gong have never seen battle. Those who discuss the matter say that unless more forts are built along the river and permanent garrison troops stationed there, Guyuan cannot lay down its burden. These are truly discerning words!

The strategic advantages of the natural terrain have now been outlined here. Yet only after we understand defensive strategy can we make use of that terrain. Recently the northern barbarians have run rampant, repeatedly invading Yunzhong and making sudden incursions into the Three Jin region, shaking the Central Plain with alarm. Military reports arrive in streams [?], and urgent feather-marked dispatches race back and forth. Can it be that, with the Xianyun invading our lands, even a flourishing age cannot be free of alarms? As for examining defensive strategy, what you, sir, have said sets it out fully…

title: 嘉靖二十二年浙江鄉試錄
text:
矣即今兵食告乏當事者已有隱憂其在
當講者愚則以爲選將帥招降順激勇敢
速調發重守令明法制六者其尤也兵志
曰得賢將者兵强國昌故兵者國之大事
命在於將將不賢則雖明主無成功矣乃
者選將求賢廣推薦之條重武舉之選著
爲令甲以先天下宜得有才如李牧之破
東胡充國之平西羌者以應其求而今所
用未必盡如其人也豈推薦者之尚未循
===
其實乎故曰選將帥者此也上無疑令則
衆不二聽動無疑事則衆不二志凡虜於
夷者今既來降而吾殺以邀功非但不祥
而已今之邊將得無有此弊乎故嚴令招
降厚加優恤則人皆懷土而思歸虜必勢
孤而難入矣故曰招降順者此也夫邊患
不時而軍戍有限故古之置邊縣以備敵
也民至有所居作有所用莫若選近邊之
壯者給之以兵甲資之以金帛使之居則
punctuated:
矣。即今兵食告乏，當事者已有隱憂。其在當講者，愚則以爲選將帥、招降順、激勇敢、速調發、重守令、明法制，六者其尤也。
兵志曰：「得賢將者兵强國昌。」故兵者，國之大事，命在於將。將不賢，則雖明主無成功矣。乃者選將求賢，廣推薦之條，重武舉之選，著爲令甲，以先天下。宜得有才如李牧之破東胡、充國之平西羌者，以應其求，而今所用未必盡如其人也。豈推薦者之尚未循其實乎？故曰選將帥者此也。
上無疑令，則衆不二聽；動無疑事，則衆不二志。凡虜於夷者，今既來降，而吾殺以邀功，非但不祥而已。今之邊將得無有此弊乎？故嚴令招降，厚加優恤，則人皆懷土而思歸，虜必勢孤而難入矣。故曰招降順者此也。
夫邊患不時，而軍戍有限，故古之置邊縣以備敵也，民至有所居，作有所用。莫若選近邊之壯者，給之以兵甲，資之以金帛，使之居則
translation_en:
…have already been fully set out. At present, troops and provisions are reported to be insufficient, and those responsible already harbor private anxieties. As for the measures that ought to be considered, in my humble view six are especially important: selecting commanders, welcoming those who surrender and submit, encouraging the brave, expediting mobilization and dispatch, giving due weight to prefects and magistrates, and making laws and regulations clear.
The Military Treatise states: “He who obtains worthy generals has strong troops and a flourishing state.” Thus military affairs are a great concern of the state, and its fate rests with its generals. If the generals are unworthy, even an enlightened ruler cannot achieve success. Recently, in selecting commanders and seeking worthy men, the provisions for recommendations have been broadened and greater weight given to selection through the military examinations. These measures have been promulgated as statutes to guide the realm.
